What's the degree of difficulty in, you know, trying to protect against that? >> When I was at Green Bay helping Halfley, it was more fun to put those guys in there than, you know, have to worry about some of that other stuff. Um the uh it's it's a great scheme. I mean, it's a great scheme because you have so many big guys out there and they all have the ability to rush the passer and drop. Um, so you have to kind of pick and choose your battles. Um, but that's definitely something that that they really executed well uh last week and it's something we got to have a good plan for. >> In training camp, I feel like Carson's inaccuracy or sorry accuracy I should say was kind of a mixed bag. >> Yeah, I thought he did some good stuff. So, so with the accuracy stuff, it actually could be more just like your comfort in the offense rather than something we do with your your actual mechanics or your arm. Oh, >> definitely. It's it's a combination of everything. It's obviously your preparation and understanding of the system, the intention of the play, what you're trying to attack, and then choreographing your feet within that to know if it really is open or isn't open based off the looks that we're looking for. So, it's definitely a combination of everything. Um Reggie obviously he's explosive. Uh he does some great things down the field. He he's got an amazing skill set. I mean, Semi, he's like that that guy, you know, where he's always going to be. He's always doing the right thing. Um, and I mean he made a couple great catch uh made a great catch for Dallas I think it was. It was a critical situation. He caught a caught a out route. Um, so all those guys I mean we've got, you know, all kinds of guys that we're going to be throwing out there and trying to put him in the best position possible. >> With Carson, Trent McBride was in here earlier in the week. He was talking about some of the offplatform creative throws he's been able to make. I I remember the the no look one in training camp. what stood out to you about kind of his ability to make some of those creative plays? >> Oh, he's definitely doing that. I think that's him having fun. You know, when you're prepared um when you know that perfect look that you're trying to attack and then if it's not there, being able to be creative back there to be able to move people to the right spots uh with your eyes and some of those snow lookers. We don't need to do too many of those. Um not yet. Uh but but all those things kind of pair up and and in the end, that's what what you want. You want a prepared quarterback that's out there having fun. Um, and you can see, you know, all these quarterbacks throughout the league, the ones that are are very successful are the ones that are so comfortable that they're playing ball out there. And and that's what we want Carson to do. We want him to be able to go out there and play some ball.

Liam and both Jake Bailey reached out to me as soon as possible and wanted to get you know, his number to reach out to him uh start building a relationship with him, same as me. So, yesterday was a bunch of time at meeting in um you know, my office talking to him about the operation, what we like to do, and then uh today we're going to go back out there. We're also going to kick in the indoor as well. um you know so those things it's it's a lot of work a lot of preparation that these guys are going to have to do in these next couple of days so it should be should be good uh that we get this time together. >> How do you land on Jake? Like is that a thing where the you look around and you look at other teams like you know rosters or whatever you say maybe I want this guy or does Ian and those guys bring you names? How does how does that work? So, as special teams coordinators around the league, you're always going to have a ready list. Like, you're going to always look up there. But I I I give a lot of credit to Ian and his staff. Um, immediately, you know, they were like, "Hey, this is a guy that, uh, we see and he's done a really good job this past year, um, and the year before." So, I thought they did an unbelievable job, um, you know, narrowing it down and picking and saying, "Hey, this is a guy um, do you like him?" And I was like, "Absolutely." you know, went back and watched his film, you know, when he was at Chicago, Washington, at Baltimore, all those different types of even when he was at San Francisco and uh wrote up a quick report again on him and then uh again, credit to Ian to go out and getting this guy. So, u really really happy uh about it. How hard is it to diagnose, you know, when a kicker is having issues? Because I feel like more than any other position could be lights out in practice and then for whatever reason, if it's a mental thing or what have you, things just might, you know, fall apart in the game. >> It it's uh interesting because that that was the talk that I had with Nick um when he came in. Um you know, just trying to diagnose everything from what we did in practice, what we did during pregame. Um, you know, those are the things that you're going to continue to go over and I'm I'm going to continue to go over them even after meeting with Nick. And, you know, that was the biggest thing where a guy who makes all a lot of his kicks during practice and you feel comfortable with him, you feel confident and then he goes out to pregame. Uh, it just comes to a time. It's obviously a performance-based business and it just wasn't happening at the at the time. So, um, that's again I give credit to Kevin and Ian. We all came together, had communication, and just decided it was time to move on. >> Looking at uh at the three wins this year, a common uh theme was kind of like a big play on special teams. Zack Harrison's blocked field goal and Green Bay, some of the big returns against San Francisco. How much of that is as a team do you guys talk about, hey, if we can generate kind of some of these game-winning type of plays on special teams, we've got a good chance of of success. >> Yeah, that's every week. you know, we're talking about building what we call X plays, explosive plays, uh, that we want to have at any point in time. I think our kickoff return team has done a good job these past couple of weeks have really, you know, paying attention to the details, understanding um I would have said, you know, before this last game, we were penalty-free the two games beforehand, but I thought our guys have really locked in just understanding if we do create Xplays and we create field position, whether it's in the return game, whether it's kickoff, punt, uh that's obviously going to help our team out. We talk about winning the field position battle every single week. So, uh we got to continue to harp on it. our players are, you know, locked in. So hopefully we can get that right uh this week as well. >> Helms is your leading tackler, I I believe, right? And then I think he's tied for the most snaps he's played as well. If he ends up playing more on the back end, does that change how much he can play for you? >> Yeah, I mean, it's something that we we've talked about already. Um, you know, we'll continue to look at it throughout the week and see how much he is playing on defense. uh you know, we're not going to ask a guy to play on four core special teams when he's playing a bunch on defense. But I think again that's the communication that Brick, Kevin, myself, and even, you know, Tommy on the offensive side, whatever player there is playing a bunch on offense. Uh I think we do a really good job of communicating with one another and just understanding, hey, the big picture is we'd love to play him on special teams, but we've got to be smart about it. >> What makes him work in that regard? again huge hitter I'm sure which helps a lot too and he can run but what makes him so you know good in that regard >> yeah I think he's really instinctual uh you know he had a great tackle this past game against Cincinnati where uh we were on kickoff and they ran like a middle game on us and he did an unbelievable job of working his way inside and it was a one-on-one tackle with a returner and uh that was just his instincts took over and found that open gap and then made a great play and you know, fundamentally sound. Obviously, making a tackle like that, you just can't dive off the diving board and and try to lunge at someone. And he form tackled them and made a great play. >> What's Khalil Herbert added? >> Uh, a lot. You know, I I think he's done an outstanding job for us. Uh, you know, catching the ball, getting up field, getting vertical. You know, he's a running back, so he's got vision. So, there's certain things that we have on our our return unit where he's going to have to read some blocks and I think he's done an unbelievable job. And to the credit of the other players as well, you know, I think they've done a really good job of blocking for him. But, uh, here's a guy that ends up um, you know, catching the ball with forward momentum, which we ask him to do all the time, and then his vision cutting ability has really helped him out and creating Xplays for us. Sorry, this is a this is kind of a random one because I don't believe y'all have had to do an onside kick or anything yet this year, but just with the new rule change of like having to declare an onside kick late in the gate, like have you seen any changes to that across the league or or anything? >> No, I mean, again, it's uh it's a play that, you know, I always look at it, you know, the league always tries to get a certain percentage and we're we're all trying to make it better and more competitive at the end of the game. you know, that's what fans want to see and everything and it makes it exciting. Uh, you know, my deal is that when we start making more, you know, tweaks to it, uh, you know, you're ahead of the game because you're winning and you don't want to give them so much of like, okay, how are we going to give this the other team a better opportunity to go and try to win this game? So, I haven't really seen a huge uptick on it, but I know last year it ended up going up a little bit more percentage-wise. Uh, which helped out. You know, again, makes it more competitive. But, uh, it's funny you said that because that was one of our major talks with Jake Moody today about onside kicks and, you know, what type of onside kick does he like is he had multiple kicks? Uh, that's one of the things that, uh, you know, he's got to learn our terminology. We've got to find out what he does best. So, uh, that was one of the things that we end up talking about today. >> Cory Lean, what does, what does that change mean for you? >> Um, not a ton. We have a ton of confidence in Cory. Um, you know, really appreciative of news and everything he did for us and did for this organization for a lot of years. And news is a great guy. Really liked in the locker room and um, you know, wish him the best. Um, you know, want to make sure that's stated, but you know, Cory's a guy we have a lot of trust in. and he's done a nice job for us uh since he's gotten here. Has a lot of familiarity with coach Callahan and and you know, the run schemes and some of the communication up front, but you know, we expect Cory to play at a high level for us. We expect him to communicate really well and run the show as as centers do. And Cory's got the right demeanor and personality for that position. And um I know the guys around him feel confident in him and I know Mike feels confident in him. So um [snorts] you know, we expect to move forward. Is it possible that calling this stuff will be a little more natural for him even than it was for news because he spent so much time with Bill come, you know, before? >> Yeah, I just Yeah, I think it was an easy transition for for Cory. He's got a great um wealth of knowledge in the system and the run scheme and the communication scheme uh how to get everybody on the same page. So, um you know, a lot of that was new for that whole group. Cory was the one guy who had a lot of consistency in it. So, um that gives you a lot of confidence in being able to operate. Is it fair to say that Cory might be a a better scheme fit than Nel was? >> I don't want to get into all that. You know, like I think both guys can play at a high enough level for us to win and um just leave it at that. Yeah. >> You brought up he's not as athletic maybe, but he's a little bit heavier than Ryan was. Does that change the complexion of what you guys [clears throat] the run game maybe? >> Yeah, I think um you know certainly it changes some things up front in terms of how combinations work. Um maybe it protects the inside of the pocket, you know, in terms of being a little bit more stout, but didn't feel like there were a ton of limitations with news to begin with. Um you know, obviously we feel like Cory can give us a really good chance to go out there and operate and play to how we want to play. And we're going to have uh you know, they got some good inside players obviously, so we'll have our work cut out for us. But, um, we're fortunate that we have a veteran in the building that's played a lot of football, that's confident, that can communicate and get everybody on the same page. >> Against, uh, or yeah, against Cincinnati, Mike, three, three scrambles, 50 yards. Was [clears throat] that, um, an intentional like conversation that you guys had in the week leading up to that to say, "Hey, you're athletic. You've got athleticism." You know, how did that come about? >> Mike brags a lot about his 40 time, so we kind of, it's unofficial 40 time, but like, "Hey, we're going to see it anytime." No, I mean I think as Mike started playing getting more comfortable um you know it's something we've talked about for a while now and like you don't design scrambles obviously but um you know it can be a critical part you you study the top third down teams across the league every year there's usually a consistent theme if quarterbacks can pick up a couple first downs a game with their legs usually those teams ranked at the highest part of the league. Um, and so there's always examples on film. There's always examples of how it can um, really impact the defense and teams have to to focus on that. So thought Mike did a great job being vertical in the pocket, stepping up and being decisive when it was time to go. >> What's he claim it's 40 times? >> He claims like high 44s. I think unofficially it's 451 or something. So we remind him it's not quite in the 44s. Um, but there's been a lot of chatter about that for a while. He brought up yesterday and we're talking to Jake M about this as [clears throat] well that he thinks you guys are close. >> Yeah. >> How what do you need to do to bridge the gap from where you are to what you can be offensively? >> Yeah, I think we all just got to do a better job. You know, I'll put a lot of the the onus on myself. Um we are close, but you know, close in this league doesn't quite get it uh to where you want to be. And um you know, we've shown flashes of being a a very top level offense in the NFL and being able to score a lot of points and move the ball and be versatile in our attack. And um we just got to find the consistency. You know, we had, you know, critical penalties, we had, you know, some mental errors. We had some calls that you want back in moments like it's all of us together to make sure that um you don't waste any bullets. So, um, the consistency part of it so important because you get in these high leverage games, you get in these games where the margins are so are so thin that all those plays add up. And you might say, "Hey, there's six or seven of these you want back." Well, that's the difference between scoring 17 and scoring 35. And, uh, certainly I felt like we were capable of doing more last week and we left some out there. and um challenge the staff, challenge myself, challenge the players to to fix those things and continue to move forward [clears throat] to playing to the to the level that we're capable of. >> I I know better than to ask you about any specific play call or whatever, but I think I've seen Bjon kind of take a handoff at the goal line five or six times and just immediately turn towards the sideline and outrun guys. >> Y >> to that pylon. Like is that a unique skill that he possesses? that ability to just say I'm just going to >> Yeah, he's fast. Yeah, he is fast. Um I think you see that across the league. There's some there's some schemes that based on how they defend it becomes a pylon pylon run. Um and if you watch, not to get too far in the weeds, like if you watch like the 11 personnel run game inside the five, you're going to see a lot of that. Um so certainly when guys are packed in, if you have a guy that can get to an edge, it's it's an advantage. And they ran a nasty pick stunt down there on the one where they picked for the nose who looped and is in the A gap. And so be made the right cut and right decision and obviously he has the speed to capture the edge and I thought, you know, our receivers did a nice job of collapsing that edge for him and uh providing that cut. >> We talked the last few weeks about trying to start faster and then you had that opening time drive. What do you think was working there and um is it replicable? >> Say that one more time. >> Is it replicable to >> Yeah, I think yeah, we want to build off it. I thought, you know, our first two drives, shoot, we went right down the field. First drive coming out of the half, went right down the field. Felt like we had a nice blend. You know, you get the drive started with an easy completion that leads to a first down and then you c you catch a couple explosives in the run game. You know, we uh had a short yardage play we felt really good about that was able to hit and then, you know, Mike obviously stepping up and scrambling. Um, look, we uh we want to be able to create more explosives. You know, I think that's something that we're after and that will lead, you know, when we were really rolling, we were creating explosives in both the run and the pass. So, you look at those drives, you know, we had Bejan on the rail route there to start the second half. That's an explosive that jump starts a scoring drive. You have the scramble and the long run on third and one that uh ignite the first touchdown drive. So, you know, I think when you're able to find explosives, find the ability to create those, um, that can be great. But we've also shown to be methodical and we've had a I think the first drive of the second half was like seven and a half minutes long and we were able to kind of pick up some critical third downs and you know we had another 11play drive where we come away empty-handed and um we just got to continue to focus on the details, focus on the things that allow us to stay on the field and be efficient. >> You talked about explosives. Kevin earlier this week kind of mentioned when a team is sending pressure that a counter is is kind of looking for those explosives. Has the thinking changed on that over the years? because I feel like it used to be all right, what's a hot route? How do we kind of get a quick beater here to just be like is how do you balance those two things? >> Yeah, I think explosives come in a lot of forms, you know, like we're fortunate that we have players that if we throw a quick route, it can turn into explosive. you know, nobody enjoyed how the Chicago game went, but in the second half when they were pressuring and we were able to kind of move the ball in a two-minute operation, like we were able to have some explosives in in throws that weren't 20 yards down the field, but with some of our guys ability with the ball in their hands, those those opportunities become explosive because they're pressuring you, they don't have as many eyes and they don't have as many um bodies able to bring it down. And um we got to we got to pick and choose those spots in terms of there's times where, hey, you want to protect it up, take a shot. There's times where the right answer is getting the ball out and they better be really good in open field tackle because if they're not then we have a chance those those plays become become more than what what they're caught at. Um you know the other part of it too is if you can catch some run game into pressures like there's usually not a second or third level to the defense uh when they're pressure and everybody's on on a similar plane. So get one you know it can go for a while. So um to to attack pressure you got to all be on the same page. you know, one guy doesn't do his job, usually doesn't result in a positive play. So, everybody's got to be on the same page, understand why we're getting to certain things against pressure to make sure we can execute. >> We talked uh with you several weeks ago at length about Drake as a as a blocker. >> And I'm just curious, uh, when did you when did you first know that this is this is a weapon that that you guys can >> I think when you just watching the film when we first got here. I mean, look, I don't I don't know the answer to this, but I would be hardressed to find a better blocking receiver in the NFL, period. And for him to be a number one receiver and do that is pretty impressive. I mean, you watch those first couple runs on the first drive. He has a couple knockdowns. I mean, their linebacker bodies. Um, I think the willingness is unique, you know, like to be a player at his caliber, to be a player getting paid at his level, to be a player that has a production at his level, for him to be to have the willingness to do all those things to help the team, that's a little bit unique at his position. And we're really fortunate for that because it sets a tone with everybody else in the room. >> Was there was there one one block or one play that maybe stands out to you as >> wow this guy is you know another level as far as blocking. I >> mean he knocked two guys down in the same play last game which was pretty cool. One of them was a linebacker. So um I mean he's done it all year though and he's done it his whole career. So I think you don't have to search far to be like all right he's this is something that's a really a strong suit for him. Coach, where does the um uh catalog for your draw and screen game fit in the blitz beater uh attack? >> Yeah, I think when you're talking screen game specifically, um you know, it's things usually outside of the u the per more on the perimeter part of things. You know, we had um you know, we had one to Drake a few weeks ago outside of number one that that hit for a positive play out there versus a zero look. you know, draws can be a little bit more tough, but you know, the screen game when you can spread them out and find space on the perimeter, I think those are good ways to attack pressure. You see that across the league often. Um, and look, these guys do a great job on defense. Spags has a very multiple attack, you know, in terms of what he's going to present you. So, you got to have a lot of different answers to to be able to counter those things. >> You got Charlie Warner a touchdown last week. >> Yeah, that's a Chuck said it last week or a couple days ago. He goes, "I might be the He I don't know, maybe somebody can find this out, but like who has played the most snaps at tight end without a touchdown?" He's like, "I have to be in the top five." And I was like, "Well, not anymore." And now he's like, "Well, I got to get one on US soil." So that was me go. >> Never enough for that guy. >> Never, Chuck. Yeah. Talk about a diva. [laughter] >> Kyle's role. >> Has Kyle's role matched what you hoped it would be this year? >> Yeah. I try not to put, you know, like expectations on things. I think Kyle's done a lot of the things we've asked him to do. You know, we've we had two explosives to him that got called back due to penalty last week. So, certainly that stat line looks different. >> Um Kyle's focus and intent's been great. Um you know, he scored some big touchdowns for us. Certainly, do we want his volume to be up? Yeah. But, um you know, that there's a lot that goes into that. So, in terms of how he's approached, you know, being a teammate, attacking the the prep, being um someone that we can rely on, that that's all added up. you know, we got to do a better job like we early in the year we talked about of finding ways to have them impact the game. And it was unfortunate last week. We felt like we had, you know, probably about 40 yards that were left left out of there. Um, just with some calls being coming back. >> Just to ask you one question about the the Chiefs, Steve Spanolo, the defense. What do you see from them? >> They do a great job. I think they're third in in the league uh in total defense. Obviously, Spags has been doing it a lot longer than I have and done a great job for for a really long time. and um they present a great challenge. They're so versatile in their scheme. Um they challenge the offense. They very they take a very aggressive approach. They have a kind of a core group of guys that have been there for a long time together. So when you look at how they operate and look at how they play defense, you can tell they're confident in what they're doing and know the answers, know what they're trying to get done, and um you know, they got really good personnel and a really good scheme. So it's it's a great challenge. Um, you know, everybody thinks about the Chiefs, think about the offense in Mahomes, and quietly for the last decade or however long it's been, Spags has had one of the best defenses, you know, every year. So, um, it's a great challenge for us. It's a great matchup. I know our guys are excited about it. You know, our guys seem to like to play in these games and against these types of opponents. So, u, I'm excited about the challenge, excited about our opportunity.

title: Atlanta Falcons players speak to the media on roster moves ahead of Kansas City | Press Conference
text: just can you give us your your state of the team after a couple moves and some leaders uh uh [clears throat] gone and changed and and how you guys plan to move forward? >> Yeah, I mean you know in this league like we understand that the business of the NFL this is what happens. Um but for us like you know Jesse uh news Nick like those those are just great human beings um just in general and you know those are those are great leaders for this team that's been on this team for for a long time. I know Nick just got here but [clears throat] um you know it definitely sucks to to lose guys like that but we understand like we have to you know move forward fast um and just get ready for this week and you know those guys are going to you know play well for their teams. Um, but we got to continue to, you know, try to play out our best here, uh, the best way that we can. >> There's not many guys who were here when you got here in 2023, but the guys who got traded were among that small group of guys. So, I'm curious, is it kind of hard for you as a competitor to [snorts] understand the process of trading away guys who played a lot of quality ball here, played a lot of snaps here with also the staff saying, "Hey, we're still trying to win this year." >> Yeah. I mean, as a competitor, like, you know, we're we're trying to win regardless, man. like we understand that, you know, we got to make some moves, but it doesn't uh tear the fact that we're still trying to get to where we want to get to in the season. Um, and I know like the external out or people outside of here think that we're just plummeting the season. Like, no, man. Like, we're we're focused on this week and we're going to take it one game at a time and go from there. But, you know, we're all confident in ourselves and what we got to do for the rest of these weeks, for the season, and try to make a push, man. So, that's that's where we're at right now. What coach brought up earlier is that you talked to, you know, a lot of good leaders around you guys, just the whole organization. Were you among those? Were How much has he talked to you throughout the week of just trying to understand kind of how you guys are, you know, handling all this stuff? >> Yeah, I mean, he talked to the leadership committee. Um, and just to make sure that we, you know, put the message around the whole team like, you know, we gota we got to come out to practice, come out this week, you know, ready to go. uh make sure everybody's on board, make sure nobody comes in the building, moving around, nothing like that. So, you know, we we took that message to heart and you know, everybody everybody in the locker room is, you know, positive right now and, you know, all ready to practice, all ready to go and, you know, that's that's the message that we that we put out earlier this week so we can be ready to go for today. >> Who's on that leadership committee? Uh me, Drake, uh Chris, uh Jake Matthews, um Divine, and there's other there's other guys, too. I that's those like the guys right there. Um and then AJ, uh and then Z. So, yeah, those guys. Zaris, >> what do you feel like has been missing in these past couple of losses that has really prevented you guys from getting a win? >> Yeah, we just got to we just got to execute um at high levels like we can't we can't beat ourselves, you know. I think you know like we have a saying like if the Falcons beat the Falcons like then we're not good and so we got to stay away from that because when we don't beat ourselves we play at a very high level uh and it shows. So, you know, that's that's really the biggest message. Um, so going forward because that's how we that's how we've been losing games uh these past weeks. >> How did you find out about the two different dreams? >> Same way you did, man. Social media. Social media. >> What was your reaction to those? >> Yeah, I mean, it sucks. Like, those are those are, you know, two two guys that I respect a lot. Um, that that are that I've been playing with my my whole time being here. Uh, so you know, it definitely does suck, but I understand too. Like that's that's what this business sometimes, you know, that's what happens sometimes. So, you know, I I text those guys. Um, I just had to move on from it. >> What can you tell us about Cory Leven who's going to be talking up for for news? What's he like? >> Oh, yeah. He he's high energy. Um, he he brings great energy into the locker room, on the field. And, you know, thing about him is he it's like he doesn't have an off switch. you know, he always goes, always, um, is ready to play no matter what the situation is. So, and and he just gives, you know, extreme effort. Um, so that's who he is as a as a player and, you know, I know the guys are going to love to have that and, you know, all of us on the offense, we we enjoy Cory, so I know he's going to go out there and give his all. Um, and and then we'll just, you know, I'm I'm going to try to make him right on all situations, running past. So, and he knows that. So, it's going to be, you know, be it'll be fun playing with them. >> You guys are in a really unique situation because, you know, the record is three and six, but the reality is is that you are a half game out of the first place. >> Yeah. >> So, uh you know, losing some of some of these these guys this week, um how do you as a leader kind of keep everyone focused on the task at hand because division title is still within reach? >> Yeah. Um, like like I've been saying, like we focus on today, focus on tomorrow, focus on Friday. Um, and and get to get to Sunday and and make sure that we're, you know, at our at our tiptop shape for the Chiefs because, you know, we start looking ahead, then that's how we that's how we lose. So, for us, like staying staying focused on this game right here, um, and worried about this game because this game is very important and every game that we play from here on out is going to be very important. Uh that's the mindset that we have to go into in order for us to win in or in in order for us to get to where we want to get to. >> You're on pace right now for a new career high in carries this year. Does it feel that way to you? >> No, I feel I feel good, man. I feel great. Um yeah, that's that's what I'm here to do. I feel good. >> What made Jesse unique as a leader? >> Uh just his attention to detail and everything in his life. um just when he even walked in the building like he was, you know, very intentional of what he was trying to do, who he was trying to lead and what he was trying to get done. And I think that I saw that and even just the conversations that we had um trying to make this team into into who we wanted to become. Um he just had a clear vision on it and in practice like he would never take a play off. He was always uh ready to go no matter what the day is even if he felt sick or anything. So that's what that's what you know made him special as a player. >> Obviously hard to replace somebody with a C on their chest, but who are some of those voices that you think could step up now and >> it has it has to be everybody you know even coach uh mentioned in the in the team meeting like because we lost guys like that. Uh everybody has to step up like can't just be a one guy thing like it has to be the whole team and we have to see it and you know we could talk about all we want but the actions have to be a lot louder than the words. >> Couple more. What are the most important things to get right when you're integrating a new guy like Cory onto the O line especially during a game week and especially you know at the start position? >> Yeah, I mean with him like he he's you know obviously been around the whole season. So he he knows he knows the offense, he knows the whole offense. Um but I I I love to see you know guy come in and next man up and and want to embrace the opportunity. And I know that he's you know he's a vet in this league, man. So like this isn't nothing new for him. Uh, so, you know, I know he's going to come in here and and, you know, like I said earlier, bring bring that energy and, you know, I'm excited to see what he can do uh, this week. >> Sean, I have I have one that's completely separate from what everyone else was asking. Uh, what is uh, what has been your favorite uh, block from from Drake London on a maybe downfield or or even line of scrimmage? >> Favorite block? Shoot, there's been so many blocks. Um, I mean, this week just on the crack block, he destroyed the linebacker uh on a toss like and I saw it with my own eyes. Like I I typically see Drake's blocks because I get to get to his box really quick. Um, but I think my favorite block with him, it was probably a couple years ago when we played the Giants and I had like this uh goal line run and he just took the corner and the corner just couldn't go nowhere. Like he was just stuck and I just ran right outside of him um and or cut it right up inside of him, sorry. Uh, but that's probably my favorite. >> So, he blocking like key line guys, too. Like >> Yeah. Yeah. He blocks everybody. He blocks at a high level, too. And that's why I respect respect Drake um so much even more than just him catching the football and running routes. title: Byron Storer Press Conference | November 12th, 2026
text: All right, before I start, uh Tony, I got to tell you, man, we talked about uh the UFFL and the trick plays. Did you see the Raiders reverse they ran on kick return? >> I did not. >> Uh so you manifested it. [laughter] Uh it worked. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> For touchdown? >> No, not for a touchdown. I think it got past the 40 yard line, but uh I was thinking about you when I saw that play. [laughter] >> All right. Go ahead. >> What do you got up your sleeve this week? >> I know. I trying to keep it simple, trying to get past the 30 yard, 35 yard line. >> Yeah. I just wanted to ask in the first half to have those two illegal formation penalties on kickoff and kick return, what what happened there and then how disappointing is it to get the second one after you just got the first one in the first quarter? >> Yeah. So, those are um the little small details, alignment details, you know, you you think back to those are install one we go over. Okay, here are the quadrants, guys. These are the rules. You have to stay still from the time the blow the the whistle's blown to the time the ball is caught or hits in the landing zone. these very little details now that you cover early on and and it's a good reminder for me that I have to recover these rules over and over and over again because in my mind you get what you emphasize and I have to emphasize the rules more frequently throughout the week because I think what happens is you get so caught up in the personnel, you get so caught up in the scheme. you get so caught up in what you're gonna do, how you're going to attack their opponent, that some of those small fine details get lost in the shuffle. And so, it's just a great reminder for me that I have to remind these guys every week about the the rules because they are unique and we have a lot of young guys on our team and it and it's their first time through with this new kickoff, kickoff, return. Um, so that's that's it. Have you seen what the Jets are doing on their kickoffs? I have >> thought about that or or what are your thoughts on that? >> I I think you know if you have a guy that can kick off I know I think Eric Reid can kick off too. He was at the Kansas City Chiefs for a while. Um you're talking about Andrew Beck kicking off, right? Um I think if you have a guy that can do it at a high level and be able to cover down, um I think it's worth exploring. Um, I'm not sure we have that guy on our team yet, but uh, you know, if you had that guy, it's always a, you know, a possibility of adding another coverage player to the play. >> Andre with the 51 yard there at the end and the ice in his veins and just how well he's done on the 50 plus. >> Yeah, I I think I was really happy to see uh Andre go out there and hit that game uh that the tying field goal to keep us in the game, send us to overtime. Um, yeah, I think he's just, you know, he's gone through some adversity this year and I think he's on his way back up. Um, so I'm really excited for him. >> Obviously, the weather feels like it's turning here. What does that change for you when you're coaching up these guys or even Andre and Cory, just how special teams feels like it changes when the weather becomes an issue? We went out there today and uh we got some wet ball drill, you know, and I think the guys after the Jets game, we understand how important it is to be prepared for the elements. And so we've really um took it on that challenge every week, you know, getting wet ball drill and then going out there. We have days like this where we can go out there in the rain and the wind and get some work done. So it's really just u taking advantage of the opportunities like today where you can go out there and get some work in some inclement weather. What did you like most about the the forced fumble with Aiden and Donovan? What like what can you what did you what stood out and then what do you take away from that as you try to maybe get more of those kind of big plays on on your side of things? >> Well, I think you know it's it's um a testament to the guys that we have on the punt team and that I I get to work with every single day is you know they're covering down there. You know they're giving everything they got. You know, Aiden's a 280lb man, defensive tackle, running down there and um straining great effort and then going to make a t not only going to make a tackle, but getting the ball out at the same time. And then the strain of Donovan McMillan to try to go make the tackle, not quite get the tackle, and now he's straining to go get the ball. And just those plays for me are the most exciting just for the guys. You know what I'm saying? They work so hard. They practice. We cover kicks. uh you know couple time a few times a week throughout uh throughout the week and then to have them have success to put our uh offense in a position to score some points on the plus 19 yard line. Uh that's that's big for us. That that's exciting. That's what that's what we're trying to do, you know, that's that's what we're about. >> Do you think it's important to go down to the stadium when the weather turns bad and practice there? >> Uh you know, it's something to think about. We haven't done it. Um, but I think we get enough wind out here to kind of I know it's different and um we've been blessed with some really nice days in at home games. Um, so things are changing and uh but I I'm I'm lucky to have Andre and Corey and Rex who've kind of been through it. Now, if I had a uh all rookie group, I I definitely think that it's a we we'd have to make a trip to the stadium for sure. >> Gunners um end up out of bounds as much as they do. Um, I mean, you guys got flagged for for, you know, being first to touch the ball on that, but it, you know, seems like having them maybe run inside of outside seems a little bit, but just why do they take that outside route the way they do? >> All right. So, when you when you're putting the ball, you're punting it toward usually you're trying to punt it toward the boundary to shorten the field. And so you have releases by the gunners toward the punt direction. So you'd like for both your gunners to release the same direction. So if you're punting left, both guys release left and one guy ends up into the boundary. Now you can't run out of bounce on your own. A lot of times those corners will force you into the white. And so now uh you have to, you know, take a line to reenter. You know what happened on that play was, you know, DT um didn't realize he had gotten in the white, you know, and so we just had a discussion on the sideline and just said, "Hey, if there's any possibility that you could have gone out of bounds, all you got to do is just point to the ball, tell your teammates, you you you and and they touch it." So, it's a it's a big learning experience for us, and unfortunately, it cost us 30 yards of field position, so we had to learn the hard way. Um, but I just don't think that's it's not possible to change what we do in terms of staying out of bounds. That that's just part of the deal. >> People, I guess like outside fans, whatever, think about what like successful special teams look like. I think a lot of times they just envision punt returns all the time that are breaking big or kickoffs that are breaking big and like hitting every single kick all the time. But as a as a as the person who's working with those units every single week, every single day, what in your mind makes like a successful special teams team, special teams units that you work with? >> I think it comes down to, you know, dominating field position in any way, shape, or form. you know, you could go out there and dominate field position with just the punter and he's, you know, kicking it 50 yards out of bounds, you know, and not giving the returner any opportunities or you're, you know, you know, covering uh kickoffs and you're you're getting drive starts on the 25 yardd line inside the 30 uh in coverage and then when you get your opportunities to return the ball, you're getting 10 plus yards of return. you know, you're you're constantly creating favorable field position for your offense and you're setting your defense with a long field. And then when you have opportunities to score and make big plays, you take advantage of those opportunities. So, a good special teams unit dominates field position and also takes advantage of opportunities to score points. >> With KC having a little bit of a an ankle from from last week, can you 100% count on him to return punts for you this week? I was impressed with Casey like in the game, you know, we were making contingency plans and, you know, he wanted to go out there. So, um, as far as I'm concerned, uh, you know, he's available for us this week and and we'll make adjustments as they come. >> It looked like Isaiah was the guy on Sunday for for kickoff returns. Is that something that's going to last? Are you going to keep trying more guys there? >> We're always going to rotate guys. That's how we do things. We're always u making sure guys get multiple reps because you never know what's going to happen in the game. But we're I'm really encouraged by what IB is doing and so um I I'd love to see more of him. I think he's just going to get better and better at that role and I think he's excited about having that role. >> Is Dylan is Dylan Samson just not available for that at this point? >> No, he's available. He's available and uh so I just want to make sure we're smart with him depending on what his role how much his workload is on offense. um just to make sure I'm keeping in mind what's best for the team, not only for the special teams unit, he didn't need to touch that ball, right? Like it wasn't in danger of going in the end zone or anything. Um but I feel like I see that a lot across the league where the [snorts] ball's bouncing back and guys carried in the end zone like do you have those conversations guys like you know I know you're running down at full speed but like take a breath because sometimes you only have to touch the ball. >> Absolutely. Yeah, and we have meetings uh every single day and we go through, you know, we always keep an eye on what goes on throughout the league. So, we're always looking at penalties throughout the league. And um Coach Tandy, Keith Tandy, he's my assistant. He he works with the gunners and, you know, each week we go over those specific situations to just try to keep it front of mind for the guys to make sure that they know, hey, you go out of bounds, you can't be the first one to touch it. And there's a variety of different situations that come up time and time again that you just got to be aware of at the gunner position. And so that that's one of them. And uh you know we I think we'll as a unit now we'll all understand the importance of that rule. >> You study which officiating group you have to know whether they're more strict on holding or lenient. >> I do not. No I do not. No. I think that's a uh that's something I've done in the past, but we have not done that this year. >> All right. Thank you.

title: Mike Rutenberg Press Conference | November 12th, 2026
text: what what do you uh think you guys can do better this week to get that short up? >> You know, um every week, whatever it is, we address it like I always say, because that's just what football is. And in terms of the run defense, you know, great run games are are based on violence, which is what we're built off of, discipline, fits, and straining of the ball. And we'll continue to preach our style of strain and violence and our style of the mind to do our best in the fits. practice it like we've been doing it and continue to whatever it is take that approach in everything we're trying to fix. >> I I don't know what percentage of plays you've used a third linebacker but it's a very small percentage and yet teams are adding an extra offensive line then against you. So, it's more just about repetitions more than anything from that perspective. >> So, a case of you think your third safety is a better player than your third linebacker? >> No, it has nothing to do with this person's better, this person's better. The whole key to playing great defense is to play as fast as humanly possible. So during a week to get as many reps for as many people as we can between walkthroughs, pre-practice walkthroughs, practice, that's just the approach we've taken. >> We talked to Jared Bur earlier today and he said that he visited with a a team psychiatrist to help him be a better pass rusher. I know he is that player and he'll continue to work. He's working on it in practice. He's constantly working and studying film. It's not how close he is. It's just him continuing to do what's best for him to get himself to where he wants to play and us helping him as much as humanly possible. >> I know you guys always call that beline the engine, but I think only three sacks from the unit as a whole over the last three games. So, just how do you look at that production? I mean, I know last game you got sacks from other positions, but struggled with it obviously these last three weeks. >> Yeah, again, you guys have been around me long enough that I I never look at it from one position. It's it's all 11. And and sacks don't just come from the engine across the league. Sacks come from sometimes great coverage. Sacks come from sometimes a good pressure. Sacks sometimes come from the engine. And we will go as our engine goes. And as we continue to go and uh you you continue to see those guys revving that engine up, but it's not actually anything about like Dline has to have sacks. It's just us trying to make the offense as as uncomfortable as possible. It looks like the Texans are incorporating Tank Dell into their offense more slot receiver. So, how does that affect you? I just talk about how his emergence after that severe injury. >> Unbelievable player, right? Unbel I mean he was unbelievable coming out obviously unfortunate with with his injury. Always happy to see a player come back from any type of injury and it's not just Tank. I mean, they're extremely skilled offense. um you could rattle off their whole receiving core and put the tight end in there as well in terms of the pass game, which I know you were referencing. And then kudos to CJ Strad and what they're doing. So, I'm excited for our battle. I I I love our DBs. I love our back seven. And I'm excited for the battle. >> What is it about? >> What What is it about Miles Harden makes him such an effective blitzer? >> Man, you know, I could go on for a while. It's kind of like how you asked me about Carson last week and I was like, well, he'll just, you know, fix himself. Um, you know, Miles is one of those guys who's self-made, right? And, um, I obviously wasn't here with him previous to this year, but you can see his preparation. You can see his attention to detail, his diligence, his desire to play for his teammates. So, not only is he an effective blitzer, he's an effective cover guy, but he's constantly working on his craft, constantly working on the diff different schemes of the week, and he's asking questions. Hey, Rudy, if we they do this, what about this? He works with Jeff Anderson, our Nicholls coach, and it's really cool to see all that come together and see have success. It's a credit to him. >> Go back to Jared. Is there anything I'm sure you're trying to figure it out, but anything schematically you can do to free him up or give him better opportunities um than he's had at his home? >> You know, as a coaching staff and from Monk down to the defensive staff, we're always trying to get all of our players in the best positions and we're always looking schematically um technically to see where we can get all of our players, whether it's Jared or Miles or Carson. Um, so that's just a constant day-to-day process. Obviously, it has to do with the opponent and what we think they're doing or what we think they're going to do to us. And then how can we get our players uh in that best position to be successful by situation as well? >> At this point, no one's really 100%, but you've got a number of guys on on your side of the ball dealing either coming back from or dealing with injury. Mason, Malik, Denzel, Carson. How much maybe as the weeks go on, do you see the health maybe improving on some of the things you're working on, stopping the run game, the tackling, uh, and even going into the by-week and just trying to give them more time to come back from what they're going through. >> You know, um, it's probably cliche, but it's week 10 of the NFL season and everyone's beat up across the league. Um, I don't think, what's the best way for me to say this? Circumstances aren't going to get in the way of us trying to be successful. And whether we're beat up or not, I know those men that you're talking to, they went out and just had an awesome practice, no matter beat up or not, and they do it every day. And they give everything for each other, and it's cool to see. But yes, I'm sure they're excited to to get healthy when the by-week comes. But that doesn't mean that they're their mentality is heart, mind, fist, and they're doing it every day. Those guys are in that training room. Those guys are working and they practice their butts off. >> I don't know if you answer this, but I'm going to ask. >> Probably not. >> If a team like puts four wide outs on the field, which they do. Would you cover that fourth with Iman or a quarterback? >> I mean, you don't really think I'm going to answer that question, do you? I I appreciate WHAT YOU SAID. YOU'RE PROBABLY NOT going to answer this. So, I'll keep what we're doing internally, you know, but I appreciate you asking. >> Yeah. >> Coach Bunkin talked yesterday about mental stamina in these games um in in all phases. >> Sure. any particular area, but I just want to ask you about your unit because some of the, you know, fourth quarter drives you guys have allowed. What do you do to kind of help when it's the late in the game and guys are tired and worn down? What can you do to help them be in a better position to get that crucial stop to, you know, to get off the field and, you know, give the offense the ball back with a lead rather than needing the offense to go back down and and and get those points back. [snorts] >> You know, we absolutely in those situations want to get off the field. And when we don't, it kills us. It kills us football-wise, not in life. It does. Um, but no, no one drive defines a game. And I think that's important for the whole team to know and that's what Monk always talks about whether it's starting fast, finishing faster, making the play at the end of the half going in, knocking getting a three and out after the halftime. Each little six-second play defines the game. And then of course at the end of the game, great defenses try their butts off to finish. And during the week, I'm not going to get into what we do, but what I can promise you is we are always addressing whatever came up headon honestly together and figuring out the best ways. Whether it's in a meeting, whether it's out at practice, whether it's a drill, we do all that and our guys are bought into that and it's really cool to see. >> With Ronnie not being able to practice the last couple days, um, how comfortable are you with Emanuel if he's got to take on that full time? I know he had to fill in early in the season and how have you seen him kind of grow into that from week one? >> Yeah, I think we've all seen him together, you know, grow into it starting with all the great plays he was making on special teams into his role on defense. Um, not only has made a lot of plays for us defensively and helped us, but he's communicating at a high level, he's helping us through all the different adjustments that we make. And, uh, if that is the case, everybody counts on Eman because he's done it already. When called upon on special teams, he did it. when called upon to come in a game, he does it. When called upon in crucial third down, he does it. Again, the attack style defense, while we always reference it starting with the engine, which it always will be, that is the core of what we do, but our tact style defense is all 11. It's starts with the engine and it goes to the second level of getting downhill. It gets to the third level of protecting us uh on deep balls and explosive plays. And then when a third level player has to come down to the second level, the attack style defense has to do with pressure, bringing different people. So, we are an attack style defense and I'm proud of the way those guys are doing it. Thank you. >> Awesome. All right. For sure. Yeah, you got it.
