Those are the five best guys and he's sticking with them. Um so outside of making a lineup change, you know, how how do you course correct on those penalties so that, you know, you know, there's just been so many of those those drive killers that you've had this year. So, outside of making a lineup change, what do you do to to get those penalties to come down? >> Yeah, I think and and this this is what he did yesterday. I think you you got to just be honest. Hey, this is where we are. Like we're not good in this area, you know? And and you put up the stats and you show the guys. And um so that draws attention to it. And that's part of it. The other the other thing is looking at what type of penalties you have, right? Like the ones that you that you have no uh tolerance for are the ones that take no talent that in that's pre-snap penalties, right? It's it's snap count things. It's things that are just focus and diligence from the group, right? Um so those are the ones that you really try to attack. Uh as far as holding and things like that, do you coach guys to keep hands inside? Of course. You know what I mean? But some of those are did they see it? And a lot of those can be 50/50. So all you can do is coach the technique, right? So that you try to lower the likelihood as as much as possible uh of all those. But yeah, you just you emphasize it, um look at which ones they are, right? And and then just try to attack it. >> [clears throat] >> Knowing that Houston pass rush like it is, how does that affect uh the game plan? >> Uh yeah, I mean it it affects everything that you do in the pass game. You know, that's what you have to think about first. Uh and there's there's everybody's got a piece of that, right? The the chip plan that like I said, we have every week and most teams have every week. Um and then how you're going to distribute routes and all that, getting the ball out on time, um handling the different protection looks that they give you because that can hinder your ability to chip at times. Um yeah, so it's really all inclusive. But to to answer your question, I mean anytime you play premier pass rushers, that's got to be at the front of your mind um when it comes to any pass play, really. >> When Sean Jenkins been running the ball for you just, you know, individually looking at his >> Yeah, I think he's a a very physical um downhill runner and he's tough to tackle, you know? And he also he's been doing a great job of maximizing downhill, you know, runs for us even when it might not look like there's not a whole lot there. Um and I think it's just continuing to try to dip into that as much as we can. Um and then to work with him on on the other things that maybe are things he hasn't done a ton of, right, in his career. Um uh different different run schemes, I mean, you know, and you just keep attacking it that way. >> Red zone numbers haven't been great in recent weeks and really like as a season-long trend. What what does it take not just for you guys specifically, not like fans to diagnose your issues, but like what do good red zone offenses do? >> Well, I mean, it starts with in my opinion your ability to run the football in. I mean, the the lower that you get down there the less room there is to throw, okay? And if you're able to run it in now you're going to force them to do something extreme to stop you from running it and now there's more room to be able to throw the ball. So it it starts with being able to run the ball and and then from there it's it's it in the past game it's it's great anticipation, um great timing, right? Maybe big targets, you know, all those things uh kind of come into play, but everything there is is kind of heightened because of the the restricted space, right? So the timing, the ball location, um and then like I said, the ability to run the football in is where it needs to start. >> Specific to the New Orleans game you had two goal line possessions both didn't go the way you wanted. Was that unique because you have a new quarterback in there and timing was all messed up or do you feel that the push you're getting is not good enough? >> Yeah, I I wouldn't say it was the the I'll answer the last part first. I wouldn't say it was the push. Um I think we do a good job of staying low and grinding our feet and trying to move people. Now we movement got us, you know, a little bit on uh really on both of them, but um certainly the one that was, you know, a little bit further out not the fourth and one play. Um so that's something that we're that we're looking at attacking. Um just just being better against the movement, okay? And then uh the other piece of it is just the the the timing and the execution as a group, you know, on the fourth down play uh wasn't wasn't what we wanted there, you know? And and you got to tip their hat to them too and they they played it pretty well, you know, they did they did a good job um as well. >> When you think about a like the success of a run game, for you, what how much of it is on the front scheme and the protection, how much is on like the individual back? >> Uh it's it's all parts, I think. Um it starts with being able to move the line of scrimmage, you know? And I think that we've seen growth in that every week. Now, it hasn't always shown up in the in the production end of it, you know? Um but I do think that we've seen a lot of growth in being able to displace and move the line of scrimmage, which is where it starts. No matter who you have running the ball, no matter what the scheme is, you know, that's where it starts. And then, yeah, from there you try to I mean, the scheme is numbers and angles and matchups. Like that's really what you're looking at. Um you know, how do we how do we get the best matchups that we can as far as blocking the guys that we want to with our guys? A lot of that that comes down to tight ends. And then uh you know, how do we have numbers and and angles advantages by formation? Um so that's a piece of it. And then, yeah, the runner certainly a piece of it as well. Um it's not always the the big runs like I talked about uh with Quinshon specifically. It's it's sometimes it's like, hey, turning two or three into four, five, six cuz now you're staying more efficient, um which is another huge key piece of of being able to run the ball, you know? Everybody wants explosive runs, but the main thing is to try to stay efficient, you know, if you can cuz now you're staying ahead of the chains and it helps your whole offense. >> especially those two 60 plus yard plays that they made. Is is that sort of a glimpse into how they can complement one another in this offense and just, you know, get those explosive plays in slightly different ways? >> Yeah, I mean, sure. Anytime you have um you know, more than one, which we certainly do, uh explosive play potential skill players, I think it's harder to defend. Um yeah, so certainly. >> Another short yardage question. Um are you are you guys reluctant to go a little exotic there with a wildcat look, a direct snap look? We saw a Fannin taking direct snaps in training camp. Are you not there yet to do something like that? >> Uh no, I wouldn't say that. It hasn't come up yet. Um, but we're certainly not No, we're certainly not against that. It's not like we've ruled that out, said, hey, we're not going to do uh any of those things. Some of that's week to week. Um, sometimes those things too are are things that you know, you practice for a number of weeks before you actually see them show up in the game. Uh I would say so that's that's another piece of it uh as well. But no, we're not we're not against any of that. >> Last one. Carol Fanning going earlier, you know, it seems like he opens up this offense when you guys get going and throwing the ball. >> No no doubt. I mean, that that's always getting our best skill players touches um throughout any part of the game and certainly early is is definitely a part of our thought process. We tried to a little bit earlier uh in the game and it just it didn't go his way. I mean, we had one that um one that you know, should have and could have and then we tried to throw a screen to him, you know, didn't get end up uh getting that completed. But yeah, that's that's always something we're that we're trying to do. >> Let's squeeze one more in for him specifically. >> Yeah. >> When the two-point play, how vast is like the playbook on on two-point conversion plays when it's not something you're running like all the time obviously? And what are the conversations like kind of deciding what you think could work in any given scenario? Like like you mentioned when this field is so condensed like that down there. >> That's a great question. So you start obviously by looking at what the the team you're playing does. And now sometimes it's a specific deal, so you may have to go back, you know, years um to look at uh what the defense does in those situations. And if there's a tendency, then yeah, you you know, you try to plan for something and prepare the guys for the looks as much as possible, knowing that like just like any play, it could be something different, right? Um so you try to call plays where depending on the looks, you know, you you think that your better players are probably the primary target and you try to do something that's familiar to the quarterback, you know, so that hey, if it doesn't go as planned, at least we have reps at this play and he's been able he's seen it, you know, against multiple looks so that he has some comfort in the play as well, especially if you're unsure of what you're going to get. Um but often times it does involve going back, you know, a long time in coordinator history uh just to try to get a enough of a sample there um to plan for. >> Appreciate it. >> Yeah. Thanks, guys.

title: 2026 Cleveland Browns Press Conference
text: Uh Tony, I got to tell you, man, we talked about uh the UFFL and the trick plays. Did you see the Raiders reverse they ran on kick return? So, you manifested it. [laughter] It worked. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> No, not for touchdown. I think it got past the four yard line, but I was thinking about you when I saw that play. >> All right. Go ahead. >> What do you got this week? I try to keep it simple trying to get past the 30 yard 35 penalty kick off. What what happened there and then how disappointing is it to get the second one after you just got the first quarter? >> Yeah. So, those are um the little small details, alignment details. You know, you think back to those are install one. We go over, okay, here are the quadrants, guys. These are the rules. You have to stay still from the time the blow the the whistle's blown to the time the ball is caught or hits in the landing zone. these very little details now that you cover early on and and it's a good reminder for me to recover these rules over and over again because in my mind you get what you emphasize and I have to emphasize the rules more frequently throughout the week because I think what happens is you get so caught up in the personnel, you get so caught up in the scheme, you get so caught up in what you're going to do, how you're going to an opponent that some of those small fine details get lost in the shuffle. And so, it's just a great reminder for me that I have to remind these guys every week about the the rules because they are unique and we have a lot of young guys on our team and it and it's their first time through with this new kickoff kickoff return. Um, so that's it. >> Jets are doing on their kickoffs. >> Thought about that or what are your thoughts on that? >> I I think, you know, if you have a guy that can kick off, I know I think Eric Reid can kick off, too. He was at the Kansas City Chiefs for a while. Um, you're talking about Andrew Beck kicking off, right? Um, I think if you have a guy that can do it at a high level and be able to cover down, um, I think it's worth exploring. Um, I'm not sure we have that guy on our team yet, but, uh, you know, if you had that guy, it's always a, you know, a possibility of adding another coverage player to the play. >> Andre with the 51 yard there at the end, just how well he's done. Yeah, I I think I was really happy to see uh Andre go out there and hit that game uh that the tying field goal to keep us in the game, send us to overtime. Um yeah, I think he's just he's gone through some adversity this year and I think he's on his way back up. Um so I'm really excited for him. >> Obviously the weather feel like it's turning here. What does that change for you when you're coaching guys or even just how special teams feels like it changes when weather becomes an issue. >> We went out there today and uh we got some wet ball drill, you know, and I think the guys after the Jets game, we understand how important it is to be prepared for the elements. And so we've really u took on that challenge every week, you know, getting wet ball drill and then going out there. We have days like this where we can go out there in the rain and get some work done. So, it's really just u taking advantage of the opportunities like today where you can go out there and get some work in some inclement weather >> about the the force fumble with Aiden and Donovan. Like what can you what did you switch it out and then what do you take away from that as you try to maybe get more of those kind of big plays on on your side of things? Well, I think, you know, it's it's um a testament to the guys that we have on the punt team that I I get to work with every single day is, you know, they're covering down there. You know, giving everything they got. You know, Aiden's a 280lb man, defensive tackle running down there and um straining great effort and then going to make a t not only going to make a tackle, but getting the ball out at the same time. And then the strain of Donovan McMillan to try to go make the tackle. not quite get the tackle and now he's straining to go get the ball. And just those plays for me are the most exciting just for the guys, you know, and they work so hard. They practice. We cover uh you know, couple time a few times a week throughout uh throughout the week and then to have them have success to put our uh offense in a position to score some points on the plus 19 yard line. Uh that's that's big for us. That that's what that's what we're trying to do, you know? That's that's what we're about. you think it's important to go down to the stadium when the weather turns bad and practice there? >> Uh, you know, it's something to think about. We haven't done it. Um, but I think we get enough wind out here to kind of I know it's different and um we've been blessed with some really nice days in at home games. Um, so things are changing and uh but I I'm I'm lucky to have Andre and Corey and Rex who've kind of been through it. Now, if I had a uh all rookie group, I I definitely think that it's a we we'd have to make a trip to the stadium for sure. >> Out of bounds as much as they do. I mean, you guys got quite, you know, being first to touch the ball on that, but seems like having them maybe run inside of outside seems a little bit just why do they take that outside route the way they did? >> All right. So, when you when you're putting the ball, you're putting it toward usually you're trying to punt it toward the boundary to shorten the field. And so, you have releases by the gunners toward the punt direction. So you'd like for both your gunners to release the same direction. So if you're punting left, both guys release left and one guy ends up into the boundary. Now you can't run out of bounce on your own. A lot of times those corners will force you into the white and so now uh you have to, you know, take a line to reenter. You know what happened on that play was, you know, DT um didn't realize he had gotten in the white, you know, and so we just had a discussion on the sideline and just said, hey, if there's any possibility that you could have gone out, all you got to do is just point to the ball, tell your teammates, you you you and and they touch it. So, it's a it's a big learning experience for us, and unfortunately, it cost us 30 yards of field position, so we had to learn the hard way. Um, but I just don't think that's it's not possible to change what we do in terms of staying out of bounds. That that's just part of the deal. >> I guess outside fans would ever think about what like successful special teams look like. I think a lot of times they just envision pump returns all the time that are breaking big or kickoffs that are breaking big and like hitting every single kick all the time. But as a as a as a person who's working with those units every single week, every single day, what in your mind makes like a successful special teams team, special teams units that you >> I think it comes down to, you know, dominating field position in any way, shape, or form. you know, you could go out there and dominate field position with just the punter and he's, you know, kicking it 50 yards out of bounds, you know, and not giving the return any opportunities or you're, you know, you know, covering uh kickoffs and you're you're getting drive starts on the 25 yardd line inside the 30 uh in coverage and then when you get your opportunities to return the ball, you're getting 10 plus yards of return. you know, you're you're constantly creating favorable field position for your offense and you're setting your defense with a long field. And then when you have opportunities to score or make big plays, you take advantage of those opportunities. So, a good special teams unit dominates field position and also takes advantage of opportunities to score points. >> KC having a little bit of an ankle from last week, can you 100% count on him to return pumps for you this week? I was impressed with Casey like in the game, you know, we were making contingency plans and, you know, he wanted to go out there. So, um, as far as I'm concerned, uh, you know, he's available for us this week and and we'll make adjustments as they come. >> The guy on Sunday for kickoff returns. Is that something that's going to last or you keep trying more guys? >> We're always going to rotate guys. That's how we do things. We always uh making sure guys get multiple reps because you never know what's going to happen in the game. But we're I'm really encouraged by what IB is doing. And so um I I'd love to see more of him. I think he's just going to get better and better at that role and I think he's excited about having that role. >> Dylan Samson just not available for that. >> No, he's available. He's available and uh so I just want to make sure we're smart with him depending on what his role, how much his workload is on offense. um just to make sure I'm keeping in mind what's best for the team, not only for the special teams unit. >> He didn't need to touch that ball, right? Like it wasn't in danger of going in the end zone or anything. Um but I feel like I see that a lot across the ball back, you know, I know you're running, but like take a breath because sometimes >> Absolutely. Yeah, and we have meetings uh every single day and we go through, you know, we always keep an eye on what goes on throughout the league. So, we're always looking at penalties throughout the league. And um Coach Tandy, Keith Tandy, he's my assistant. He he works with the gunners. And, you know, each week we go over those specific situations to just try to keep it front of mind for the guys to make sure that they know, hey, you go out of bounds, you can't be the first one to touch it. And there's a variety of different situations that come up time and time again that you just got to be aware of at the gunner position. And so that that's one of them. And uh you know I think we'll as a unit now we'll all understand the importance of that rule. >> Study which officiating group you have to know whether they're more strict on holding or lenient. >> I do not. No I do not. No. I think that's that's something I've done in the past, but we have not done that this year. >> All right. Thank you. Great. think you guys can do better this week to get better, >> you know, um, every week, whatever it is, we address it, like I always say, because that's just what football is. And in terms of the run defense, you know, great run games are are based on violence, which is what we're built off of, discipline, fits, and straining of the ball. And we'll continue to preach our style of strain and violence and our style of the mind to have do our best in the fits. Practice it like we've been doing it and continue to whatever it is take that approach in everything we're trying to fix. >> I don't know what percentage of plays you've used a third linebacker, but it's a very small percentage and yet teams are adding an extra offensive line against you. Why are you reluctant to add a third line? >> You know, it's has nothing to do with reluctance. It's just constantly about different formations, schemes, people on the field and how we can get our players our to try and get them to be at their best to see the same thing over and over to get their cleats in the ground to get their eyes where they need to be. So, it's more just about repetitions more than anything from that perspective. case of you think your third safety is a better player than your third linebacker. >> No, it has nothing to do with this person's better, this person's better. The whole key to playing great defense is to play as fast as humanly possible. So during a week to get as many reps for as many people as we can between walkthroughs, pre-practice walkthroughs. That's just the approach we've taken. We talked to Jared B and he said that he visited with a a team psychiatrist to help him get better pass rusher. How do you think that's going to help him? >> I mean, I'm not going to discuss Jared Verse in terms of what he does off the field, but I'm really proud of Jared for his approach, for his attitude, uh the way he's working with his teammates and our Dline coaching staff to help himself get to where he wants to go. Do you think >> how close is he to being that player that he was with the Williams? >> You know, I don't look at it as how close he is. I know he is that player and he'll continue to work. He's working on it in practice. He's constantly working and studying film. It's not how close he is. It's just him continuing to do what's best for him to get himself to where he wants to play and us helping him as much as humanly possible. >> You guys always call that line the engine, but I think only three sacks from the unit as a whole over the last three games. So, How do you look at that production? I know last game from other positions, but struggled with it obviously these last three weeks. >> Yeah. Again, you guys have been around me long enough that I I never look at it from one position. It's it's all 11. And and sacks don't just come from the engine across the league. Sacks come from sometimes great coverage. Sacks come from sometimes a good pressure. Sacks sometimes come from the engine. And we will go as our engine goes. And as we continue to go and uh you you continue to see those guys revving that engine up. It's not actually anything about like Dline has to have sacks. It's just us trying to make the offense as as uncomfortable as possible. >> It looks like the Texans are incorporating Tank Dell into their offense more slot receiver. So how does that affect you? Just talk about how his emergence after that severe injury. >> Unbelievable player, right? Unbelievable. I mean, it was unbelievable coming out. Obviously unfortunate with with his injury. Always happy to see a player come back from any type of injury. It's not just Tank. I mean, extremely skilled offense. Um, you could rattle off their whole receiving core and put the tight end in there as well in terms of the pass game, which I know you were referencing. And then kudos to CJ Stra and what they're doing. So, I'm excited for our battle. I I I love our DBs. I love our back seven. And I'm excited for the battle. What what is it about Miles makes him such an effective? >> Man, you know, I could go on for a while. It's kind of like he asked me about Carson last week and I was like, well, he'll just, you know, fix himself. Um, you know, Miles is one of those guys who's self-made, right? And, um, I obviously wasn't here with him previous to this year, but you can see his preparation. You can see his attention to detail, his diligence, his desire to play for his teammates. So, not only is he an effective blitzer, he's an effective cover guy, but he's constantly working on his craft, constantly working on the different schemes of the week and he's asking questions. Hey, Rudy, if we they do this, what about this? He works with Jeff Anderson, our Nicholls coach. And it's really cool to see all that come together and see have success. It's a credit to him. anything I'm sure you're trying to figure it out, but anything schematically you can do to free him up, give him better opportunities um than he's had at his home. >> You know, as a coaching staff and from Monk down to the defensive staff, we're always trying to get all of our players in the best positions and we're always looking schematically, technically to see where we can get all of our players, whether it's Jared or Miles or Carson. Um, so that's just a constant day-to-day process. Obviously, it has to do with the opponent and what we think they're doing or what we think they're going to do to us. And then how can we get our players uh in that best position and be successful by situation as well? >> 100%, but you've got a number of guys on on your side of the ball dealing either coming back from or dealing with injury. Mason, Malik, Denzel, Carson. How much maybe as the weeks go on, do you see maybe improving on some of the things you're working on, stopping the run game, the tackling, uh, and even going into the by-week and just trying to give them more time to come back from what they're going through. >> You know, um, it's probably cliche, but it's end of the NFL season and everyone's beat up week. I don't think, what's the best way for me to say this? Circumstances aren't going to get in the way of us trying to be successful. And whether we're beat up or not, I know those men that you're talking to, they went out and just had an awesome practice, no matter beat up or not, and they do it every day and they give everything for each other in school. But yes, I'm sure they're excited to to get healthy when the by-week comes, but that doesn't mean that they're their mentality is heart, mind, fist, and they're doing it every day. Those guys are in that training room. Those guys are working and they practice their butts off. >> Answer this, but I'm going to ask >> probably not. >> A team like puts four wide outs on the field, which they do. Would you cover that fourth or a quarterback? >> I mean, you don't really think I'm going to answer that question, do you? I appreciate I said you're probably not going to answer this. So, I'll keep what we're doing internally, you know, but I appreciate you asking. >> Yeah, Coach Mon talked yesterday about medical in all phases. Sure. But I just want to ask you about your quarter drives you guys have allowed. What do you do to kind of help when it's late in the game and guys are tired and worn down? What can you do to help them be in a better position to get that crucial stop to, you know, to get off the field and, you know, give the offense the ball back with a lead rather than needing the offense to go back out and get those? you know, we absolutely in those situations want to get off the field and when we don't, it kills us. It kills us football-wise in life. It does. Um, but not no one drive defines a game and I think that's important for the whole team to know and that's what Monk always talks about. Whether it's fast, finishing faster, making a play at the end of the half, going in, knocking, getting a three and out after the halftime, each little six-second play defines the game. And then of course at the end of the game, great defenses try their butts off to finish. And during the week, I'm not going to get into what we do, but what I can promise you is we are always addressing whatever came up headon honestly together and figuring out the best ways. Whether it's in a meeting, whether it's out at practice, whether it's a drill, we do all that and our guys are bought into that. And it's really cool to see. >> Ronnie, being able to practice the last couple days, um, how comfortable are you with he's got to take on that full time. I know he had to fill in early in the season and how have you seen him kind of grow into that from week one? >> Yeah, I think we've all seen him together, you know, grow into it starting with all the great plays he was making on special teams into his role on defense. Not only has made a lot of plays for us defensively and helped us, but communicating at a high level. He's helping us through all the different adjustments that we make. And uh if that is the case, everybody counts on Eman because he's done it already. When called upon special teams, he did it. When called upon to come in a game, he does it. When called upon in crucial third down, he does it. So if he's out there, nobody's going to bat an eye, including him. >> This and you're getting rush from the interior, but the fact that you guys really aren't getting what you might have expected or originally thought you were going to get from your edge rushers. Can you play the kind of attack style defense effectively the way that you want to without those guys on edge? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. Again, the attack style defense, while we always reference it starting with the engine, which it always will be, that is the core of what we do, but our text style defense is all 11. It's start with the engine and it goes to the second level of getting downhill. It gets to the third level of protecting us uh on deep balls and explosive plays. And then when a third level players has to come down to the second level, the attack style defense has to do with pressure bringing different people. So we are an attack style defense and I'm proud of the way those guys are doing it. Thank you. >> Awesome. All right. For sure. Yeah, you got it.

title: Travis Switzer Press Conference | November 12th, 2026
text: Yeah. All right, guys. Fire away. >> So, a return to um Deshawn, of course, this week. So, what do you um need to see from Deshawn? What are you expecting from him as he gets back out there? Hey, I don't think it's changed um from the same things that we were looking for before, you know, and and the things we've been preaching. Um you know, let's do a great job with the operation piece. Uh let's take care of the ball, you know, make the plays we're supposed to make and and uh and go let it rip. Yeah. I don't think it's really changed. >> I know you guys Todd talk about slow start, right? He says he's doing everything he can. So, I'm curious, what have you guys tried and then what is still up to try to kind of jump start this thing in the first quarter? Yeah, we've first thing as a staff, we looked at everything that we've done early in games and like when we looked at it, it was like, man, we got we've kind of tried a little bit of everything, you know, as far as, hey, let's um maybe call some CAM plays early or uh we've tried running it early, we've tried movement passes, we've tried, you know, so we looked at that and it was nothing really spiked out as far as um hey, this is the direction we should go there. But uh and then we've also just stressed it to the guys, especially early in practice, you know, like Wednesday's the first period is always a tempo period at the first team period, you know, so we've tried to stress it there. It's like, okay, we're going fast, but also, hey, we're trying to start fast. Like that's the point of uh of this um you know, of this period here. And yeah, I can't say that it's been like, you know, one thing that jumped out to us. We just got to keep attacking it and and try to stress it. Um yeah, and just try to get get better there. Seems like Spencer has had maybe like a bit of a rough go the past couple to some really tough edge rushers. Um just what can he do to be better? What can you guys do as a staff and as a offense to maybe put put him in some better positions against some of these tough matchups? >> Yeah, I mean we're always conscious uh I'll answer the last part of it first. We're always conscious of the matchups there. And I mean look it there's good edge rusher edge rushers all around the league and it doesn't matter who's at tackle, you know, you're going to chip and you're going to do those things for the elite edge rushers. So, that's something that's always at the front of our mind um of every game plan. But, as far as you know, Spencer as an individual, just keep trusting his technique and keep growing his technique. You know, um the one thing Hop mentioned the other day was, you know, there there's now some tape out there, you know, on him. So, uh you know, guys may have a plan, you know, maybe that's part of it. And then he just needs to keep developing his techniques and really trusting himself because like he's shown the ability to be as good as he wants to be and and he wants to be good. I mean, he's wired the right way. He's very diligent. Um, so yeah, just keep keep trusting your techniques and keep developing uh your techniques. >> You've had two games in particular [clears throat] have the ball in the lead with four minutes to go in the game. How frustrating is that to you coaches that you can't can get a four-minute offense going? I >> I think it's frustrating to all of us. I mean, not just the coaches, right? I mean, that the the players felt the same way. Um, obviously last week we had, you know, the penalty that kind of set us set us back. um uh as as far as moving forward, you just keep attacking it, you know, and and yes, it's been frustrating, but the more situations that we're put in there, you know, the better we're going to be as we move forward. You you just like anything, you you get what you emphasize. So, um yeah, you stress it to the guys, you get in the right mindset. Uh execution's at a premium, right, in those parts of the game. Uh and that's what you stress. >> Does it keep coming back to penalties? >> Uh I mean, certainly the one did, you know, last week. Um, and that's certainly something that we've been attacking this week. I mean, uh, from from the top down. I mean, co coach's team meeting, uh, you know, yesterday included that type of stuff. So, yeah. I mean, that's that's certainly something that that we're attacking this week. >> Was very clear yesterday. He's not, you know, making any lineup changes with the offensive line. Those are the five best guys and he's sticking with them. Um, so outside of making a lineup change, you know, h how do you course correct on those penalties? So that you know, you know, there's just been so many of those those drive killers that you've had this year. So outside of making a line of change, just what do you do to to get those penalties to come down? >> Yeah, I think and and this this is what he did yesterday. I think you you got to just be honest. Hey, this is where we are. like we're not good in this area, you know, and and you put up the stats and you show the guys and um so that draws attention to it and that's part of it. The other the other thing is looking at what type of penalties you have, right? Like the ones that you that you have no uh tolerance for are the ones that take no talent that it's pre- snap penalties, right? It's it's snap count things. It's things that are just focus and diligence from the group, right? Um so those are the ones that you really try to attack. uh as far as holding and things like that, do you coach guys to keep hands inside? Of course. You know what I mean? But some of those are did they see it? And a lot of those can be 5050. So all you can do is coach the technique, right? So that you try to lower the likelihood as as much as possible uh of all those. But yeah, you just you emphasize it. Um look at which ones they are, right? And and then just try to attack it. >> How does knowing that Houston pass rush like is how does that affect uh the game plan? Uh yeah, I mean it it affects everything that you do in the pass game. You know, that's what you have to think about first. Uh and there's there's everybody's got a piece of that, right? The the chip plan that like I said, we have every week and most teams have every week. Um and then how you're going to distribute routes and all that, getting the ball out on time. Um handling the different protection looks that they give you because that can hinder your ability to chip at times. Um yeah, so it's really all inclusive. But to to answer your question, I mean, anytime you play premier pass rushers, that's got to be at the front of your mind. um when it comes to any pass play really. >> How long has Quinn Sean Judkins been running the ball for you? Just you know individually looking at his >> Yeah, I think he's a very physical um downhill runner and he's tough to tackle, you know, and he also he's been doing a great job of maximizing downhill, you know, runs for us even when it might not look like there's not a whole lot there. Um and I think it's just continuing to try to dip into that as much as we can. Um, and then continue to work with him on on the other things that maybe are things he hasn't done a ton of, right, in his career. Um, uh, different different run schemes. I mean, you know, and you just keep attacking it that way. >> The red zone numbers haven't been great in recent weeks and really like as a season long um, trend. What what does it take not just for you guys specifically, not like fans to diagnose your issues, but like what do good red zone offenses do? Well, I mean, it it starts with, in my opinion, your ability to run the football in. I mean, the the lower that you get down there, the less room there is to throw, okay? And if you're able to run it in, now you're going to force them to do something extreme to stop you from running it. And now there's more room to be able to throw the ball. So, it it starts with being able to run the ball in. And then from there, it's it's in the pass game, it's it's great anticipation, um, great timing, right? Maybe big targets, you know, all those things uh kind of come into play. But everything there is is kind of heightened because of the the restricted space, right? So the timing, the ball location, um, and then like I said, the ability to run the football in is where it needs to start. >> So specific to the New Orleans game, you had two goal line possessions and both didn't go the way you wanted. Was that unique because you have a new quarterback in there and timing was all messed up, or do you feel that the push you're getting is not good enough? Yeah, I I wouldn't say it was the the I'll answer the last part first. I wouldn't say it was the push. Um I think we do a good job of staying low and grinding our feet and trying to move people. Now we movement got us, you know, a little bit on uh really on both of them, but um certainly the one that was, you know, a little bit further out, not the fourth and one play. Um so that's something that we're that we're looking at attacking. Um just just being better against the movement. Okay. And then uh the other piece of it is just the the the timing and the execution as a group, you know, on the fourth down play uh wasn't wasn't what we wanted there, you know, and and you got to tip their hat to them, too. I mean, they they played it pretty well, you know, they they did a good job um as well. >> When you when you think about like the success of a run game for you, what how much of it is on the front scheme and the protection? How much of it is on like the individual back? >> Uh it's it's all parts, I think. Um, it starts with being able to move the line of scrimmage, you know, and I think that we've seen growth in that every week. Now, it hasn't always shown up in the in the production end of it, you know, um, but I do think that we've seen a lot of growth in being able to displace and move the line of scrimmage, which is where it starts. No matter who you have running the ball, no matter what the scheme is, you know, that's where it starts. And then, yeah, from there, you try to I mean, the scheme is numbers and angles and matchups. Like, that's really what you're looking at. um you know, how do we how do we get the best matchups that we can as far as blocking the guys that we want to with our guys? A lot of that that comes down to tight ends and then uh you know, how do we have numbers and and angles advantages by formation. Um so that's a piece of it. And then yeah, the runner certainly a piece of it as well. Um it's not always the the big runs like I talked about uh with Quinn Sean specifically. It's sometimes it's like hey turning two or three into four, five, six because now you're staying more efficient. Um, which is another huge key piece of of being able to run the ball. You know, everybody wants explosive runs, but the main thing is to try to stay efficient, you know, if you can because now you're staying ahead of the chains and it helps your whole offense. >> Travis, with Casey and especially those two 16 plus yard plays that they made. Is is that sort of a glimpse into how they can complement one another in this offense and just, you know, get those explosive plays in slightly different ways? >> Yeah, I mean, sure. anytime you have um you know more than one which we certainly do uh explosive play potential skill players I think it's harder to defend um yeah so certainly another short yardage question are you are you guys reluctant to go a little exotic there with a wildcat look a direct snap look we saw Fannon taking direct snaps in training camp are you not there yet to do something like that >> uh no I wouldn't say that it hasn't come up yet. Um, but we're certainly not No, we're certainly not against that. It's not like we've ruled that out and said, "Hey, we're not going to do uh any of those things." Some of that's week to week. Um, sometimes those things too are are things that, you know, you practice for a number of weeks before you actually see him show up in a game. Uh, I would say so that's that's another piece of it uh as well. But no, we're not we're not against any of that. >> Last one. >> Harold Fannon going earlier, you know, seems like he opens up this offense. You guys need to know the ball. No, no doubt. I mean, that that's always getting our best skilled players touches um throughout any part of the game and certainly early is is definitely a part of our thought process. We tried to a little bit earlier uh in the game and it just it didn't go his way. I mean, we had one that um one that, you know, should have and could have and then we tried to throw a screen to him, you know, didn't get end up uh getting that completed. But yeah, that's that's always something we're that we're trying to do. >> Let's squeeze one more. >> Yeah. um when the two-point play, how vast is like the play book on two-point conversion plays when it's not something you're running like all the time obviously and what are the conversations like kind of deciding what you think could work in any given scenario like like you mentioned when the field is so condensed like that down there. >> That's a great question. So you start obviously by looking at what the the team you're playing does and now sometimes it's a specific deal. So you may have to go back, you know, years um to look at uh what the defense does in those situations. And if there's a tendency, then yeah, you, you know, you try to plan for something and prepare the guys for the looks as much as possible, knowing that like just like any play, it could be something different, right? Um, so you try to call plays where depending on the looks, you know, you you think that your better players are probably the primary target and you try to do something that's familiar to the quarterback, you know, so that hey, if it doesn't go as planned, at least we have reps at this play and he's been able he's seen it, you know, against multiple looks so he has some comfort in the play as well, especially if you're unsure of what you're going to get. Um, but oftentimes it does involve going back, you know, a long time in coordinator history, uh, just to try to get a enough of a sample there, um, to plan for. >> Appreciate it. >> Yeah. Thanks, guys.

title: Jared Verse, Denzel Boston & Carson Schwesinger Press Conference | November 12th, 2026
text: We're good. I know we talked about the run defense a bunch and the numbers don't look good last week. What did you see when you watched it? Did you see any um signs of improvement against the Saints? I think I think we definitely have signs of improvement, but it's too late in the season for us to have these little uh issues where one play, you know, starts turning into something bigger and it becomes spilling out to the whole defensive line. We all need to step up a little bit more. I think uh myself included, I can do a better job of closing the B gap, but I think we can all do a better job and uh just winning our one ones collectively. >> Was it tackling better earlier in the season than it has been the last couple weeks? >> I think it's just, you know, wearing tear on the bodies. I think we all have to be uh make it cognizant in our minds that we have to make these tackles, be more cognizant of it, and just get our hands on the ball carry and just bring them down. I think, you know, early in the season it was good. I think right now it's not as great, but I think we can definitely do better. >> Uh Jerry, uh the Texans see a shot hasn't been pressured that much. They haven't allowed many sacks. What have you seen from them and kind of what's the key? >> Yeah, I think I think CJ's playing amazing right now. I think he's definitely gotten better at uh you know being able to see and you know translate that to the game and I think he's definitely taking the offseason he had to develop and become a way better player in the aspect of being a quarterback. I think that the offensive line is very good and I think they uh they go up against some very good rush groups and everything like that. I think we just got to focus on us. You know I think we do a very good job of getting after the quarterback, you know, and I think we just going to do our thing. >> Jared, I know we we've talked to you individually about your sack production, but I think over the last three games the Dline total has only had three sacks. Is that something that you guys talk about as a group? Like, hey, for for this defense to be its best, we we need to create more pressure. >> I think that goes without saying. I think we all know that. I think we go as or the engine goes. And I think we are the engine. I think Malik, you know, Mason, me, myself included, and then Isaiah, I think we have to start off by being better, you know, as a collective for. I think we can all get to the quarterback better. You know, missing Malik last week was a huge key issue for us. You know, he's somebody that generates a lot of pressure for us. But I think myself, you know, I'm mainly going to put it on myself. I haven't played well at all this season. I think uh after taking a little bit of time looking at me at what I can do better cuz I think uh that group goes alo that's my mindset and anything I do. >> J the first time that you've gone through like like long in terms of like I think this your first year or so in Los Angeles you come through a couple games. What did you do to kind of get past that game and just kind of you know make sure that it didn't affect you the entire game? >> You got to keep struggling. I mean you can't do anything uh more than what you can do. You can't go out there and start doing some crazy things like going like like a training with a monk or nothing like that. Like it's just you just got to keep working. Obviously like I'm I'm upset with the way I've been playing. I don't think it's anything physical. It was nothing wrong with my body. It's nothing like that. I think it was a mental aspect of the game and I think I've attacked it very well these last couple weeks, but I think this past week is a big key thing that I've done that I'm I'm very excited for this next week. >> Was this a week that you kind of picked Titus's brain a little bit more? You guys as a defensive line unit? >> Definitely. you know, he's even came to us before we even had the chance to come to him. He came to us, gave us a couple key tips, you know, give uh, you know, cuz obviously, you know, we a teammate now. Obviously, that was the old teammates and everything like that, but he's came to us, give us some good tips on how we can attack these guys and get to the quarterback. >> When you say when you say you haven't played well at all, I mean, that was where you're what do you think why do you think that is? No, >> I think it was just a mental aspect of the game. I I can uh we could be here all day and I could talk to you about each key play that we played all season long, but I think that would be a waste of all of our time. It's just simple to say, you know, I think the Browns fans are upset about it. I'm upset about it. I think we all have a reason to be upset. I just haven't done enough and I think I've I've taken the time to figure out what the issue was. I've attacked it and I think I'm ready for this week. >> Talk about mental stamina when it comes to like penalties and stuff like that. You guys have had some late game situations, giving up points when you've had opportunities to to close games out. How do you attack mental stamina and become better at that so that when physical moments pop up, you guys can do what it takes to to close out? >> I mean, we can't get comfortable. Football is a very long game. You It's a 60-minute game. If you played great for 58 minutes and then those last two minutes, you give up nine points, you not you didn't do anything right. You failed yourself and failed the whole group and the organization. At the end of the day, we've been doing that for a long time. We play great the first 58 minutes. We might not play great the first drive and then the rest of the game's amazing, but then that first drive might come back to haunt us. So, we we've done a lot of things like that. I think it's just the aspect of realizing we have to be better. You have to win your one on 11. I preach that and I realize that every time I you look anybody in the eyes, we just got to win. Everybody's got to win that one-on-one. If we do that, we're going to be a great team. >> Two questions real quick. Um the first one is, can you share with us what did you identify maybe on film or whatever or what's this change that you have made this week to try to spark your game? I I would more so prefer to keep that to myself. I I'm excited for it. But I've uh I took a lot of time self-growth and uh I met with Dr. People a little bit and I figured out what my issue was. >> Okay. And then and who is this doctor? >> It's our team psychiatrist. >> Okay. And so do you think it was something sort of like >> psych? Psychologist. >> Was it something psychiatrist >> like blocking you, you know, more mentally? >> I think it was definitely a mental block. My I've trained my body every day to push myself to the limits of what I'm physically capable of doing. So, I don't think it was any issue with my body, but I think I've uh taken the steps to figure out what it was after meeting with a couple people and everything like that, but to keep it from getting further than that, I'm just going to leave it at that. >> Okay. And then, um, I wanted to ask you also, um, Mason McCormack did not get fined for the plant of you. What did you think of that? >> Obviously, that that's, uh, what was that, two weeks ago? Three weeks ago. Can't do nothing about it now. The play happened. Can't be upset about it. It happened. It's football. >> Last one from Tony. Um, I don't know what percentage of players you guys only feel two linebackers. It's a large percentage. In the past, defenses have improved the run by putting a third linebacker on the field. So, is that being discussed? >> We're going to stop the run with four and we're going to stop it with two linebackers behind us cuz that's what we're made of and that's what we're capable of doing. Thanks a lot. H. >> He's ready. >> Yes, sir. He's ready to go. You be back out there today? >> Um, working for it. Yeah, that's that's the goal today. >> You feel better than you did a few days ago? >> 100% feel better. Definitely uh on the right path. Definitely just trending up each and every day. >> Denzel, do you guys feel a sense of urgency to get in this week after going into >> Oh, for sure. You know, I think no one likes to lose. No one wants to lose. you know, that was a tough uh loss that we had last week. Um, we got to move on from it and definitely strive, you know, scratch, claw, whatever we got to do to get this next win to get us back on that winning track and and get those good good vibes back around the city, you know? >> I know last week we talked about the rookie wall and it's been a long season. Like, are is there part of you looking forward to the by-week to kind of decoy present it? >> Definitely. you know, get get to get the bye-week, you know, really get to reflect on the first half of the season, you know, get to watch over what you need to and also, you know, let the body recover, let the body heal up, and then get ready to go for that second half. I think we got a great bye-week, you know, it's like right in the smack middle of the season. So, um, yeah, heal up, take some time to reflect and get ready to rock for those next eight weeks. >> You and Casey both had, you know, some big plays on Sunday in that game. How much do you feel that that game sort of exemplified a little bit of like the dynamic that you guys can be in the confidence? >> Yeah, I think that's actually like the first game where we have been able to really show that and like both of us are making plays at the same time on the field. Um I think it it just was the first showing of our complimentary duo that we have, you know, and I think that there's a lot more to build on, you know. I think that there's still more for us to go out there and show. Um and I think every day we work towards that goal as well. How about you feel with Deshawn being back out there and have you guys kind of going back to your regular candy one? How do you feel about all that? >> Yeah, you know, I think it's just, you know, getting back into another rhythm again. Um, you know, getting Deshawn back out there, making sure that he's feeling comfortable, making sure that, you know, um, we're on top of our assignments, our alignments, and, you know, making sure the quarterback feels good with the people that are out there on the field and that he trusts everyone to make plays, um, no matter who's on the field at the time. Did you guys feel is there anything that you guys you two can do to uh you know kind of rejuvenate the the deep ball? It seems like sometimes like you guys could maybe connect a little bit better. Is there anything we can do during practice, after practice communicating wise to get that rolling? >> Yeah, for sure. I think um you know, we just got to we got to rep it more. We got to get more reps with each other and understand what we're seeing in different looks. And I think that comes not just from um getting reps on the field, but also seeing it together. you know, seeing that when this look happens, this is kind of what I'm thinking or when this look happens from my point of view, this is what he's thinking, you know. So, um, just getting on the same page and make sure that we stay on the good track and just keep building a good rapport. >> I know we talked about it earlier in the season when you had a couple of those eight balls, but how much do you enjoy, you know, like an explosive play like that? And then the one last week, did you know you had him when you did that little stutter? >> Oh, for sure. Once I hit the stutter, um, and I got the separation, I kind of knew like, you know, that we have a big play that could happen here. Um, when I seen the ball in the air, I was like, you know, we got to go get that. Let's come back down and go get it and then try to get in the end zone. Um, he got me by my shirt. Unfortunately, didn't get in the end zone. I kind of look at that. I will never um have a long undershirt again. It's going to be cropped, cut, cut, cropped off um probably rest of my career in the NFL. So, um but yeah, no, definitely after the stutter, I knew it was going to be a big play. Um it was just a matter of time if the ball was going to find me and if the play was going to be made. What about just the fact you caught it on uh the helmet, the guy's helmet and like the reaction after that and and how much do you relish a play like that because it just seemed like using your size, you know, to your advantage. >> Yeah, like you just said, you know, using my size to my advantage, understanding that an advantage and a superpower that I was gifted by God was to be able to go get the ball, you know, and um being able to track the ball in a good way. So, um but I think it's just all about momentum when those big plays happen. You know, you get a burst of energy. It feels like the whole team, the sideline, everyone kind of gets very excited. So, um I think it helps with switching momentum in the game. Um especially in a tight game that we were in. >> I know you want to win first obviously 20 yards a catch. A goal of yours this year? >> A goal? Um my goal is really Yeah. Like obviously just to win games, you know, put the team in the best position to succeed um at the highest rate and, you know, just control what I can control. Um obviously stats are great, all that stuff's awesome. Um but at the end of the day, I just I just want to win. go to the playoffs, you know, have a chance to go win a Super Bowl. >> And so, a team that's so good at putting pressure in the quarterback as Texans are, how does that affect the game plan? >> Yeah, you know, I think um that we just have to focus on what we can control, you know, um focus on our game plan and not focus on their game plan, not and understand that just as much as they have game records, we also have game records on the other side of the field, too, you know. So, um just making sure that, you know, we keep it about us and don't focus on so much of what they can do and, you know, what we can control. What um what what has allowed kind of the young guys to just really thrive? I know last game Casey Harold, you what is it what has kind of allowed all you guys to to really thrive? >> Um I think being able for us to bounce off each other um you know different looks, different um we're all learning this offense together and and you know growing with it throughout this year. And then also I think um us just being able to have trust from our coaches, trust from our fellow guys around us, our teammates, that you know we're out there, we're the best at what we do and that we're going to be able to get the job done in any given circumstance. >> Thanks guys. >> Thank you. >> Yeah. Thank you. the time crunch, guys. >> Carson Jared said that he despite the numbers against the Saints, he thought there were signs of improvement against the run defense. [snorts] What did you see? >> Yeah, I think we had some improvement. Um, just recognizing stuff, communication, and and executing our calls and and like ID said, there was a a few uh execution errors. Um, but overall, especially after the the first drive throughout most of the rest of the game, I think we did a good job and it's just a matter of finishing after that. >> Concerning run defense, um, historically, you had a third linebacker who helped to run the def. Has that been talked about? >> Uh, no. >> I mean, >> well, we just we're we're we're running what's called here. I think we we have the capability to to to stop uh the run and whatever we're in, and it's more of our job to to be able to go out and do that. >> Carson, what about Straoud and and what are you seeing from him given how well they've been playing over these last >> Yeah, he's a he's a he's a good player. He's obviously um got experience over over the the years he's been in the league and um they've got they've got a lot of weapons to be able to throw to um and and they've they've gained some throughout the year as well. Um so really uh really good at finding them and then um you know just got to like we've been talking about keep keep a guy like that in the pocket and and and get uh get to get to him. I don't know how many like most defensive defense like you saw that kind of down aggressive. >> Well, you just got to be able to eliminate the explosive passes. I think that's a big thing for their offense and um just know going into it uh what what our keys are to be able to do that. >> When you mentioned the need to finish, what do what did you see last week and a couple times early this year that's preventing you guys from getting that big stop? just execution in the end and and we we got to have all 11 guys doing our job and um you know, especially those last couple drives. It's it's not it's not everyone as a whole, but um it's it's different people on every play and so we just got to have that mindset that that we're all going to be doing our jobs and and executing what we got to do uh that late in the game >> against Pittsburgh. Um I don't know if [snorts] you thought you struggled, but you gave up a couple plays and then you played so well against New Orleans. like did you feel the need to have a big personal like kind of bounce back? >> Um, no. I think I'm focused on each week as it comes out. I think um there were things obviously to to to get right in terms of uh after that Pittsburgh game and and and make make sure I'm going into the game uh uh feeling good and um so just was was focused on that throughout the week. >> What is it about you Carson that allows you to play it? Well, everybody really in in the NFL is playing with with with something. And so, um, you know, it's it's just, you know, knowing the difference between being hurt and being injured and and doing everything you can and throughout the week to to get yourself ready to go for the game. And we got a lot of guys who who are, uh, you know, very disciplined and getting their bodies right and and making sure that they're able to help us win on on Sundays. >> Um, going back to their kind of pass game, like do they do anything that stands out in terms of how they're able to be so explosive? Uh, well, they have, like I said, they've got they've got a lot of good receivers. They got a quarterback who knows that who who who can throw the ball deep, especially when uh, you know, he's got a clean pocket and, um, so you got to be able to cover those guys and execute um, uh, to eliminate the explosive passes. >> Good guy.
