There's more third and longs than I feel like I've ever seen uh at this point of the year in in many cases throughout the entire course of a year and we're halfway through. So I think they do a great job of just applying pressure and making you make mistakes and um that's why it's so important for us to play a clean game. >> Obviously a lot can change between week one and today. Is there a balance between here's what they did in week one versus here's what they've done in recent weeks in terms of studying that? Yeah, there there's always a natural evolution throughout the course of a season. So, yeah, I think you you study it, but they've definitely done some different things really in in every phase of the game. >> Can you get Scott Moore back? >> Well, he's a big he's a big time weapon. So, uh if he's able to go, that that'll definitely boost our returns. And then also, you know, we'll see how we use them on offense. >> How are you guys a different team than the week one team that faced the Vikings in Minnesota? Well, I think everybody's a different team. You know, week one, you might as well throw week one out the window in most instances. Uh, a lot of there's a lot of craziness that goes on, especially in week one. You know, unscotted looks just um and you just never know what you're going to get. So, I do think it it's going to be helpful. that place is such a hard place to play and it caused us some issues where we didn't have everybody on the same page, especially from an offensive standpoint. Now, I would say the uh the the pressure is going to be on our defense in regards to being able to communicate and getting all 11 on the same page. And knowing that with a new quarterback in there, there's probably going to be some wrinkles that we haven't seen. On that note, what have you learned about you and your team and the resilience you guys show and the confidence you've built over the last >> I think you just hit hit both of them right there. I think we got a resilient group that uh never feels like they're out of the fight no matter what the circumstances and they're going to keep battling and that's all you can really ask for. You got to just try to truly embrace that one play mindset uh one play mindset and just keep going and then where wherever the score is at the end that's the score. Did Josh have his surgery yet? >> Not yet. >> So then you won't know till after that as far as the long term. >> Yeah, tomorrow. >> It's kind of off topic. Do you think Warren Bronson's going to have a chance to play this year? >> I would I would expect that, but um what are we five weeks since he's had surgery or whatever and that usually takes a little bit longer time to recover than five weeks. >> What do you thought of the season that Carl Brooks has had? You know, especially with some of the things you guys have kind of dealt with injury-wise and defensively. Yeah, I think he's done an outstanding job. Just a consistent force on the inside. Um, you know, and and just goes out there and does his job and does it at a high level. >> We've seen what Chris Brooks can do on passing downs. What is what would he give you as a ball carrier? >> Well, I think he he ripped off a couple nice runs in that game the first time we played him. And I think the the running game, especially the later you go in the season, the more important it is. Um, as the weather turns, especially at home, you better be able to run the football. What's the uh challenge Van Ginkle presents as far as he can like basically do everything, can't he? >> Yeah, he's on the ball, off the ball, can play coverage, can rush the passer. I I just think his instincts are on another level than most. Uh he just he he can recognize plays and he'll play out of things and you might think you have something and then oh no, Van Gingle's there and he he'll take it away. So, I think he's just a a highly intelligent football player that plays the game at at a really high level. >> Matt, with Jordan winning obviously the NFC offensive player of the week, does anything surprise you with him anymore in terms of just obviously what he can do, but just is it is there more that's there more in the tank obviously with him too? >> Well, I mean, I'd say he's he's pretty consistent and we hit the resiliency piece. He's so poised, so resilient. He doesn't allow one play to affect the next. Uh he's been doing this under duress in in many situations and he still continues to deliver. So I think he's he's playing as well as anybody in the league right now. >> Feels good. >> Have a good one.

title: Dak Prescott on 49ers Matchup | Player Interviews
text: D, simple question up front. How do you guys turn the corner and start getting wins at home? What's the difference between what's going on with you guys successfully on the road versus your struggles at home? >> Yeah, we got to win. Uh, simple. I think Shotty says it best out of the game. The best way to learn to win is to win. And so, um, you know, last week getting into that game the way it ended and, you know, having to go down and having to win and defense having to get a stop that that's real, you know, and that's what games are about. And so, for me, it's about understanding that they're going to come down to the last drive and if they don't, cool. like we'll worry about that then, but expect them to come down to the live drive on either side of the ball and and we've got to go make the plays to win and ultimately that's what the NFL is about and that's what makes it great. And so, um, we got to expect a four quarter game, if not more, and and plan to make the plays when when they're, uh, needed to be made. >> And just talk about making sure that you're staying where your feet are as far as just focusing on the 2026 49ers and not what's happened historically against you guys when you play those games. >> Yeah. Um, I think it's easy. I mean, for me, I'm always right where my feet are. And uh I know those LA last years don't serve anything for this. I mean, you're talking what? New coaches and and a lot new players since just the last time we played them. And so, um it's easy for me and just uh understanding that the rival is still there. They're going to try to come in with a level of physicality that we we can't say what we're going to match, but we've got to bring our own our own physicality and start this thing fast and understand the kind of game it's going to be. >> Oh, so was your teammate obviously for a long time. What did you come to appreciate about him and what are you seeing on film and St. Fran? Yeah, I mean the same the same guy that that that was here and just a guy that that loves football is flying around. Um motor is is at a thousand and that's obviously uh it shows up, you know, it shows up and he's not quitting on a play. Um I'm sure he's going to be know excited to try to get a sack on me, but he's a guy who does everything the right way, always took care of his body. Um loved his teammates and I'm excited to see him tonight. >> Maybe not because it's the 49ers because you know last year don't matter, but they are seven and one, one of the best team in the league. You guys only got one win over the last two years of a team with winning record. Does that matter beating a team of that caliber and really putting some juice behind the momentum if y'all get the two game winning streak? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, playing as good as a team, right? I think I mean they're one or two seed right now in the NFC and just one seed. Yeah. And then right having an opportunity to get them here at home and can't ask for anything much better, especially where we are and what we've been where we've been right now in our season. And um yeah, as I said, momentum is real. It was great to get a win last week, but uh this is a real challenge, real challenge, and a real opportunity uh for us to capitalize on. >> Overshan just said that he didn't think his penalty was a sign that this is an undisiplined team. Do you agree with that? >> Um yeah, I agree with just I mean, obviously in that that play, I mean, yeah, I mean, guys excited guy just, you know, wanted to go celebrate with with his guy. And I mean, I saw the video. I've really only seen it once and right felt like he caught himself midway through like what the hell am I doing out here? So, um, you you can't put that on coaches. You know, O's got to be accountable in that, and I'm pretty sure he has been, and probably to you guys, and I know he was to me and accepting, you know, you just can't do that. Um, but we can't have the mini spin as we did in in this past game on offense, defense, all the way across the board. We've got to clean it up. Simple as that. >> In in that moment, you did have a pretty heated comment for your sideline. Was that the message that you were trying to send at that very moment? >> Yeah, it was just be more disciplined. You know, I didn't understand that it was just, oh, I didn't know if they threw it. I didn't realize like players could come off the sideline even in uniform and just, you know, that many guys celebrate. And yeah, for me, I'm just mad that was another penalty thrown. Uh, and it's one of those, you know, I'm never going to take ask players to take away their energy or or to compress their excitement or anything or suppress their excitement or anything like that. But, you know, plan to make those turnovers, have some celebrations, but act like we've been there before. And I I think what I at that moment, what I said was was heard. >> This game is a cerebral game between you and Fred Warner. Uh yeah, a good bit. I mean, obviously he's uh the best probably linebacker, you know what I'm saying, in the NFL right now. And you just said it, the way he plays the game mentally of reading the splits, reading the uh you know, the the back, whether he's in the near and the far, making making his different calls and um they're simple defense because he can get them in what they need to be and they play fast and they play they play hard and so um yeah, there's a little bit of a chess match there, but it's no different than the the the play callers calling the plays. And at the end of the day, it's about execution. I know you have to focus on yourself, but you guys need the Giants to lose a game or so. Do you find yourself rooting for Washington tonight? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I find myself rooting against any team that plays NFC East. [laughter] >> Two NFC East teams >> and then the one that does a favor when loses. So, [laughter] yeah. Uh obviously, who is it tonight? I'm sorry. Washington. Yeah. And DQ. Like, you know, I'm [laughter] cheering for DQ all day long. So, uh yeah, that's obvious. said, "No, I mean, I'm not necessarily there. There's a bunch of games left and we've got to still play them. So, um, no worry in that sense of what they're doing, but yeah, you obviously want them to lose and you're going to cheer for the other team to get that done." >> D, how do you plan when there's uncertainty around whether George will be able to play or not play? >> Uh, I mean, we prepare, we put in the plays, you know, for him to play, and we've got, uh, guys that will be able to be ready to step up. I mean, Flo's showing what he's done and the rest of the guys are are itching to get an opportunity if that's what if that's what it comes to. >> Even with George out, see put up almost 200 yards. Just how valuable is he and especially being able to put him anywhere in the formation? >> Yeah, I don't know if I can speak and just get the words to say how valuable that guy is, and just what he means to this offense, what he means to me, and just how great he's been and and getting open and understanding what we're trying to accomplish. And uh not only that, just the communication throughout the game. I think that's where he's taken such a huge step and such a step that that's big for me is just being able to go talk to him after plays. Not that we haven't been able to, but getting such a clear answer back of what he's saying or what he wants what what he wants to get done or, you know, maybe even taking some ownership on something that's already happened. And so, he's in a great spot. He's playing great ball. Um, you can tell just just the way that he's practicing, the way that he approaches the building. Um, yeah, we just got to keep finding a way to feed him. >> Going back to the thing, is there something to having a good cop bad? In other words, is it your place to be to be disciplining some of these guys or saying something after a penalty like that? I know Treyman used to get frustrated, you know, during the Barry era. He felt like that wasn't his job and it frustrated him. Is is that something that's going on here or is that just it was like a oneoff thing? >> Yeah, I mean I was pissed. um I spoke my mind and I think uh I don't think I've ever been short or shy too in in a moment when it's you know truly truly bothered me and yeah that was just a big play and did you know turnover or excuse me turnover happened and a flag comes out and yeah it's just like we did did some great great stuff here like let's not minimize it and so I'm not going to get into you know whose job if I need to be the disciplinary if others aren't we're grown men at the end of the day I don't think and me personally if you need to somebody to tell you what you should and shouldn't do. I don't know if this is the business for you. >> You guys had so many strong leaders as a rookie and then I think of some of those guys that have moved on obviously. When did you start feeling comfortable in that role? >> Early on. Uh rookie year. And I think it's, you know, some of those other leaders that that you're probably talking about of really telling me to be myself. Um I it's always kind of been in me, I guess, right? To to lead people and and want to be the voice. And so, you know, as a rookie, you're just natural. Like, I'm going just get in where I fit in. Yeah, I know I'm the quarterback, but I've got Jason Whitten, I've got Shawn Lee, I've got these guys. But when those guys elevate you and really um allow you to step into that position that you want to be um from day one, I don't know if I would have turned out to be the player that that I am if I didn't have those guys encouraging me to know, don't hold back. Like, I don't care if you're a rookie, you're our guy, and we're following you. I know you said that the coaches and players have changed over the years with this Niners thing, but there's something about the core of their defense that remains the same from when you started playing them a couple years ago, even if the names and coaches are different, like how they play stylistically. >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, absolutely. And I mean, even, you know, coordinators for them have changed and they're still doing the what they want to do on defense or what they've done on defense through the coordinator change. And whether that's Shanahan's, you know, overall call, this is what I want to get done or not, or, you know, what Fred does a great job and and Green Law do a great job of doing. Yeah. I mean, the core is there and it's a it's a defense that very very familiar with. >> Does that make prep easier this week or do you have to guard against that a little bit? >> I think anytime you you have that that thought you have to guard against it, you have to go through the same preparation and through your same process the same way. And uh and also, you know, with there being new personnel, find new guys to to attack or or what's the soft spots in the defense that you can get to. >> So, not even a small party, you said I want to get a 49ers monkey off our back. >> I mean, I I want to beat them. Absolutely. And I'm no I'm not naive to what's happened or or my history against them. So, um but to put that on the rest of these guys or to put that on the locker room, I think that's that that's that's stupid. You know, this is about us going in and getting a win and us trying to, you know, win this game and get some momentum going and get backto-back wins for the first time this season and build off of that. And so, what a great opportunity to get to do it against against a 7-1 team. 7 to1, right? It just so happens that it be the Niners. So yeah, obviously I want to get a win and any everybody and anybody in this building does for sure a bunch of different reasons, but at the end of the day it's a seven to1 team coming in here and we've got an opportunity to beat them and we've got to go do everything we can to get that done. >> Halfway point of the season, Dak, how would you characterize this this year so far? >> Uh we've got to go get a win this week. Uh I'm not I'm not you know everything's in front of us and at the end of the day it's all you can ask for is to control your destiny and I think we still have the ability and and opportunity to do that and I know how big this week would be and so um that's my focus. >> Speak you mentioned Whiten. Speaking of have you seen play calling in coaching? Did you see that in his future when you were playing with him and are you surprised to see this? I guess you're not surprised to see the success in Norman. >> Yeah no not not surprised by anything he's done. um know just knowing the football runs in wit's veins and um that's who he is that that he would definitely be a coach and he'd be a good coach at it and um you know to see his climb happen I guess so fast in a sense right just from high school coaching and going and being the tight end coach already being the coordinator by the end of the year and understanding that's going to get him a coordinator job next year if not there in in Oklahoma or a head coaching job somewhere else. Um, he's a guy that that that I that I followed and that I I understand what he's trying to get done, whether it be the offense or whether it be the whole team and a guy that's going to do it the right way and just I know that from the time that I spent with him and the man that he is. >> There was a clip of him uh chewing out a receiver for running the wrong route. Did he ever chew you out, rookie year? Did you ever get any of those Jason Whitten chew outs? >> Uh, no. I don't think I got any of the chew outs. I got some maybe some silent treatments here and there in between [laughter] in between plays or something if I didn't throw it his way or you know he thought he was open. Uh but he didn't shoot me out. He he understands that you know I'm just as pissed you know at myself. >> Do you see him being an NFL coach one day? >> Absolutely. If that's what he wants to do. I mean I think it's a big difference when you're talking high school, college and NFL and what coaches are asked to do and what coaches are even trying to accomplish. But if that's in his goals absolutely. >> 49ers fans are known to travel pretty well. They've said they're going to try to take over a lot of the Do you guys prep for a silent count? I mean, I think there was an issue a little bit in the playoff game 22 like 40% of the crowd was red. You guys prepare for that or what's what's the mentality with that? >> Yeah, I mean I wouldn't be surprised for one. Um and then two, yeah, I mean we'll we'll get some work in just our silent. I mean obviously we've been on a road lot this season so it's not anything foreign or not anything that we've been been well at is is our silent cadence. And so we'll get a couple of reps at it. We'll prepare, you know, for anything and everything. And so I just challenge Cowboy fans to not let that happen to show up uh support and understand what they mean to this game. >> What do you got to roll? >> Thank you guys.

title: What's Really Going on With the Cowboys' Front Office?
text: Yes, no moves from the Cowboys today , and as I wrote in today's article, no team talks through their front office more often than them. We have been hearing statements from Jerry Jones and Stephen Jones for several weeks now. They've been asked about the trade deadline since the transfer of Joey Porter Jr. on September 30th. And it was clear that the closer the deadline, the fewer substantive negotiations were conducted. And now you see what deals have been made, and if we talk about today, there is nothing remarkable. Of course, the move of Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars was notable, as they traded for him with first- and second-round picks. Today, Kirk Cousins ​​returned to Minnesota, but top edge rushers like Khalil Mack, Josh Sweet, and Max Crosby didn't move anywhere. From what Jerry and Stephen had been saying over the past week and a half, it seemed that there had been no serious discussions. So I believe, as crazy as it may sound to many, that if there was a real opportunity, they would make another move.  I just don't think it materialized at the edge rusher position.  I don't know if they would have done this in other lines, but I'm sure many are glad they didn't change anything. Although there are those who are disappointed that they didn't trade George Pickens.  I'm not in their camp, but I know people who thought it was worth getting at least something for George from teams that needed a receiver.  But they look at it differently .  You know, they still believe they have a chance to make the playoffs.  I'm not sure the events of the Colts game give reason to think so.  Maybe next Sunday will change your mind, depending on how they play. So, the only change in the lineup, actually there are two of them. It looks like they will add Kendra Miller, a former Saints running back, to the practice squad and release Redi Stewart. So it's nothing serious, but they're doing it with Kendra Miller because Tyler Goodson has a knee injury that, apparently, was n't considered that serious during the game . And then, after getting the scan results, it became clear that it was serious, he was probably going to miss some time, a few weeks, and that's unfortunate because he was clearly playing well, and as we've discussed many times here, they need to have two running backs that they can rely on, they seemed to be getting on the right track and had that, and now this injury happens.  So the only other injury news I'll say is it looks like Joey Porter Jr. and George Pickens are going to be the same this week, they'll probably be limited in practice and it'll all be decided on Friday and depending on how they look then, they could potentially play against San Francisco.  Um, I don't see any chance the Cowboys will hold their own against the Niners without Joey Porter Jr. and George Pickens, and they might not even hold their own with them .  So it will be noticeable.  Well , yeah, that's probably all I have. What do you think about the fans, John, who are angry about what happened at the trade deadline, or what did n't happen at the trade deadline? What about the fans? What is the question? What does Joe John think about fans who are angry that John is not saying anything, not communicating anything during the trade deadline? I don't know if that's fans in the plural , but yes, no.  I think there was one fan on Twitter who was upset with me for not reporting anything when nothing happened.  So, I'll say this about the deadline: I wasn't expecting anything because I felt like they were betting on Joey Porter Jr. So I thought this must be their big exchange. I, however, thought, well, they could take some small step.  Could they somehow get stronger?  A 2028 sixth, seventh round pick, and hell, teams are trading 2029 picks.  Did you see this?   The 2029 peaks are now being exchanged.  So I'm wondering if a fifth-round pick in 2029 could get you a better backup running back, or a rotational edge rusher, or another linebacker.  I thought maybe this was something they could pay attention to.  They didn't do it .  Am I worrying for nothing?  No, it's been a long time since I felt this way when they don't make any moves.  I think it doesn't matter.  The years when I felt passionate about it were the years when I felt we could fight for the title , and you should try to get a reinforcement player because that's what other teams are doing.  I give credit to what the Jaguars are doing.  The Jaguars already had a pretty good defense.  They took and added new guys to it right after the season started, like, hey, we were good last year.  We are good this year.  We don't sit back and rest on our laurels, saying we're a good team.  We don't need to do anything else.   The Yagas, the Niners, the Seahawks, the Bears— they've taken massive steps to become better. So I respect their actions because they are real contenders for the title.  I wish we could do the same, but we are now at a different stage of this window, if there is one at all. So I'm not particularly worried about the lack of exchanges.  I would like to do at least one or two, but we have what we have.   Was there anyone who was traded in the last few days that caught your attention?  For the Cowboys. Look, a guy named Henley. For us, no.  Henley would be appropriate.  Yes , that's my opinion.  I remember covering his game, was he from Washington? Washington State. Yes, Washington State. State, yes. Aha.  I see him as a much better version of Shamar James.  A linebacker who plays forward is a good athlete.  But we need help on the defensive side.  I would ...have there been any exchanges of wing- backs?  This is exactly the position that I ... It seems there were none worth paying attention to. Of course.  Yeah, that's... The Eagles guy was almost traded. Arnold. Almost traded, but... I think the tweet saved the Bengals. I saw it, I saw it. He really saved them. Tell me about this tweet. It.  I saw that guy. I'll try to explain it as simply as possible, because it's still a bit confusing.  But apparently the Bengals were going to trade an Eagles player who was really just a random signing. But this exchange could cancel out next year's potential compensation peak due to certain rules. I don't know the exact rules.  So someone tweeted: hey, if they agree to this trade, someone who follows the Bengals, they could lose a compensatory pick in the third round in 2028 or whenever there is, in the 27th .  And then Adam Schefter or Ian Rapoport announced about 10 minutes later: this exchange will not happen yet, because they do not want to lose the compensation peak in 2027 or 2028.  But it's not official yet.  This is only on paper for now.  So I think that tweet could have saved them. Er, er, er, the compensatory pick was, I think, the third round for Trey Hendrickson. So, I think they just wanted this third peak more than Arnold. One hundred percent, he's not worth the third round. And he deserves a third. It was some weird rule that nullified third-round picks.   I don't know how, but apparently such a rule exists. I mean, can you imagine Twitter doing the job of management, Sky ? Hey, you know what?  I won't say anything more because I used to troll this until a few coaches this summer said, "No, we're watching you."  We take your ideas.  And Christian Parker tried to stop it. So you know what?  You guys figure it out .  They are watching.  They read Twitter. I'm telling you, uh, all these Pablo Torres doing these deep investigations, it's just...I don't know if you've seen that video. This is a whole different sport, but how was he able to track down the company Ballmer used for Kawhi Leonard.  Did you see that, John? Yes. Listen, there are people who will find out anything you try to do secretly. But yeah, to your point, Sky, yeah , I mean the Jags and even the Phillies have an understanding that we're playing badly, we're going to sell a lot of guys. And I think they might be preparing to get a new quarterback, and they'll have the resources to do that, especially in the draft. So, for me, to compete, to trade for big players, to miss out, to sign guys, to miss out, and then to trade those same players and get back first-, second-, and third-round picks...It's crazy how they do it. Thanks for watching this Cowboys Collective piece.  We're on air twice a week, so be sure to subscribe and don't miss a thing.

I mean, it seems like he's pressured the quarterback a lot even if you know the first seven games he just had one sack. >> You know, when you look at like I I I tell the guys, you just keep rushing. He's had a lot of hits, a lot of hurries, you know, and you look back and and George don't want to hear this, but he had a sack taken away in the in the in the Charger game, you know, they came back said if his knee if they had reviewed it, his knee was down. So things like that, you just got to keep rushing. Can't worry about just go on to the next play and keep chopping wood. And then when you keep chopping, the tree is going to fall down just like the sacks will come. >> Joe, collectly as a defensive line, what do you feel like is the strength of that group? I tell you what, the numbers, I mean, it's it's a deep group and and there's a lot of different when you look at Chris, you look at Peter inside, you look at what KT's brought us, some physicality in there, has a great motor. Uh the addition of Bryson in there, he's had some like in one of George's sacks, he had really good pocket collapse right at the quarterback. And then obviously the the the the edge guys, George, Race, Felix, and Ashton going inside and outside. both of those guys. It's just a real deep group and uh and and and love coaching them. >> Joe, how do you manage Chris Jones when he has a season where he starts off at a half sack trying to have in the flow of the season, then turns it on late, you know? How do you just manage him uh and his miss just getting out there and making sure he can be his best productive self on it? >> Well, you know, Chris grinds every day. He practices really hard. He he had a great training camp and sometimes it just happens. And I tell him, I said, you know, when Big Poppy hit one off the Green Monster, he didn't throw the bat. So sometimes you're getting in, you're just not quite finishing. Like the first rush I thought Chris had in the game, you know, or actually he had a really good red zone rush, but it was the one where at the end of the rush he strained and you might not see the stat. He had a deflected ball, but he he hit Gino's arm. We had they had an open receiver. It was in the red zone and then the ball hit the dirt. It was a great rush. And then the second one, he beat the guard inside. You just got to keep rushing. And then obviously he uh he dominated in the game >> when you guys know I mean obviously Peter's been gained up a little bit so that's not affected his workload but with our Mason has there been kind of a a concentrated effort to to try and manage his workload to make sure he's ready to make a contribution in the second half. >> You know he he gets the opportunities you know averaging probably close to 30 snaps a game on on the edge stuff. The hardest thing to do in this league for a rookie and I've been in this league 20 years is to rush the passion. it it's different than it is college. They set you different. You get trippers every down and you got to learn. It took George till the 11th game to get his first sack and then he had a sack every game and he was starting. So, I mean, I think our Mason has given us some really good edge rush. Uh he's been at he's been at or near the quarterback a lot. Uh and just got to keep working and keep grinding to finish. >> What uh what do you guys have to do up front with Bean Robinson? Um setting the edge all ton of things. >> Coach Spags leads every training camp with it. We first of all, you got to build a wall. You got to play with great knock back. Keep your shoulders square. You got to set the edge so he can't get the edge. And then when he cuts the ball back, we got to make sure someone's tracking the hip. But it's it's all hands on deck. It'll take all 11 to stop the run just like it takes all 11 to get after the quarterback. >> How does he compare with other backs you guys have faced? >> He's as good as a back as we faced in the league. He can stick his foot in the ground. He can jump cut. He can take it to the house. He's a home run threat every time he touches the ball. and he can run you over easy. >> Last one. Joe, >> I know you just mentioned the depth that you guys have, but how much of what you guys do and what you're trying to execute is still predicated around Chris there. >> Oh, yeah. It starts, you know what we always say, he's the piston that drives the engine and as he goes, we go and uh sometimes that might be not on the stat sheet, but he's got two or three people looking at him all the time and other things open up for other people. But, you know, I'm going to just say it like it is. Chris is the best defensive tackle I've ever been around and and he's a hall of fame player and when he goes we go. So, you coach all the guys, but how much of your attention is is trying to get him going when maybe he's not? >> I think I think you know, you always try to get each guy going and and and that whether that be the call, whether that be individually working, but I mean, just he knows how to get going and you this is his 11th year and uh I mean it's like it's like anything when you have the opportunity to win a one-on-one, you got to win it and uh but he's a selfarter. Chris gets going. >> Thank you. Appreciate you. Yeah. Email being down. >> Email that. You guys having trouble with your email? >> No. >> Uh, what are your uh first impressions of Josh Downs and what you've seen of your beard? I know it wasn't much of a practice yesterday. >> Yeah. First, it's it's great to have Josh here with us. um somebody I've always had a great deal of respect for as a player and then working with him yesterday, it it's really clear on how professional he is and you know great work ethic uh was embraced by our receiver group right away. Uh and it was easy to do that because of the type of person that he is. So I was very impressed with his first day of work here at the Chiefs. How do you see him fitting into the rotation of the lineup because played predominantly a lot of slot in his career. Is that where you kind of envision him being there for you? >> Yeah, I think his role is a work in progress. You know, just being here a day, he's trying to learn the playbook, uh, learn his teammates. So, I do think this is a work in progress. We're going to see, we know what he does well, and we're just going to try to fit those things within our system of how to help us, you know, win games on offense. So, I'm certainly looking forward to working with him. Uh, he's excited to get to the field today and every day is going to be some learning for him, just learning the playbook. >> You're obviously missing what Taekquin brought to you. Do you think I know he's not the same type of guy, he's much smaller, there's a lot of differences, but can he do some of that? Can he give you some of the ability to go downfield? >> Yeah, I think that, you know, like Taekquin obviously we know what he brought for us. Uh and and uh and I think that we've done we've replaced Taekquin through kind of by committee and I don't think that's going to be any different with Josh. You know, he's going to bring certain things that maybe Taekquin brought. Uh whether it is downfield or whether it's a short to intermediate route tree. I he does a lot of things really well and we're going to take advantage of the things and use the things he does well and that's our jobs as coaches to do that. >> What are the coaching points for Xavier as he continues to progress this season? the coaching points that Xavier are no different than the other guys were asking. It's like truly just embrace what we're asking him to do, get better every day, which he's done. I mean, Xavier is a very hard worker. Um, he is very coachable and it's it's really neat to see the interaction with our receiver group. They get along very well. So, you know, like adding a guy like Josh DS is another step in the in the process for Xavier where he can really lean on another player in this league and learn from him as well as his coaches. So, Xavier's done a good job of just doing the things we've asked him to do and working really hard to do those. >> About halfway through this first year here with Cyrus, uh, have you seen him making the progress you'd like to see, understanding the offense and doing those things at this point? >> Yeah, Cyrus has made improvements. He really has. um we're excited about. He had a great uh two weeks of practice for us. Our expectations is this week he'll have the same type of preparation. He has uh really improved his meeting room just his overall uh learning the playbook and then taken it to the field. That's really what I've seen the last couple weeks is he's been able to take some of the details uh that we've stressed in the meeting room and take that to the field. And that's really been evident to us as a coaching staff the last couple weeks. So, you know, the arrows up for Sai. He keeps on improving. I think it's always challenging for a young player at any position. U you know, to that first year in the league to learn all the nuances and the thing that goes into playing in each position regardless if it's a receiver or not. So, uh he is improved and he will continue to improve and he's worked very hard to do so. >> This is your first year here and I know a lot of folks around here are not surprised when Patrick does certain things, whatever. when you watched him get hit and come off the field and be in pain, what was your first thought? And or were you shocked at all that three or four minutes later he was back out there throwing the ball? What just since this is your first kind of year being around him? >> Being around him, not shocked at all that he was right back out there. This is a fierce competitor. I mean, he's unbelievable. His toughness uh is incredible. I mean, to have a leader like he is on our football team, I can't say enough great things about what that brings. And it's contagious. you know, when our players see him go back out there when things not might not be perfect for him, uh, it's contagious and our guys follow and I am, you know, so appreciative to be on a football team with Patrick Mahomes. >> Last two back. >> Yeah, collectively for you, what do you need to see from this wide receiver group over the next eight games? >> I think consistency. That's, you know, what we're asking all of our positions right now is just let's work for consistency. There's certainly been moments where we've done it the right way and there's been moments we've fallen short of that. So, it's really bringing the consistency across the board at each position. Uh, you know, and and just we're asking the guys to improve every day. So, we're going out there today and our goal is to improve and get better. And if we do that, then we'll work towards the level of consistency that we're talking about trying to get to. And then when you acquire a guy like DS mid-season, how do you kind of like break down the playbook and and get it to a place where he he can learn and go out there and play fast and be productive? >> Yeah, I mean it's always whenever you have a player that's learning a different language, it's a process. The thing that uh is great about Josh DS is how intelligent he is and his work ethic is is so good. Those two things allow you to teach this stuff to him uh in a way in which you hope he can learn it and take some of the things to the field and really help our offense. Heat. Heat. Everything. Heat. Hey, Heat. Na. N. Go ahead, guys. Chris, >> I know you don't care about stats, but what it feel like to get a couple sacks. What's the week been been like in the D line room with the game you guys had and what you can maybe build from that? >> Something we can build off of. Um, got good momentum going into Atlanta. you know, we was able to get after the quarterback with a fourman rush and um it's a lot of momentum we can build off of that. >> What kind of juice even in the defensive side does an addition like Josh Downs bring to the the entire team? >> Um listen, he's sweet, man. He's sweet feet. I know when we played him, um you know, we doubled him a lot. The game plan was around him and Jonathan Taylor, of course. So to have him on our side right now, it's a it's a sweet thing. I think he we gonna be able to utilize him in a deep ball, get him open and open up for everyone else on the offense. So, >> good. >> What would you say was was the key to defensive approach to be on running a game? >> You know, and trying to um play fundamentally sound uh reset the line of scrimmage with the Dline. Um you know, um he's a very patient runner. um inside, outside, he can break a big one anytime he his hands are on the ball. So, you know, for us it's about playing fundamentally football, playing discipline. >> Chris, how much uh do you take it upon yourself to get the pass rush going when when it wasn't >> just a fourman rush? We stay in a four-man rush, we can get it going. Chris, you guys have uh typically generally been really good against elite running backs, managing them, you know, to an extent enough to win the game. I guess what do you think has been the underlying threat of being so good against these backs who d it seems like they do more damage against other teams every week? >> You know, we got really great coaches, great assistant coaches who um spent put us in the right position to execute. um do a lot of film study and and and a lot of watching of the tendencies of uh a team and what they do best and we try to counter react to that. >> Uh Omar's back kind of practicing to wrap himself up. What uh what do you see from him and what could he maybe add for you guys in a couple weeks? >> Other guy got to help us get up to the quarterback. I think you know the skill set that Omar brings, you know, he's uh a really really good pass rusher. we haven't had him enough to kind of utilize his skill set. So to have him back, to have him in rotation can add depth to the D line. >> Thank you everybody. Thank you.

He has a good feel for kind of playing in the NFL and their scheme is similar to our scheme. Obviously verbage and everything like that, but we can utilize him in his his role in his spots. Um but at the end of the day when you get guys in the building and they're picking up stuff like we had to walk through earlier and he's picking up stuff quickly um then you can kind of give him more and more and so uh he's definitely a smart football player and I think it won't be um a long time until he's really getting utilized in the offense. >> What stands out about the Falcons' defense and what you need to be aware of, you know, on a short week play? >> Yeah, I mean, they fly around. They fly around. They fly to the football. They're able to get turnovers and sacks and stuff like that. And and they have I mean, their offense, they have talented players there, and they've they've beat some really really good football teams this year. And so it's a really talented football team. They they they fly. They play hard. And so it'll take us executing at a high level in order to go out there and have success. And so it'll be a great environment going down there playing. And it'll be a great challenge for us. >> After a couple other quick things about the elbow, I know you mentioned the other day that just being able to pick up the ball made you feel reassured, but it looked like it was pretty tough that first ball or two you threw on the sideline. Do you remember >> Yeah, yeah. I mean, just I got a lot of swelling pretty quickly, and I think just that swelling, it was I was throwing the ball. I wasn't feeling exactly how I usually feel when I throw it. But then as we were working on that second half, she was really getting the swelling out of my arm, which made it more feel more comfortable to throw the football. And then we were able to kind of how we we handled the game in the second half, we were able to run the ball really well, so I didn't necessarily have to push it down the field. And so we're in a better spot now than we were then. And so we'll continue to get better there. >> And just your feeling after getting the MRI, I mean, sound like you were pretty optimistic, but were you pretty relieved to know? >> Yeah yeah, for sure. Cuz I mean, anytime you get in there, I mean, you never know what it's going to show on the on the machine after. And so you can feel as optimistic as as you do, but then you get in there and something something happens. And so obviously after talking to the doctors and stuff like that, I I feel like I'm in a great spot. Now it's just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I'll I'll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible. >> Last one, Steve. >> On top of the elbow, nobody always talks about the work that you guys do in the off season to kind of prepare for situations like that. How much has that helped you uh in your career? >> Yeah, I mean, it it's it's helped a ton. And you can see the see it, you know. You can see from the stuff that I do that it whenever I get put in some bad positions that sometimes I'm able to have some resistance to some injuries. I mean, you can't stop everything, obviously. Um, but uh all that work does pay off in the end. And if I didn't see it, I wouldn't be doing it because it sucks to do. So uh I'll keep doing it. >> When it comes to the plan, do you you guys go over things or is it something that you want to do or how does that work? >> No, it changes every year. We go over like different positions from tape that I was in um and and the years previous and then we try to do stuff to attack that stuff. Um and so there's there's a plan of why we're doing stuff, you know. We want to make sure that I'm I'm obviously able to do things and and play at the best, but like be able to prevent injury so I can be on the field as much as possible. >> Uh for you for you, you know, with Josh Dallas coming in, how do you feel going to be able to help out with this offense and just conversations with him? How that's mentioned with the wide receiver group? >> Um I think he's going to be a great weapon to be able to add to the weapons that we already have. He's a great player. You can watch his film and and see that for yourself. I think we're going to find you know coach Reid, EB they're going to find the best ways to make sure he contributes to the offense as best as he can. >> What advice can you give him as far as like teaching him the offense? I know it'd be a group of you guys trying to help him out. Patrick said their offense has some similarities. So did you see that in the walkthroughs that it's he's kind of picking things up a little bit quicker? >> I mean Patrick probably sees that a lot more than me. We just kind of take each week We We prepare each week you know play at their place. So it's not necessarily seeing their how their offense is but I'm pretty sure you know since he's a great player it won't be hard for him to adapt and to learn the offense under coach Reid. >> Is it related to that? What do you think what's the hardest thing you expect for him to have to deal with to get get ready fast? >> Uh personally I probably would say the personnels. Uh just take some time to understand personnels and figure out when specific words are said that you're in a certain position on the field. >> And is it hard to get used to how what to knowing what Patrick wants too? Just that in itself? Is that going to be a learning curve for him? >> No not necessarily. It's not really hard to understand what Pat's thinking on the field. Once you love the game of football and you're you know doing everything you can to get open you know Pat's going to do everything he can to get you the ball. So as long as you separate and make some room to make sure he can make the throw which he will. So I mean as long as he does that it'll be easy for him to you know prepare for the plays. >> The lens of attention that he's going to get as he gets into the offense, what could that potentially do for you and or the and maybe Kelsey? >> Uh it's going to do a lot. It's going to do a lot for the whole offense. He's going to be down the field, middle of the field, shallow routes, whatever wherever he has to you know run his play. It's even going to open up the run game just because we a lot more weapons to for Pat to throw the ball. So, it's going [clears throat] to be, you know, just a lot more confidence in the receiver room as well. >> You're halfway through the season, Rashod. Where do you feel like you stand right now is far as the season has played out? >> Um, I mean, I don't really know exactly where I stand. Uh, I know I'm in the wide receiver room full of great wide receivers and we just focus on going to win each game. >> Has the first half, you know, played out the way you expected or you know, met or exceeded expectations or is it >> Uh, I've had a lot of times where I wasn't playing, so I don't really have expectations for um anything further than preparing for each week. I mean, I'm touching the ball, we're winning games, and I feel like that's all that matters. >> What would it be >> anything Go ahead. >> Uh, just thoughts about the Falcons defense. The record's not great, but they did beat the 49ers down there. What what do they look like on tape to you guys? >> They look pretty good. They have a good secondary. Um, they're going to be [clears throat] home. They're going to be excited to play. Uh, a lot of teams are usually excited to play the Chiefs and we just got to make sure we have the same excitement and same preparation uh throughout the week of practice. >> Last couple go by and then Matt. >> Rashod, anything specific you guys do with the group of receivers to bring them in that whether it's a, you know, new group chat or whatever? I mean, have you already taken measures to do that? >> Um, I mean, I trained [clears throat] with Josh in the offseason as well as coming out of uh college uh in Florida. So, I mean, I have a a relationship prior. And um I mean, not necessarily I mean, we're in the same area in the locker room. So, you know, we're in there joking around. We're in the uh in the meeting room joking around, talking to each other in the uh in as far as like learning the plays or how he needs to open up the playbook on the on the iPad and stuff like that. So, just communicating with each other and just having fun playing the game. >> And were you in touch with him right away when you saw the trade yesterday? And if so, what did you what did you try to get across? >> Uh, I didn't really say much. I was in touch with him uh when I seen the first rumor, just seeing what was going on, what was going through his head. So, I mean, I am happy that he's here. Uh, I talked to him last night, and I just sent eye emojis, and he was like, you know, you hear his time, so he's ready to go just like we are. >> So you guys knew each other beforehand. You trained together. With you being a veteran at this system, how beneficial is that for him, do you think? >> I think it's really beneficial. Um just [clears throat] to know that he already had a a brother in the locker room. Um and he's going to have a lot more brothers as as far as the, you know, preparing even just for today in practice. He's going to be out there with us and, you know, just getting a feel for how we prepare and how we just still have fun even though we're getting work done. >> Thanks for cheating. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Go ahead. >> Well, I make the reports out that you reworked your deal. Obviously probably helped out to get Josh in here and everything. That process, how's that work? How how involved are you in it? >> Uh yeah, my agent called me a couple days uh prior. Um obviously we're trying to make a move, and they just needed a little bit more space. So um like I said, like we can bring in good players and um help our team win football games. I'm all for it, but uh that's pretty much all it was. A of days of communication, just giving me a heads up that this might happen or this opportunity could happen, and I mean obviously we could bring good guys in the building. Uh I'm all for it, so. >> Is that something that was discussed? I know they talked about the past that Pat's deal was set up and such that they knew that might be something that have to do was that when you originally signed that deal, was that something that they talked to you about that hey on down the road we might have one of these opportunities? >> Uh no, it's kind of just kind of kind of recent honestly. Uh they're trying to figure out how they can make this roster a little bit better, so um it was kind of just last couple of days honestly. >> Nick, this is kind of obvious, but how how how much do you think that reflects your own um desire to win? >> Yeah, obviously everybody in this building, not just me, wants to win football games. I've been here for a long time and have liked success doing that, so um I talked to the people that are our captains, our leaders, and our coaches, and obviously like Pat taking um um his deal and stuff like that to help to help the team win, so I think everybody in this building's kind of buying into that. >> Is there >> You played you played those guys two and obviously Josh kind of beat you guys. Just what's it like preparing for him ahead of the game and obviously competing against him? >> Yeah, we go into that game understanding the type of player he is and what he can do versus man coverage and and work his way in the slot and in zone, so um obviously I think there's some things that uh he can bring to bring to this team as why why we brought him in, but um he does a lot of work in the slot and I thought he was pretty shifty, able to run out the catch, I get the ball fast out in space, um runs a different uh different routes and kind of breaks leverage and stuff like that, so I think it'd be good for our offense. >> Nick, with the Falcons, you know guys always seem to face some great running backs. Last time you ran up against >> Mhm. >> just what is the challenge of facing Bijan and how he maneuvers that offense around them? >> Yeah. Uh he's electricity in a bottle is what I say. Uh able to change direction. Uh I get a feel uh cutbacks. We see it all the time. Everybody's at the point of attack because he can cut it back and put pressure on the backside corner on on the outside zone to the opposite side, so uh he's electricity in a bottle like I said and uh I'm going to take all hands on deck. >> Nick, that last game you guys had down there, is that a good reminder of how how thin the edge is between winning a game and not and served you guys well to be thinking of that? >> Yeah, obviously. Um we played down there like you said it was a a fourth down play to win the game. Uh it was before overtime, maybe before going into overtime, one of those two. Um but I kind of take just the margin of error uh the margin of error in this league is very little and you can kind of see it week to week how many one-score games and teams winning from uh three points or less and then teams coming back from 10 or 10 points down and winning games uh week to week. So all those things, man, you can kind of definitely see that throughout the weeks. >> Nick, I just have one more question about the contract. From a real life standpoint, there isn't something bad with reading it receiving this immediate check of I mean that's not that doesn't take too much convincing I I'd imagine. >> No, uh definitely wasn't too much convincing. Uh but yeah, like you said, man, I'm just trying to make this roster a little better, man, and um obviously I'll take a little bit of advancement if I can. So >> On Bijan, what is the most difficult thing about him? >> Uh tackling space. They do a good job of running down for the routes and giving him check downs um creating space. Uh but also just um screens. They do a good job rocket screens, running back screens, uh throwing the ball on the flats and then they also outside zone teams give them a chance to I say like a punt return kind of read blocks and kind of set up the blocks and explode through the middle of the line of scrimmage. So uh I think that's kind of the most difficult thing. He does a good job of creating space with his body movements, but also they do a good job of doing that as well. >> Nick, what does it take to develop a peanut punch and execute it that well the way you did last week and you think that's the best one you had in your career? >> Yeah, I've been searching for for forcing a forced fumble for a couple of years now. It's been like two or three years. Uh I was kind of watching Jeff's tape uh from when he had versus the Raiders and like his elbow's a little bit higher than mine's been in the past and that's kind of one of the things I was trying to do and I was able to get my elbow above my wrist and create a downward angle um kind of got the ball out. So that's kind of one of the things I was working on throughout the week and kind of played a difference for me. >> You guys have gotten more of those this year. It didn't seem like you you guys as a unit did a lot of punching at the ball before. Is that a concerted thing this year to kind of do that more often? >> Yeah, in training camp I kind of mentioned on it a little bit but create more turnovers, sack fumbles, and forced fumbles. Uh we were good in my first couple years in the league here and then we were down on the bottom of the league the last two years. So we went to training camp definitely with a focus point uh creating turnovers. We did every single day uh before practice before we got started. So we just kind of get the ball on the ground as much as possible. >> Nick, you said you were kind of in practice. I mean you were kind of you know we've seen times in camp where maybe some of the offensive guys don't like it. >> When you guys are working on that. In season, you talk about you just you maybe have some drills you do or even when you guys are out there and you know, you you're live fire on some of your offensive guys. >> Yeah. Obviously, you got to do live fire of them sometimes, man. Like you said, our offense not fumbling the ball that much this season. I'm knocking wood on that, but we're forcing fumbles. So it pays dividends for us, man. They protect the ball, we come get it out. But yeah, in practice we can kind of do live reps as much as possible. >> Thanks, Zach. >> Yep. Thank you. >> Thank you. >> Take us through what the last couple of days have been like for you. Obviously, getting traded here, how you found out, kind of all the details of >> Yeah, I mean, Sunday took a took a tough loss. Wasn't wasn't my best out there. But it was you know, a lot of stuff going on through that. And then Monday, meetings. Regular Monday didn't really have much going on. And then Tuesday, it was like 3:30, 3:45 and I get a text and they were like, hey, come come see me at the facility. And I was like, oh, I was surprised. And had to had to move quick and get things going right away. And I was on a plane about 3 hours later and now I'm here. So >> What's the feeling of going from a you know, two win team, obviously wasn't going to make the playoffs, to being in the mix for the top of the AFC? >> No, I I I I got so much respect for the Colts. Two and six or not, I mean, they they drafted me, they showed love to me. I enjoyed my time there. So you know, it's great to join a team like this with so much history and so much winning in in their past and even now. So I'm excited to be able to be a part of a group like this and contribute where I can. >> Zach, what does How should to you to hear from Patrick kind of right away and and to stay in touch with Rashy along the way. Did those things or you kind of help you get acclimated a little? >> Yeah, it's good when you know guys um welcome you and accept you, so I feel like um at this point it's it's my my turn to like earn their respect on the field and earn their respect as a teammate and um I'm going to do what I can to do that. >> And what do you expect it to be like just to sort of get started with Patrick and learn how to be on the same page with each other? How how are you going to go about that I guess? >> Yeah, build that relationship with them and then you know um on the field when he throws me the ball just catch it and and keep making plays when um he throws it to me and um you know just just do anything I can to learn the offense as fast as possible. I don't want to I don't want to be a guy that's you know asking everybody what the play is, what the formation is. I feel like that's when you kind of get left behind, so um I want I want to do everything I can to learn as fast as possible. >> [clears throat] >> Yeah, I mean that was actually my my genuine emotion. It wasn't anything like to throw salt on anybody. I just was I was excited for the opportunity and it was it was simple as that and then um those were literally my emotions. I kind of just uh you know I kind of screamed when I saw saw the text, but um you know it it uh some people don't like that uh but you know I apologize to those who don't, but that was that was my reaction. >> Was Kansas City always a place that you wanted to go? >> Um you know I I feel like if they were pursuing me um you know you want to go where you're wanted and they were pursuing me, so um I'm definitely excited to join a team that thinks I have value. >> Rashy, you said nothing but respect for the Chiefs and there are reports that there were other teams that were interested that maybe you directed them that this is where you wanted to go. Can you confirm that they gave you kind of an option on on where you want to go and you pick Kansas City? >> Um I know they made uh a decision based off um the betterment of their organization and um I respect them for sending me to an organization like this. Um those are great people over there and um I feel like they they did right by me and you know um this is the choice they made. >> Josh, what number are you going to select? >> 12. I'm going to wear 12. >> And why 12? >> Um no specific reason, but you know the equipment manager was like, hey, you wore one and then you wore two. So now you can, you know, put them together. So I'll go with that. >> A little last scheduling quirk. You're not going to get a bye week? >> Nah, no bye week. No bye week, man. It's all right, though. Get to play an extra game, man. We love football. >> Um and this is a little homecoming. Your first game's going to be down in Atlanta. You're from down there. Have you already gotten a a million ticket request things? How's that going to work? >> So it's it's a little like we got to figure it out. I know my parents don't want me to worry about that and all and um it's it's kind of like a a surprise that I'm here now. So some people like weren't even thinking about that and now they might be like, oh, like he's going to be here this weekend. So um I'll try to figure that that out over the next few days and go from there. >> Patrick mentioned that there were some similarities [clears throat and cough] in the playbook with the Colts and what you have here. Just your initial look at the playbook and just say how makes it show you how quickly you can get to adjusted to this with maybe the similarities and what's with the Colts. >> I mean, you just got to uh learn the concepts, honestly. I feel like a lot of concepts are going to be similar. Um it comes down to learning the the vocab and the positions and um you know, don't want to go too far into it, but I feel like that's the main thing. >> Josh, what do you want to >> Rashee said that mentioned you guys train in the off season together instead. What's kind of your relationship with him? And are there any other guys on the team that you've worked with in the past? >> Yeah, I've known Rashee. Um we did pre-draft together and uh we we we developed a pretty good relationship. That's my dog. Um yeah, he's pretty cool and um we we've been cool throughout all these years and and I'm excited to play with a guy like that. He's really good. Um I went to school with Diego Pounds and uh Josh Downs at uh North Carolina. And um off the top of my head, that's where I know. I mean, obviously I know like of Xavier Worthy like plays receiver and he was at Texas when I was at UNC. He was doing well. So um it's cool to play with guys like that. >> Josh, what do you want to bring to the offense and also as a teammate? >> Um I mean, I want to just help any way I can. Um pretty much that's the main thing, help whenever I can, whenever they call my number. And as a teammate, just be there for the guys, support them, and uh you you congratulate my teammates and make a play for them as well. >> You're shooting to be a free agent when the season ends. Just how much of this is about demonstrating what you can be as a receiver in a new sort of setting, and how much of this is maybe a potential opportunity for you to maybe stick around past the season? >> Could be both, but you know, honestly, just want to be where my feet are right now. And today I'm here in Kansas City. I got to have a good practice today, get ready for the Falcons. And just got to focus on that. That's the main thing. I don't want to look ahead and start making scenarios in my head or anything like that. >> Josh, you mentioned helping in any way you can. Obviously, you've returned punts in your career. Do you think do you see that happening here or >> Uh yeah, we'll see. I don't I don't know what they have planned and all that, but we'll see what happens with that. >> Josh, Patrick talked about after you learned that you were getting you were coming here that he messaged you about the city more than just about football. What did he talk about the city? >> You know, I've so I've we're Pat Patrick Mahomes is like a close friend that I've worked with years ago. So me and him me and him are pretty close as well. So they're just, you know, breaking me in, kind of telling me what are some good areas to stay in. And I'm going to start looking into that and you know, possibly getting some good food spots. You know, I like to I like yeah, I like to I like to eat. So I'm a little skinny, but I do like to eat. I do like to eat. >> Hey Josh, um just related to Patrick, obviously you you followed him and I think known him in some ways, but what's just your excitement or anticipation of playing with him? >> Yeah, man, great quarterback. I mean, who wouldn't love playing with a with a quarterback of his you know, caliber? Three championships. You can't really put it in words. Like as a receiver, you you love playing with a quarterback like that. So been following Mahomes for years and you know, like when when people are in college, like that's the everybody's like, oh, I want to go play with Mahomes. So it's kind of it's kind of like it's a blessing. I I'll say that. It's it's truly a blessing. >> what has stood out to you about him when you've watched him? I mean, there's I'm sure many things, but what what is it about him that makes you feel that way? >> Yeah, I mean, timing, accuracy, um great arm, and you know, he makes he makes plays in the pocket, but out of the pocket as well. So I feel like, you know, being having that scramble aspect is is really big and he makes a lot of plays out of that. And then um just being a leader. From what I've seen just today, he's he's the he's the head of the head of the snake and I feel like that's very important. >> Not just in how he's approached you or just that >> Just the team. Just just how he's how he's been interacting today from what I've seen. >> Couple more. >> So, you know, you played here a few times or a couple times. And I don't think most people realize when you guys come here you don't do anything. You just kind of come in and go to the stadium. What what are your memories of playing in front of this crowd and what it'll be like in a couple weeks when you get to play in front of them with the chanting going on? >> Nah, it's a very very loud crowd. Um they're into it. I remember we we came here week two and the tailgate was just crazy before the game and I was just like dang, I'm like this look like a like like SEC kind of like I I I never seen that um out of a NFL stadium for real. So that was that was really cool to me and then um you know, the the the chant I that that's always cool to hear and I'm excited to get out there and feel the energy. >> A lot of guys talk about playing for Coach Reed and that they would run through a wall for him. What have you learned in your your early thoughts with him? >> Yeah, nah, everybody seems to seems to like Coach Reed and I'm I'm excited to build a relationship with him and um everybody says he's a great mastermind of offense. So I'm I'm excited to to get involved with that and you know, um learn from him and and go from there. >> Thanks, Josh. Thank you. >> Thank y'all. >> Appreciate it.

title: Andrew Janocko and Rob Leonard Presser - 11.12.26
text: guys want to talk about today. All right, here we go. >> With Fernando's running ability, how much does that help maybe having to make the defenses account for it, which they didn't have to with Kirk to help open up the running game? >> I think every uh every player, no matter the position, brings a difference different and unique skill set whenever they step into the starting role. So, um, Fernando's no different and we're just we're looking for him to go out and play the position, um, and, you know, and put us in a position to to help the offense and just be part of part of that 111th and and how we attack each play. >> I appreciate that, but the question was how much does his running ability possibly help the other running backs? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, we're going to ask him to to play the position and and there are times when your legs come into play. That's something that that we'll ask him to do. But that's something we ask every quarterback to do. And if his skill set his skill set gives more of an advantage for that, then that's something that that we, you know, that that you might see show up. But, you know, playing the position of quarterback is about, you know, putting the offense to be successful. And however, however he can do that, you know, that's what we really want him to do. >> You've been working with him since rookie mini camp. What's something you can ask him to do within this offense today that maybe he couldn't do when he first got here? I think just articulate everything um the way he the way he sees it, the way he feels it, and then do it in a manner that can explain to everybody. Um so, you know, just from a mental standpoint, being able to paint the picture in his mind and paint the picture to everybody else within the offense. >> Is there a moment that stands out to you since Tuesday where it's been like, okay, he's ready for this? >> I think I think ready for this is a collection of preparation. So, I don't think there's an aha moment. I don't think there's ever an aha moment. We're a we um you know, we're a collective of of preparation and that's that's what we want to see each other as an offense and really, you know, not him, our offense. It's not really about him being ready, it's about our offense being ready to play, our offense being ready to go and then helping this organization be successful. >> Uh coach Aldwin talked to us a couple weeks ago about how you would notice Fernando being out on the indoor practice field late at night going over the game script. I was wondering and articulating the play calls and everything. Anything else? How much did that you think that helped him be up to speed to get to this moment? >> I think anything you can do to prepare yourself any any extra edge you can edge you can get you know that's that's what we're looking for. So what so however a person learns and however a person puts themsself in position to be successful what what player what position group how they go about doing that that's um you know it's just trying to trying to chase an advantage. Yesterday, some of the players were saying that Fernando was the same competitor um even before and then how after a couple days of practice, do you still see that he's just the same person or does something change mentally wise knowing that he is preparing for a starting role? >> I think you know whether it be quarterback, offense, right guard, um whether it be receiver, whether it be running back, you know, we ask every person to come in there with and and be the ultimate competitor. And so with him, it's no different than what we ask Tyler to do um or what we ask Jaylen to do or any any of our players. You know, we ask them to come out and compete on every single rep. Um every single meeting is a competition to come out and do that. So, you know, it's it's you know, he's one of the 11 that we're asking to do that. >> Andrew, when you look at Mike McDonald, historically against rookie quarterbacks, the blitzes and the pressures go up, um not surprisingly. So, how do you replicate that in practice for a quarterback that's getting ready to see it for the first time uh in an NFL game? >> Um, you know, obviously, you know, knowing coach and knowing, you know, how well that defense has coached and how well they perform week in and week out, we know that that's going to be a heck of a challenge for us. So, we're trying to put him in position as much as a game like whether it be whether it be this defense or the next defense or the next defense. You know, there's always things that you're looking for on tape to try to to try to put yourself in the game, make as many game-like reps as possible, but we understand that this is a very well coached team. It's a very well-run organization. They're world class for a reason. So, we have to be on our best and, you know, every position has to go out and be able to execute at a high level. We try to replicate everything in practice, but at the end of the day, it's about going out, trusting your training, and sticking to your techniques. >> Would always talk about the importance of playing instinctively. Have you seen that rub off on Fernando playing less out of his head and trusting himself at this point? >> Yeah, I think every player, especially as they grow. Um, again, and I know I sound like a broken record, but Fernando, but but all of our players, you know, they we ask them to trust their training, trust their assignment, and then go out and make a play and do their job. So, and then that's when the best players, they do play extin instinctually. So they go out, they rely on that and they um you know and that's part of being successful as a player in this league is being Extinction League cuz if you just run lines on a paper um you know that'll you know that'll take you so far. But it's it's about playing the game and then and then feeling a game. It all comes with experience and it all comes with um you know just creating that that general comfort and feel as you get into a game. >> From the beginning of training camp to now, you know, is there one particular thing that you've noticed that Fernando has improved at the most as a player? text: Boon was limited today and I'll take any of your questions. >> How'd it go for Fernando today with his first practice in the start? >> Went well. Yeah, you know, uh it's just being being upfront and honest with the team and that's that's what I would that's what I would want if I was a player. Just tell me the truth. How late uh Kirk is staying? How I'm working with receivers in between periods? Uh what do I what I do postpractice? um what questions I I need to be asking protection-wise. They've as a family done so much for me. And for you, I mean obviously that thrusts you into a lifelong dream as as you mentioned. How do you process that just the the emotions of it and now the responsibility of it? >> I believe in the principles in the quarterback room that coach Janokco, coach Kubak, and coach Sullivan always preface is you're always one play away. How did that approach help prepare you to take over this offense? that compete with approach I think was a fundamental part of our relationship and the entire quarterback's rooms uh relationship al together and it the quarterback room that we have and that we had with Kirk was such a special moment and it was uh it was like a a a nice family away from home and so we're all getting each other better and I mean honestly it was more like Kirk and Aiden giving me tips and tricks so I'm I'm forever We're thankful >> city Clint City is going to not >> limit you anyway.
