He's always told, you know, everybody on the team and he's been a great he was a great leader and captain on the team and really brought us together and had a lot of togetherness. So that's something that I I look to exemplify and uh take from his lessons. been a lot of anticipation for you for this moment throughout your career. Just how ready are you physically, mentally, you know, leading up into this game today, uh week 10? >> Yeah, like I said, this is a new experience. It's great. It's against a fantastic opponent. However, I've an unex I have so much trust in the coaching staff in the front office and my teammates and the leaders of the team to go out there and best support everybody's 111 so we could do our job with the best ability in your progression up to this point. I think that there's so many great minds in this building, in this facility. I've been I think the element that the the quarterback room has early on emphasized is always listening and taking in some information whether it's from coach Kubak, Coach Denco, Coach Sullivan, or any of the other quarterbacks or offensive linemen or tight ends or running backs or receivers. And so I think being receptive and listening has helped me progress. However, like I said, there's still a long way to go. >> Was there a lasting memory that you're going to have of Kirk as your teammate? >> Well, I mean, he's not I mean, he's not gone like he's gone from the RA. He's not gone forever. So, I mean, I still hope to like like we said, we hope to connect in the offseason and you know, he I can reach out for anything. So, I'm sure I'll talk to him, you know, probably after this game or, you know, after the season or or or something. But I mean just how how great of a teammate he he was and everyone seeing the Netflix show and you know you hear things from media but Dax be in with him and spend long hours just in the quarterback room with him was extremely special. I'm going to miss him and I really appreciate and I'm deeply am deeply thankful for everything that the Cousins family has offered to me. >> That locker room talks highly of you privately when the cameras aren't on and just how you've earned their respect. No ego and I know it's a winning game. you got to win in this league, but what does it mean to you the way your teammates have embraced you and accepted you and genuinely believe in you? >> Yeah, I think it was a great lesson that I learned early on is to try to be yourself and we have so many great teammates in there and I've I mean, I can't thank all of them enough for how they've brought me in, supported me, and I just those are my brothers, and I'm so excited to go to war with my brothers and be able to fight every single play and do everything I possibly can to to help us all succeed. The In-N-Out tradition. >> What's that? >> Will we continue the In-N-Out tradition after >> In-N-Out tradition? That's a It's a team It's a team decision. Uh, I mean, that that that could be a good idea. >> You think you'll pick up the tab like Kirk did? >> Oh, for sure. If we do, yes, I will. Yes, I will. Yes, I will. >> Your family has always been important to you. Did you give yourself a couple minutes to to, you know, share this with them? And what was that like? >> Well, it came out on the news before I got to even talk to them. So, uh, they they called me and was like, you know, it's been it's what you've been doing your whole life and what you've been preparing for and it came at a little bit of a, you know, unexpected time, but still a fantastic opportunity and can't thank them enough for their support. >> You talk about the blessing and the curse of playing against an opponent like, you know, the Seattle Seahawks in your first start and how much of the film have you dig into so far yet? Yeah, the coaching staff and I and personnel staff, we've watched I would say I've watched a good amount of film so far in my routine, especially a routine that I've modeled whether it's coach Janokco, coach Sullivan, coach Kubak, ones that they've recommended and also taking from Kirk and Kirks and Aiden's past processes. And so we've been doing the same process every week. So continue on keeping the same thing and keeping the main thing, the main thing which is the process. And they're a very impressive team and the lead I mean they're one of the best defenses in the league. So, it's going to be a great challenge and I'm excited to do my 111th out there. >> Big game for Indiana this weekend. What would you describe co coach signetti's three big characteristics that have been able to change this program to be in the position they are right now? >> Yeah, coach Signetti always says fast, physical, and relentless. So, best luck to the Hooers. I have confidence in the Hooers and uh yeah, >> go Bloomington. Go Hoosiers. So, yeah. And also thanks guys. >> Thank you guys. God bless. He's OC guy. Yeah.

title: Aaron Donald & Rams Coordinators On Maximizing Roster Depth, Week 10 Against the Cardinals & More
text: How much fun is it to watch Aaron and Miles outside together from your perspective? >> It's a lot of fun. And uh, you know, specifically Aaron, seeing him come back, the joy that he has, seeing him celebrate others, seeing him last week celebrate the picks, you know, and all that type of stuff, and seeing him celebrate Miles Sack, and I was just so happy for Miles, um, you know, going through, talking through the adversity that he'd been through. He'd never missed that much extended period of time, and you know, going out and feeling like the player that he that he truly is, and obviously why we brought him here. So, you know, really happy for those two. And you know, the game's about, you know, playing hard and having fun, and uh, that's what it's all about. >> When you kind of envision what that might look like, is it is it close now or >> Yeah, I mean, we're you know, we're always building. We're always seeing we're going week to week and doing whatever we can to, you know, get a win that week. This league is so hard, um, just to win a game. It's so hard to stop people. These coaches are so good. The opposing teams are so good, and uh, obviously great players is the number one thing, and uh, you know, we're lucky to have those two. >> With the injuries on offense and as well as your defense is playing, I don't know, pressure or is that a heightened responsibility to continue the defensive success? >> Uh, I wouldn't say that. We're we're always just we're always just trying to stop people from from scoring, you know, no matter what it is. And uh, you know, we have high expectations for ourselves. Um, you know, I know our guys have the highest expectations. I know our coaches do as well. Um, so, you know, that 's our job is not, you know, is get our offense the ball back as many times as possible or score ourselves, and uh, that's all we're trying to do. >> To have a player well, you have several, but with Miles doing it for the first time in this game, to have a player that can close close out games or, you know, put an exclamation point on that, what's that like for you as a defensive coordinator? >> Oh, great players are the thing, and and Miles knows, you know, that's one of the main reasons we brought him here uh, to be a closer. And we think we got a bunch of closers on our defense to go out and finish games and get our offense the ball back, and uh, that's the job. And you know, it's a feeling as a coach um when you got great players that you can go out and trust and and do their job and play hard and make plays um and it's really fun to watch. >> What are the challenges >> It it is a challenge you know you're you're trying to figure out what he likes, what he doesn't like you know obviously the cut ups and the tape and all that stuff you're watching is not necessarily you know he's not necessarily in them he hasn't taken a regular season snap this year so you're doing a little bit of double duty where you're studying the scheme, you're studying the players that are going to be playing against in the game as far as the line and the skill players and like and stuff like that but you're also doing your due diligence on him and the quarterback and what he likes whether it was you know he only played in the Hall of Fame game or what he liked back at Miami or Georgia uh different things like that how he moves in the pocket so you know but nothing we can't handle but yeah it is different than obviously playing somebody that's just on the tape. >> How do you uh feel Emanuel and Josh played in light of Trent being out? >> Oh excellent I mean excellent I mean uh obviously Emanuel extremely productive bunch of PBUs I thought he was awesome in the run game physical tackling he made that play on the screen um after the uh um on the sudden change and I thought Josh has just been was just as steady as ever you know and those guys have just been ascending all season long um coach Lake uh coach Beak and and Mike Hunter do a great job with that group and I think that group's ascending and you know so we really trust those guys to continue to play well. >> You played them last month you kept them out of the end zone but they also sustained some drives and had some how do you come out of that game feeling about how you played against them the first time? >> 100% we didn't get the win so obviously it wasn't good enough um and you're 100% right they were able to hold the ball from our offense they were able to sustain some drives and get the ball down in the red zone um and we know we got to be better in order for our team we got to play well it's a really tough offense to get off the field and we got to play well in order to get our offense the ball back. >> Is there anything about Trent McDuffie that you've kind of grown to appreciate that you've only really gotten to learn once he's in the building that you maybe didn't know from the fall? >> Yeah that I mean it's really you know everything I mean you know Jimmy Lake had you know had the history with him at Washington. So, you know, and you know, talking to Chris Petersen about him. So, you heard all the stuff, but until you really see it day to day, it's almost hard to imagine how focused he is, how locked in he is. I mean, there's very few. I don't know if he has a bad play in walkthroughs and practice where he is locked in on every single thing, every single meeting. He is the ultimate definition of a pro. He's a joy to be around. He's obviously got a great personality, great person, and he's a great leader in that room. So, no, couldn't be happier with him. And you know, I I heard it, you know, but until you see it, you know, it's hard to imagine. >> What's your evaluation of your old friend on the floor and what he's done over there? >> He's done an awesome job. He really has. That group, I think they're, you know, he's got those guys playing at a really high level. I think they lead the league in 10 plus play drives. You can tell they're playing really hard. They're playing really tough. You can tell they believe in them. They're really sound. They have an identity, but they mold it to the defense that they're playing every single week. You know, they dress things up. You know, they have their stuff and they dress it up different every single week. They got really good running backs. They got a heavy line. They play physical and downhill and then they have counters off those identity in the run game. And obviously, you know, they have a different skills, you know, different skill receivers than they had the last time we played them, but tough group of guys to get off the field. >> Thanks. >> Appreciate it, guys. So, guys. >> I mean, obviously with the injuries at wide receiver, CJ Daniels is somebody potentially that more snaps this Sunday. What have you seen from him in terms of just practices and meetings with, you know, some of the behind the scenes stuff that he's done to this point? >> Yeah, he's had a lot of great moments behind the scenes. I think we've been really encouraged about his development and his progression as the year has gone on, but he's been as fun of a player to watch on our practice field for the last few weeks. And so obviously excited for him to continue to get opportunities, but it's opportunities that he's earned through a lot of hard work, through a lot of consistency in how he's approached. So, fired up for him and yeah, stepping up into this this role. >> When you lose the >> one two punch of Devonta and Puka, it's half of Matthews's passing yards almost. How do you describe the challenge of making up that difference? >> Yeah, I think anytime you're losing guys and anytime you don't have the guys that, you know, have that rapport, specifically with Matthew, there's always going to be adjustments that you want to make to, you know, how you're planning things out, to who you're putting in position to go and make plays. And so we said it when, you know, we lost Devonta for a little bit that, man, it's it's hard to replace him and what he brings to the table with with just one person. And certainly, you know, feel that way with Puka and and all that he brings to the table. That being said, we've got guys that have all been out there on the field for us this year, have made plays and to to see them step up to the challenge, to the moments is something that I think you're excited about as a coach and and I know those guys are excited about as players. And so you you literally take it one day at a time. You plan out what the best thing is for you on normal downs, on third down and red zone, utilizing the guys that we have. But they have a lot of skill sets that we're fired up to be able to use and and see those guys go and attack. >> Do you Sean and then Matthew to an extent see this as an opportunity to kind of get created with the personnel you do have, maybe do some things that you guys don't normally do as your kind of identity when you have Puka and Devonta out there? And if so, what are those conversations been like this week to try to game plan? >> You know, I think that there's elements of of both sides and I honestly think it's true every week regardless of who's available. You you want to utilize and maximize your roster to the best of its abilities. And I think that there are identity plays, thoughts that you have that are going to stay true, you know, regardless of who's available, regardless of who's in those spots because we feel like the roster's made up of guys that that fit what we need, you know, from a lot of those identity standpoints. And then you start to evolve as, you know, the circumstances dictate or as, you know, the the the year dictates for what you feel like is best. And so there's always elements of that. Certainly when there's injury, you're going to deal with more of that where you you're trying to just put guys in the best position to be successful, not by any means asking guys to do something that they've never done or you don't feel confident that they can do, but but to be able to maximize their skill set and their ability within the confines of what you do as an offense. And so this is it's a it's a great week to be able to do that, but you're right. Sean, Matthew, the rest of the offensive staff, we're always going to have a good feel of just what guys have done, what they bring to the table, and how to utilize them best. >> With Puka and Devontae, you know, having getting most of the targets, how how do you get Matthew to trust these other guys to actually target them and throw to them during the games? >> 20 more minutes of routes on air today in practice. No, I'm just kidding. We honestly trust doesn't just show up on a Sunday. Truthfully, it doesn't show up on a Thursday practice either. There's been a lot of reps over the course of the year that those guys have built up trust. And I said it a couple of weeks ago, you know, when you have guys, you know, like Puka and Devontae available, you know that you're going to try to find ways to get them the football and, you know, utilize them in those ways. It it does not mean that, you know, the the guy that's not featured on a specific play couldn't go execute in in a similar way. It doesn't mean that those guys don't have things that they can bring to the table. You know, so I I think that there's, you know, those elements that that come to life in moments where circumstances dictate. We were talking about it the other day. It's like most times in this league, circumstances are what create opportunity. And, you know, whether that's something that happens in fall camp and all of a sudden, you know, somebody's got to step up and and play with the ones and and they start to show who they are and what they can bring to the table. If that happens in season, there's oftentimes circumstances that, you know, allow for those things to happen. Very few rookies, you know, walk onto a team and and, you know, just, man, end up being in a starting role without something typically happening. And so yeah, it's a it's a great opportunity in that way. And and obviously there's a there's a lot that's been built up, but it's a good week to to obviously up the ante a little bit with those guys in their rapport. >> It seems like when you played them last what what kind of went wrong? You had really long scoring drives, but they also got job he got sacked three times. What what do you see when you back >> You know, we were able to drive the ball consistently throughout the game. We weren't able to capitalize as much as we felt like we uh should have and could have um once we crossed the 50. Obviously, it was unique. Uh you know, we're in a in that a majority of the game without feeling confident in in the field goal operation uh which made it a little bit unique. We we got a little bit more aggressive, uh probably played in a little bit different style than than maybe you would. Um you know, but that being said, give them a lot of credit, too. They they made stops in some critical moments. I got a lot of respect for uh their defense. You know, Nick Rallis has uh always challenged us in some unique ways since being the defensive coordinator there. And so uh they did a great job last time. They'll have a great plan again and and ultimately we got to be ready for the moments. It It always comes down to a handful of plays, you know, in some of those critical moments and and you don't know exactly when that that shows up. Could be, you know, the fourth quarter on the last play um of the drive. It could be, you know, the second drive of the first quarter. Uh but we we got to be ready for those moments and to be able to step up in them. >> Seems like the last three games or so Blake Hance has provided a bit of a spark in the second half with his running and short touchdown in each of those. Has that something that you guys are noticing or something that you see you can take advantage of in the coming weeks? >> You know, it it's like it's cool having this conversation because I I definitely agree that he has provided a spark. I feel like it's the same thing. Like those guys I still like go back and forth to different moments of the season that you know, I feel like there was two weeks where it was like, man, Kairon kind of provided that spark. You think about the Philly game, think about what he did. Um you know, just early in the season finding a way to make plays plays in Denver uh and then being able to see Blake the last couple weeks and and we do feel like that. We feel like whichever of those guys is out there um that they got a chance to provide a spark. That's the type of humans that they are. They do. They they provide energy to our offense. Uh they do that with more than just running the football or catching the football. It's it's the way that they approach everything that they do. And so I've been excited to see Blake be able to provide that. Um and it's and it's huge for us. It'll it'll continue to be huge for those guys to continue to step up to the moments. >> Do you like also the guys that can help you out in the passing game now that you kind of need some other guys to catch the ball? >> Yeah, you know, just like we said, I think Kairon's done a great job of that throughout the course of the year. Um obviously Blake has done a great job. Uh you know, I think back to that Giants game, him catching the check down created a uh think back to the Bills game, him catching a check down, creating an explosive play. Blue and red teams, I feel like playing a couple of them here at SoFi I was like, which one was that? Um but it it was like it was a great job by him making an explosive play, but they're they're guys whether it's in the run game in the pass game, you get the ball in their hands, they're going to find a way to to break tackles to go make plays. Um so we we feel confident in both those guys in that way. >> Nate, yesterday Matthew was talking about obviously just going through his progressions. But in years past he's also told us he just throws to who's open. Dating back to Cooper Cup getting a lot of >> Yeah. >> That being said, because these guys are not a number one receiver, does that reinforce being more wide open with the offense? >> You know what? He I think what he said is is so true that he has such a good feel of um you know just what we're trying to get accomplished with each play and and honestly like he's got a lot of confidence in the guys around and whether that be, you know, in those days Cooper Cup and the ability to go make plays, uh whether that be Puka and Devonte and their ability, but like he does just such a great job of having a feel of of what we're trying to get accomplished with each play, being able to be consistent in in what he's thinking and how he's processing. And I think those guys have done a good job also building up confidence that they are going to be in the right places at the right time, which is key. I think when you whenever you're able to develop that, whenever he's able to have that trust, it allows them to cut it loose and to play free. And so uh there is a an element of that where um you know with us right now it's like we we feel like there's not a lot of tendencies uh with with who we have on the field and what they have the ability to do. I feel like we've seen probably more of that uh than maybe what others have. You know I think back to Kanade Mumpfield, you know, on a double move against Denver, it's like well, they they probably weren't expecting him to, you know, go and make that play in a zero blitz across the 50. But that being said, we've seen him make those same plays on our field. And so I I think that's where, you know, maybe that some of the behind-the-scenes excitement comes from, you know, from not only Matthew but us as staff. >> What advantages do you see what a guy like Xavier Smith or even Tutu comes back in into the fold? >> Yeah, what is really cool about those guys is, you know, before even getting on the field, they're they're the type of guys that you just want to go to war with. They're the type of guys that they come to work with the right mentality, right mindset every day, that they are um yeah, they they they're just the type of dudes that that you love having in your locker room, you love being in the building with. And so that that's the starting point. And for those guys, obviously, to be able to come back and have um continuity with what we've done, uh to be able to know, you know, exactly how we do it, you know, even seeing Xavier uh in in walk through yesterday. I mean, he he snaps back into it. He's got a good feel of what's going on. Uh he knows the spots. Um you know, he's really got He's played all positions in this offense. And so there is a level of comfort that I think bringing guys like that back to the right type of people, uh but but they certainly have the right mind uh for what we need those guys to to be able to do. And so it's it's huge for us. >> What what I was going to say, well, I know you have confidence in Blake and Kyren. You guys kind of have a alternating pattern that you're using, but is there ever a temptation to just let one of those guys, if he's got a hot hand, to just say, let's just go with him, keep going with him? >> You know what? There there's I think Ron Gould does a great job of having a feel. He's had so many great backs in his history of like coaching that he has a great feel of when those moments are where a guy needs a few more carries. Sometimes that's because he's rolling. Sometimes that's because, man, I want to get the other guy kind of into the uh you know, into the flow of the game. And so I think there's a little bit of both. Uh I think what you know is over the course of the season, just like we said, you're going to see those guys step up and make critical plays and critical moments and having guys that you can trust out there. Um, but you know, he's done such a great job of having a feel of of the right guy for the right moment um and and certainly been a huge benefit to our offense in that way. >> You guys back off of your like, you know, they might not know our tendencies and the personnel thing and what you see on the field. Maybe they didn't see the game when Mike was here a long time or was here a long time, so he's seen some of those things. Is Does he know that or without Kuka and Devonte different personnel, is that a way to kind of surprise him or >> Surprise Mike? Yep. You got to call him and ask him. Um, >> He hasn't seen CJ, so >> That's right. He hasn't seen CJ. Um, but no, I mean, obviously Mike has a good feel of of who we are and and you know, some of those identity pieces. I feel like the same way we've got a good feel of of that on on the other end. Um, you know, but we'll see. I guess you'll have to ask him at some point in time, maybe after the game, hey, was he surprised by, you know, maybe what CJ was able to do or what um exactly. I I think there's there's hopefully a little bit of both in in everything like, man, I expected them to do that. Man, that was a little bit different than what than what I thought would would happen, but um yeah, that that's always a cat and mouse game in general. Appreciate you guys. >> Thank you. >> How you doing? >> What's up, AD? >> Not much. A little tired today. You tired? >> No, I'm good. >> I'm a little sleepy. >> All day. Just keeps going. >> [laughter] >> No questions? Okay. >> What's what's your thought on um obviously as a defense, you guys step on the field on Sundays, [clears throat] you want to perform your best. But right now, this team's going to have to lean on the defense a little bit with some of the guys down on the offensive end. Any thoughts on that? >> Uh, we just go out there and play ball. That's all we can do. Keep trying to, you know, get the ball back to the offense. Um, trying to get as many three and outs as we can. Turnovers if possible. So um that's the mindset every week, no matter um who's down or what what not be. Um, we just want to go out there play our game and trying to um play at a high level. >> I was watching more of the tape. You alongside Myles and Myles had said today that you know he didn't get some double teams cuz they were focused on you on the inside and he was surprised how free he got but there was one where you kind of pushed I guess to his left and you spun off and suddenly you were wide open you know at Jaded and you guys talked about just the different things you can do more and more now that you're playing together and things like that >> yeah man like I said last week it was fun man having him back out there um playing with him um you know I'm I'm pretty sure he's going to get a lot more double teams this week so it's going to open up for some other guys [laughter] you know so but it it's it's good to have him out there man it it's it's a little it's a different type of comfortability when you got another type of guy out there that can make plays at any time um so to continue to just you know get better every single week continue to work with him man I think um it's going to be fun um a lot of a lot of great things a lot of good game plans that we putting in I'm excited about so um just got to keep it going though right stay healthy um keep going out there and playing good football so >> Aaron what do you see when you look at Nate Landman whatever you want to call him >> Oh man I I love Landman when I was watching that in the stands when I was retired you know um he's an impact player I love him as a leader um he bring a lot of juice to that defense man and I'm having him out there um it it it it it it's pretty cool and then anytime you know it could be a fumble anytime you around the ball anytime you you punch that ball out you know it's a scoop and score for me you know just just got to pick it up so [laughter] Now that was real funny to y'all huh Okay all right all right >> They they the Cardinals are going to start a quarterback who has never taken over a regular season snap his first game is going to be be against the line that includes you and Myles Garrett um if you put yourself in his shoes what do you think that's going to be >> I don't know cuz I'm not him so I don't I don't want to speak for him but I know he's excited to be playing um he going to go out there and try to find a way to help his team to win our job is to try to find a way to get to him make him uncomfortable um you know make his first game hell if we can so um I know he going to try to you know, do what he needs to do to try to beat us, and we got to do what we need to do to, you know, stop him and and and get a win. So. >> You guys have a sack competition between you two, you and Miles? >> No, man. We just going out there as long as we making plays and we find a ways to affect the game and win it, that's it. You know, that's it. I'm I'm I'm here for the ultimate goal. >> He he also said today regarding that he thinks you're going to get some in bunches now that you guys are back and some of the pressures you're doing. And like you said, you had a lot of opportunities in Washington and Jay just got the ball out >> Yeah. It Well, yeah, sack's coming bunches, man. It It's going to come. Just keep playing ball. Um you know, and just keep finding ways to win. That's the most important thing is winning. So, um no pressure. Not worried about it. Uh you know, I've been playing football since I was 5 6 years old, man. They they coming bunches. They coming eventually. So, um just keep doing what I need to do to help this team and, you know, when they present theirself, hopefully hold the ball and take advantage of it. So. >> Yep. Thanks. >> Derek.

title: RB Jonathan Taylor reacts to trade deadline, DE Jaylahn Tuimoloau on preparing for Miami
text: Well, back to our regular scheduled programming. Uh, the same thing that we've been doing the past couple of weeks. We've been fighting, scratching, clawing to try to prepare each week to come out on Sunday with a win and it it's no different this week. Um, we just have to do whatever we can to find a way to get better and we just got to win at home, man. We got to win at home. >> Were you surprised to remain here? >> Nah, I just knew that anything could happen, so it really was no thought. Regular schedule Tuesday, body work, and just get ready for Wednesday. >> Was it hard to keep it regular from an emotional standpoint because you don't know what's going to happen? >> No, it's been going on for weeks, so just regular schedule programming Tuesday. >> Dr. did you want to be traded? >> Nah, just regular schedule programming Tuesday. Like it's all water under the bridge now, so that's why I was excited to come see you guys cuz I'm thinking we're going to talk about the Miami Dolphins now. I thought you were all sick of it. >> [laughter] >> So like indications are there's a lot going on for the future. Like what is, I guess from the locker room from you as a leader, what's your image for this season? >> Well, for me and not only myself, but I don't want to speak for them, but I am sure we're on the same page, uh, Daniel and and Cam is, you know, as captains, leaders, we have to go out there and we got to try to rally these guys, but we also got to make sure that we're doing our things on and off the field the right way to show and and set an example for the rest of the guys in the locker room because we still got what, seven more? Seven more left? It it's guys are going to come in here each and every single week or we're going to have to go and take a road trip and it's not waiting for anybody, so it's going to be on us to try to help rally these guys and guys are also going to have to step up as well and we've seen that so far, but we we just got to continue to keep making progress because like I mentioned, we still got seven more of these things to go. >> What do you make of the the the level of talent on the team take a hit, right, these last few weeks. So how have you reconciled that in light of the fact that you do have eight more to go? >> I'm I really just thought about like man, what did those guys bring, especially just from a leadership standpoint, um just over the course of this whole ordeal, the people that we've lost. I mean we've lost some some gold standard guys. Like you know, you grow up, you want to be like Quinton Nelson, you want to be like the Forrest Buckner, like a true pro's pro. So what can I do specifically for myself? What can I do to try and not be those guys but emulate those examples that they showed me? You know, I I watched those guys when I came in the building. I'm like okay, hey, he's the example. That's what I want to do. Uh so how can I emulate that? And like I mentioned, I don't want to speak for them but I'm sure we're all on the same page but Daniel and Cam, like the other leaders on the team, how can we emulate and and raise the level? Cuz obviously we you know, you took a hit uh with the leadership and and the play as well. Obviously we know those are [clears throat] astounding players but what can we do to just try to make up for that gap if you can? I mean you can't you can't really make up for those guys but what can we do to help? >> You always had um Q blocking in front of you and you talked a lot before about knowing the lineman in front of you and playing off that. Is it difficult not having him there as the the guy in the offensive line who's leading the running game? >> Oh well it was definitely never as easy if you have a Quinton you know, as if you had a Quinton Nelson in front of you. But I'm super excited cuz I know that what Quinton left was a uh a lifelong impression on the rest of the guys on the offensive line and you know, especially Farmer for example, I know that he was like lock step and hit with Quinton to to just learn as much as he could. Um so I know that he's doing everything in his power to be himself but also try to take some of those bits and pieces of knowledge and nuggets that that Quinton gave him but the rest of the O-line as well, he impacted each and every single one of them. So I think that he left them with something that will help elevate them on and off the field cuz those guys even off the field, I mean thanks for their body, they all like tapped in and tuned in to to Quentin. >> Looking up that leadership void, is there anyone in the locker room that you've noticed that has um made a point to uh you know, pick up some of that slack from a leadership standpoint? Not necessarily just your team captains doing more, but someone that's maybe not in that fold that you've noticed that has stood out? >> And I was going to say there's been a lot of guys. I mean, someone you guys all all know like Ashton Doolin, everyone already knows Ashton Doolin's a heck of a player and he's been here for a while, but being able to step up in that in that wide receiver room to help rally those guys cuz he's he's been here. He's been through a lot of things. So to be able to give those guys a piece of perspective on how to car compartmentalize and actually go about their work each and every single week with new opportunities or whatever the the shift in their role is. So there's been a few guys and like I said, it doesn't have to be, you know, captains. That's why I want to speak for everyone, but I'm pretty sure like we're all on the same page as, hey, we need to figure out a way to help one another cuz right now we got to stick together now more than ever. >> We talked to Daniel yesterday. He said, you know, in in reaction to the trade, he said, well, you you know, you don't agree with all the decisions. It was obvious cuz you lose Quentin and you lose your top two receivers. Did you have that kind of a at least partial reaction like, holy smokes, they took three quality players from us? >> Well, I would never want to lose a Quentin Nelson. I would never ever want to lose a Quentin Nelson, but I understand there's a business portion to it. So my my thing is, okay, now what can I do to also help the rest of the offensive line and say, hey, okay, how are you guys seeing this specific scheme? You know, it's like Jaylen Farmer, for example, you know, first time being in there now full time. Okay, hey, what are you expecting? I know you have your rules and your keys, but I got to get locked in in sync with you as well as the rest of the offensive line and the rest of the running back room. We got to be in sync now with the new five guys that are up front. So I think for us is how can we make their job easy as possible, whether it's our run tracks, delivering the blockers to them. It's it's more than just, oh, hey, just get a hat on a hat. There's a lot of things that we can do that can also alleviate some of their job. >> You you can't dwell on the past at all. These these guys are gone. I mean, as cold as it sounds. What do we do moving forward? >> I would never want to lose a Quinton Nelson, but the biggest thing for us is just making sure as a running back room and as myself, you know, personally cuz I can speak for myself, how can I help these guys up front? You know, hey, are you guys thinking of logging this guy? Are you guys thinking of kicking him out? They they may like something different now that there's a new combination of guys up front. So you never know. And I think, you know, working with Tony and working with with Jim Bob, we're just going to make sure we have a a great plan put together in order to try to come out with a win. >> Have you had any conversations with Carly or Ed or anybody about like the direction of the franchise? Cuz when you trade players away, they're building for the future, but you're in the present. >> Yeah, not that's way above my pay grade. Those are those are some hard decisions that you have to make. I'm glad I don't have to make those decisions. I'm glad I just have to come in here, make sure that I'm my best each and every single day for my coaches and my teammates. So I would hate to be in that situation. I would hate to be in that situation, but I I know that they have a vision and a plan for it. And right now we just got to execute right now. The best thing that's going to help us is executing going out getting a win versus Miami. >> Were you surprised about the lighter workload you've gotten in the last few weeks? >> Not surprised cuz you always prepare each and every single week, no matter it's whether it's 30 carries or whether it's five carries. They say, hey, we got to pick up the Mike backer 15 times, we'll win the game. Whatever it is, I'm ready and trained to go. >> Are you willing to be a part of a rebuild? >> What do you mean? >> Are you are you willing if this is the direction the franchise is going, are you willing to be here and be a part of that? >> Moves have already been made. It's time to go win versus Miami, baby. >> Thanks. >> Jaylen Kyle McCord going to get the start this weekend for the Miami Dolphins. Obviously someone you are very familiar with having shared time at Ohio State. Your impressions of him and his talent as a quarterback. >> Man, I mean, he's a hard nose. He's a tough quarterback. And our times there, I mean, there is a reason he was recruited high. So he's a he's a talented quarterback and I think this is his first start. So man, excited excited for him. It's going to be just like practice when he's out State going against him, so it should be a fun one. >> What were those observations you had of him in practices, the opportunities that you were going up against him? >> Yeah, I think for me he was just a leader. Um he was a tough-nosed leader. Um never made excuses. Always wanted to get better, so for me um seeing someone like that um automatically gained my respect. Uh he's a great dude off the field too, so um yeah, I got a chance to actually it was crazy. Um got a chance to talk with him um or meet up with him um at Himeka's wedding, so we were able to catch up and and now fast forward we're going to play against each other. >> And how long ago was that? >> Uh believe this was in want to say June. >> Oh okay. >> Yeah. >> So over the summertime? >> Yeah, yeah over the summer over the summer. >> Awesome. Uh for this defense, what progression, what development have you seen over the course of the last few weeks among your defensive line kind of behind Tommy with yourself, Latu, and then obviously Kaden coming along as well? >> Yeah, I think just all the the young guys just confidence going up. Um all of us just working together, rushing together and and you know just playing for one another. Uh when no one were out there we're celebrating each other's uh sacks or or tackles they make, so um I think just those little things make a big difference. >> Obviously Kaden's been super consistent in terms of getting opportunities. We're also starting to see your rookie linebackers get more and more opportunities. What development have you seen in these first few games with CJ Allen? >> I think uh like I keep saying like confidence. Um he got that sack. He he's took on the the leadership role. Um you know getting the being starting last week too. Um you just continue to see him grow, so I think just all the young guys um from top to bottom getting their feet wet like is is tremendously helpful. Uh which is you know getting a feel for the game, getting a feel for your players uh your brothers that you're out there with, so um I think just all that and and adding it to the talents that they already have. Uh I mean it's it's sky's the limit. >> The early >> part of the season, there was so much pressure on the quarterback coming from the interior with obviously, you know, Grover and Buck and Tommy as well. How are you guys on the edges starting to take on more and more of a challenge to get more production? >> Yeah, I think shout out to the interior. You know, they're getting good push. So they're allowing the, you know, the quarterback to stay in the back for stay in his drop a little bit longer. So it's starting to open open up the rush lanes for us. And I think that just goes to show how important it is for everybody to do their job or to win on the line. You know, if we don't have good edge rushes, then we can't cause them to step up for the interior. If they don't have good push in the middle, it's hard for us to get there. So I think that just shows how much we have to work hand in hand. >> I know Shane has put such an emphasis on closing out games in particular, you know, being in that one late last weekend. What do you guys see as the opportunity that's there for you this week to kind of break this losing streak and play in all three phases type of complete game? >> Yeah, I mean, we've talked about it here where just having that standard for ourselves, you know, playing good 75 out of 80 snaps, you know, the percentage might sound nice, but it's not good enough, especially how talented everybody is in the league. So you know, when it comes from when the defense needs when the offense needs to get a stop, we get the stop. When we get the ball back, so it's just allowing us to have those opportunities and like you said, close out the game cuz you can play good for the first two quarters, but it may not be enough. That's why the game's four quarters. So playing well on all three phases is extremely high and extremely important gives us a great high percentage to win. And I think we just got to continue to execute, continue to stay together and and yeah, like you said, break this losing streak. >> I know it's been now, you know, a few weeks obviously since Buck's trade, but just with the trade deadline of this week and just the clarity, everything had a calming down with those conversations. Following Buck's departure, what's the collective responsibility that falls on in particular the rest of the the because of how much leadership, how accountability that he brought across the group. >> I think um you know with him leaving uh I mean it it doesn't go unnoticed. Like he he left a great great foundation and what it means to to play to be an elite player to be an elite person and great teammate. So um he was able to um he showed us the way showed us the uh you know how to navigate through um the league as a as an elite player and continue to play at an elite high level. Um and you know you know appreciate him to the fullest and uh you know his legacy will go but when he left I think um the impressions he left um when he did leave um that he left us with I mean it we had to take it and run with it. Um he showed us how to be a pro and you know I think you just kind of just see us like okay like hey he showed us now it's you know our time to to um instill what he established and and continue to grow uh with those uh the standard that he left and and uh the little pointers he gave us and everything.

Uh, but at the end of the day, as long as we get one more than them, I could care less. Have you ever won a game as a coordinator scoring three like three? >> Uh, no. I can't say I've done that. Not in football anyway. [laughter] >> But if it happened, I'd be happy to take it. We'd walk out of there and we would move right on. >> Uh, all right. So, uh, we'll crank it off uh, real briefly. Just want to start by, you know, just continuing to send my thoughts and prayers uh, with our captain Jack, uh, his family, his wife Megan, his son Coupe, and everybody still daily. don't want, you know, once the emotions die down in a situation like that, people tend to lose track or lose sight of the things at hand, that's still at the front of all of our minds. Um, and this entirety of this season, we're still doing it for him. So, I wanted to start with saying that. Uh, and then secondly, uh, you know, kind of talk about the way our guys went out and performed down in Miami last week. Uh, I thought it was incredible uh, from a lot of different standpoints, but the biggest thing is the no drop off mentality. No matter who's playing, no matter who's called and who's tasked with what assignment, I like the mentality that guys are playing with, the swagger, the confidence. Um, and I think it's just breathing through the entire defense. Um, I love the way that we're improving. That's what I told the guys. Like a lot of people get caught up in the numbers. Yeah, the numbers are improving and all this, but individually and collectively, I feel like each week dating back a month now, we've improved. Uh, and the biggest improvement we've taken is the explosive stuff. Uh, when you go out and only give up two explosives in a in a national football game, that's probably going to net well for defense. And our guys was able to do that. Uh so just again credit the players always start there and then credit the staff because again no staff member has made any excuse if they're at the game we're going to find a role. We're going to find what they can do to help us and try to put them in that position and we've done that. Uh and now we're tasked with going across the pond here going over to Germany excited for this opportunity. Uh and that's what we all should view it as. um another great opportunity um against a great opponent, a opponent that was in the Super Bowl um in um this past February uh and an opponent that's well coached and has good personnel. So, we know we have a tall task ahead this Sunday. >> Asking Tyreek about the defensive turnaround last week, you said we want to be the reason we do, not the reason we don't. I don't know if those words maybe came from you, but three straight games under 20 points for the first time in in five years. Can Can you feel this defense beginning to lift this team? >> Good. That's good. I'm make sure I tell Tali I appreciate him listening in meetings. Uh because that's something we actually that I've been saying from week one. Uh just a trend here, you know, and and I'm not ignorant to it. I'm not arrogant. We have a high prolific offense here. Uh been afforded that for years now. Top five offense. And that's what the talks are. That's what it's about. So just tell those guys let's make sure that we're the reason why we are doing things why we are moving forward as a team and an organization and not uh so that's been a theme since training camp and guys have taken heed to it. Um Tai is a big reason why we are doing things right right now. Uh you know he doesn't show up glaringly on the stat sheet like Lean McNeel Aiden Hutcherson do. Uh but his impact to our defense and to the team success is tremendous. You guys added [clears throat] Cisco right ahead of the deadlock. You just, you know, Dan talked about the familiarity he has with the system coming in. Just can you just speak to that and maybe you if you had any conversations with AG about him? >> Oh, absolutely. I've talked to AG two times this week already. Just figuring out what he already knows with what we do. Uh because this is different than what we were doing when AG was here. Some of the terminology is different. Some of the things we do, the nuances within it is different. Uh, but he's heard the verbiage and that's the biggest thing. Everybody plays the same coverage in the NFL. The biggest task when you acquire a guy on short notice and he's up for the game on Sunday is the verbiage. Like trying to let him know, hey, this Well, we didn't have to do that for Cisco. He jumped out at practice yesterday and it was like he's been here. Uh, he's a big athlete, um, rangy player. Um, he does a lot of things well and he has a skill set that we're going to utilize starting Sunday. Uh but he just provides again another player that's going to come in. I told the unit because a lot of people, oh we got Kirby back, we got BB. Don't look at the don't try to look at it as a luxury now with how we could start to chess piece guys, move guys here, move guys there with the availability that we're starting to get now at the safety spot. >> What does it what does it provide in terms of flexibility within that secondary? >> Yep. Yep. I think he could do it all. Um, I think that Cisco is a guy that could play in the high part of the field, the deep part, post, quarter track, things like that. But I also think he's a guy obviously with his size, his frame, his abilities that you could put him down in the box um and park him in the box as a down safety as well. So just having the opportunity to not have a one-trick pony, a guy that all right, if I want to do this, I lie with Kirby. If I want to do this, I lie with Chuck, Izzy, BB, he allows me to do that and move those guys without secondguessing them. How much did you lean on Shawn Dion Hamilton last week and a really emotional strenuous week for those linebackers? And with how well those guys played on Sunday, how much of that was a testament to the work that he did with them last week? >> Oh, I've leaned on Ham ever since he took over the room. Uh it's a big thing. Everybody joked with him when he took over that he has the hardest job on staff now. Just like my man Steo on offense. He's the tight end coach. Will you coach Dan's position? That's the hardest job on offense. Uh but to be totally transparent with you, he's been a guy with me now. I coached Sean in 2021. Connie was around, you know, and things like that. So, I've been around Ham now going on six years. I view him as a brother. I don't view him as a member of my staff. Uh and it's somebody that I have blind trust in. Uh the work that he does with that linebacker room at times goes kind of unnoticed. uh the detail that he puts in. Um I remember him running to the hospital when his wife Sam was pregnant, having a baby, and trying to run back to make sure the install was right. And I'm like, "Dude, you lost your mind. Go to the hospital before you get cussed out." And he's like, "I got to make sure the backers have the tip sh and things like just the detail that he operates with, the intensity that he operates with, it bows through the room." Uh and it exudes through the players play. Um so I was excited, man. And I thought Malcolm went out and played a high level game. I thought Derek Bournes did a tremendous job with the green dot communicating, flying around, making plays. Uh, and Trevor Noski has been a mainstay for us all year pretty much. Uh, and that's credit to Ham. So, you know, I have total trust, total faith in Ham. >> You brought the first play of the game. It's it's Rodrigo and Barnes and Noski together shutting down that run. What did that moment signal to you about their readiness for for that game on Sunday? And I I mean I would be remiss not to mention 46. Uh for for guys that go out listen uh like everybody's close with Jack, but it's a different deal when it's the brother in your room. They're in lock step. They spend every day, every minute of the day together. Uh and those guys were playing for him. And and that's what I saw outside of the work that Ham's done. You you put all that aside, I saw those guys playing for their brother and absolutely pouring their hearts out. So, credit to that room. Credit to Shan Dion Hamilton. >> You brought Lucas up uh with Hassan. I mean, what's it going to take for him to be active, I guess, and uh kind of get on the field. >> Just depends on what the week uh requires and what it calls upon and the skill set that we're looking for that week per that game plan. >> What What is where do you see his growth? I mean, has he done enough, I guess, you know, to kind of merit, you know, an opportunity, I guess, or >> when you say merit opportunity, you only get 46 people on game day. So, who are you putting down? That's the big quote. Like, there's nobody necessarily that you are going to put down with the way the Dline's been playing. So, again, it has to merit. Um, AMD has done a tremendous job. just asked the offensive line how much AMD has progressed here through not only training camp but the course of the season him Lucas those guys do a tremendous job on the look show team every week so it's just a matter of the right thing just because a guy may be progressing does that fit within the scale of the roster and how we get them to game day >> I ask was because obviously TJ was you know inactive last week so I mean that would have been maybe the opportunity to you know and >> we felt it was the opportunity to bring Lucas to the game. So, we did. >> You you you always had a tendency to be guarded when heaping praise on players, but I mean, we're going into week 10. Lee McNeil already has a careerhigh in sacks this season. Just what can you just say more about the way that he's been playing and, you know, coming back from that injury after having a full year to not be rehabbing to be able to train and, you know, get back to where he wanted to be? >> Yep. I'm I'm actually very hesitant in putting expectations on players before they go out and do it. Uh, I'm big on what the tape says and the tape says that he's one of the best defensive tackles in the league. Uh, you know, before the season started in training camp, I got a bit emotional talking about how he tried to press through the injury last year just cuz Max another one I've been around for six years now. We have a very close bond. Uh, and I know who he is. I know who he wants to be and I know what he wants to do for his team. Uh, so to watch him last year, like I said, not be able to put his foot in the ground playing on Doubleton and now you watch him this year, man, I can't be happier for anybody. Uh, great person, great human, and a tremendous player. Uh, that's playing at the level that we knew that he could play and more importantly that he knew he could play at. So, I'm excited for Mack. And you talk to Mac, you won't know that he's playing at that level because he thinks he can do more. He could provide more. He thinks there's opportunities that he's left out there. Uh, that's the beauty of coaching the players that we have here, man. >> With Eric Moore, with Eric Moore, just the opportunity that he had and taking advantage of that. I mean, I'm sure a lot of that, some of it came down to availability, but some of it probably came down to the work that he's been putting in over the weeks. Just how have you seen him earn the opportunity and be ready for his moment? >> Again, he's very blessed. I tell all those young guys, cuz they don't really understand, they're blessed and fortunate to be in Casey Rogers room. Uh, and anybody around the NFL that sat in his room and been coached by other people, listen, no knock against anybody else. Talk to the players that sit in his room and then they go sit in somebody else's room. It's different. Um, Casey's done a tremendous job with him. So has Caleb Collins. Uh, he works very closely with the younger players in that room. U, particularly the edge. So they've done a tremendous job. And then Derek Moore putting the time in during by-week. I find out that he's at the facility every day. Those are guys you root for. Those are guys you know it means something to and if you work that hard eventually it's going to show up. But I told him you had two sacks. You should have had five and really had a breakout performance. >> Alm gets an assist on his second sack. Right. >> Yeah, dude. M missed it. Hutch missed it. M missed it again. And then like Casey said, Derek Moore, there he is catfishing and bottom feeding. >> Drake May was an MVP candidate last year but leads the league in interceptions this year. What sort of challenge does he provide to your defense? And does that provide any sort of like takeover or turnover opportunities for your defense as well? >> Yeah, we see the takeaway. They're number 31 in the league right now. I think as far as total margin in their last, but that means nothing cuz they're also the number one explosive team in the league when it comes to generating explosive plays. Uh they've generated 80 of them thus far, which you look around the league, everybody would say our offense is highowered and prolific. I think we've generated 74 75. So, he does a tremendous job extending plays, pushing the ball down the field. That's the way they want to play. It's clear to us and we understand that. Um, he has a very good deep ball. Uh, his receivers extend these plays. They understand where to be, the spots on the field that the quarterback likes. Uh, again, listen, this team is a super This team was in the Super Bowl in February. So regardless of numbers, what it says, and I have the utmost respect for that coaching staff, uh, Coach Ravvel, Josh McDaniels, this this is the NFL right here. And that's what I told the guys, this is NFL football. We're going into November, and we need to be playing our best football. >> Chef, the the strides you guys have made in the secondary over the past month are probably somewhat tied to some adjustments in scheme, also to some adjustments in personnel. Getting BB back obviously goes a long way in that department. >> Yeah. What gives you the most confidence that what you've seen over the past month in that area of the defense is sustainable for the rest of the season? >> Yeah, the biggest thing is I see detail. The level of detail, the level of focus to be where you're supposed to be one more time. Uh don't search plays. Let the plays come to you. I know you guys starting to see a lot more plays being made on the ball. That's guys letting the plays come to them, not trying to jump things. Do something out of the realm of comprehension of the scheme. Uh, and again, listen, let's make a huge shout out to Deay Townson. That was a guy that came to me when things was dark and rough and had a heartto-he heart about he had some ideas that were kind of unconventional, unorthodox. And at first, I had to listen and really hear them out. And I'm just thankful that I have the trust I do in my staff, Jim O'Neal, Dre Thompson, those coaches that sit in that room, the blind trust that I have in them that when they're convicted of something, I listen and I push forward because this is us, not me. Um, and they've done a tremendous job. And so as the players in the room, >> three weeks in a row, special teams player of the week to get like a [clears throat] pizza party or something. >> Yeah, you get a pizza party. No, that a boy. No, it's funny. I that's like the it's this one award that um I I don't even know like it happens. My wife tells me uh sometimes somebody else tells me in the building, hey, congrat you know. Um I think uh it's a weird it's a weird award obviously for those guys who get it. It's awesome. Um it's also some recognition of the group. Now that being said, like I know that all those specialists feel like, oh man, I've had better games and didn't get it, you know? So, it's kind of a awkward thing. I think you know your team's got to win and then what you have to play well but yeah and then sometimes somebody else did something better than you did or what or it's perceived as better. But yeah, it's good anytime you get any recognition. Take it because we get the other side too. >> Is there any [laughter] uh uh information you have on the the turf there? I mean, obviously the soccer pitch is different than >> Yeah, I don't know. Uh my experience playing uh over there, I haven't played in Germany, but uh whatever London and all that. It's it's very similar like no big deal. I think I say this like everyone talks about all that stuff and it's great, man. It's great for the NFL. Like it just more talking points. So we go back to the Rams at the beginning of the year. You know, they travel late and the other team travels early. I've been a part of staying over there for a whole week and getting ready to play the game. We took off right after we went I was in San Fran. We played Carolina. We took off right after the Carolina game from Carolina. So, we were already halfway across country, went overseas, and then uh and stayed there for a week and got ready and played the game. And then I've also done it where we've gone over late. Um and I say this, like here's the formula. It's Yeah, here's the formula. The formula is number one, go over there with a really good football team. Um number two, make zero excuses. There are no excuses. and number three win and then come home and then everything you did is going to be perfect and everything the other team did was totally wrong. Um and it really wouldn't matter what you did. Um it's just classic in this business and they blame everything. It's like it has nothing to do with any of that stuff. Both teams go through adversity. They shift the adversity one way or the other based off how they travel or whatever. But it's all the same. I say the same thing about like head coaches. they go through a head coach and they um you know there's a head coach in place, whatever, they're not doing well. So everything that guy does wrong, they practice too early in the morning, they practice too late. They practice too long, they don't practice long enough. He's too hard on them, he's too easy on him. Um what it's just all of the above. And so then what they usually do is they lose a bunch and then so they fire that guy and they go hire the opposite because it's got to be the opposite. And then as soon as that guy doesn't work out, then it's like, okay, back to the other. And it's an offensive coach. Well, we needed to hire a defensive guy. There's a young guy. We need to hire an old guy. It was an old guy. We need to hire the young guy. Like it just goes around and around. No, what you need to do is you need to get good play good players, good people, and you need to go win games, you know? And you got to stick with the formula. Believe in something. Have some conviction. Stick with the formula. Be determined to go win somehow someway. We're going to overcome whatever's thrown our way. and we're going to go win the game or we're going to turn into a successful organization. We're going to stay the course. We're not going to let the outside world talk us in or out of anything and uh we're going to believe in ourselves and we're going to we're going to go get it done, which is what the successful people do in life. So anyway, this game to me is like I love it because it's just all the drama and it's great. It doesn't come down to any of it. >> Going back to Jake, I mean obviously the preeason uh end of preseason you it was a little shaky. I mean, you know, the >> you you thought so. I didn't. Go ahead. >> Miss kicks though at the end of the season. I mean, but I mean, obviously, it seemed like he flipped the switch once the regular season. >> Yeah. So, again, it's a little bit like that. And I'm not knocking you on it. Yeah, I get it. Yeah. You saw him miss two extra points in a preseason game. Um, I saw him kick all the kicks in practice. I have all the data and the numbers and I've said this here before but like those guys really whatever don't they call that like regression to the mean or something like that in math or you know I'm not very smart but I think it's like regression to the mean and ultimately these guys all kind of regress or find like they become who they are and so him over time has been a very high percentage kicker in a lot of different areas. He had a couple miss. But if you just take the big big picture and the whole sample size, which you guys don't see all that or the outside world definitely doesn't. They see a couple kicks on a game and go, "Man, he's, you know, not very good." But the truth is like we know exactly who he is. We have a lot of data. I think that's the other thing they say in stats. Small sample sizes are worth nothing, you know. Um, you got to have a big big picture. So anyway, yeah, no, he's been I think he's been who he's been the whole time. I think he's continuing to improve. Um, and so far things have gone his way. Some point he's going to end up missing a kick or something like that, you know, and everyone's going to turn on him and the numbers are going to be weighed down. Um, that you guys see, but ultimately, no, he's done a great job. I got a lot of confidence in him and uh, you know, I think he's over the last few years here now, he's really developed and, uh, he's just getting better and better and it's going to continue to go that way. you guys last week. You also [snorts] gave up one. I think first time in 50 years that both punters completed a pass in a football game. Uh as a man who appreciates history, what was it like to to be part of history in both ways? >> Yeah. >> Uh well, yeah, that's interesting. [laughter] Um I thought Fox did an incredible job and Tate did an incredible job. Um I also think I mean they did a great job. you know, they they ran a great play against us. It it was totally my fault. Um I know coach said that it's not his fault at all. It was totally my fault. I had us in like the worst possible call you could ever have us in um in that situation. Whatever. Uh also leading up to it, honestly, we we had been aggressive and we stayed that way. But anyway, it's totally my responsibility uh on the one we gave up. But yeah, it's I mean, you like seeing fake punts and all that stuff. I think it's exciting. It makes the game exciting. Adds another element to it. Um certainly for us, we got to do a better job obviously defending it. >> I was going to ask about what Dan said. He, you know, he said that in an effort to to spark a return for DeAndre, he kind of exposed you guys up front. So, as as the coordinator there, like what's the balance between trying to set one up without making yourself too vulnerable to to a play like that? >> Yeah. No, it's a it's a great uh it's a great word, balance. I think there is a balance to it. I mean, look, you can approach that play in a lot of different ways. If you just go out there and say, "Our main goal is to stop every fake." Well, yeah, you may stop every fake, you're probably not going to help your team out a whole lot with that unit either. Um, I would never see myself playing the game that way, obviously. But, you do have to balance it out. You have to be smart. You have to know who you are, who they are, situation in the game, really, how many points are being scored in the game, um, how valuable is a possession in the game. there wasn't a lot of possessions in that game. So, there's just so many things that when you add it up like uh we should have been in a totally different configuration. And that being said, like we've been aggressive. Um I think we're one of the better return teams uh in the league right now and our opponent's nets down in a lot of different areas and uh we have good field position in a lot of parts of the field plus 50 fringe. Um but uh so we played well with that unit, which also tells you, hey man, you got to be ready. You know, teams are going to try to slow you down. So it's definitely a balance. Um you know, I'm not going to sit here and tell you we're going to defend every single fake, but we definitely got to make it a lot harder than we did in that game. Um and uh we'll still be aggressive, but we also got to be smart and we're going to keep playing. How fun is it for you when the decision comes down in that moment to go for it for for you know for the first time and stuff like that on the fake punts? >> Oh, for our f Well, that really comes down to the head coach. [laughter] >> How fun is it for you in those moments >> to be able to do it to be able to like >> Oh, I love it. Yeah. I mean, he calls it I love it's like Tay Martin, he said, "Hey, man. When that thing came in, I was like I was so excited, but I didn't want to show it when I was running out on the field." You know what I mean? Um, so anyway, yeah, it's great. I mean, you love running them. I love the fact that Coach Campbell supports that. He's very aggressive with it. It's good. I think part of it is how we practice and he sees the execution in practice, too, which helps give a guy confidence to call those things and those guys do a great job of it. And yeah, I mean, you can't do a throw like that without Fox. Um, I mean, he his ability to throw that football is incredible. So, it's a weapon. We got to use it. >> Who designs to play like that? Is that you or is like petting involved too? I mean, >> yeah, not petting. Uh, it'd be Coach Campbell, myself. Um, and really like all those plays or a lot of them, you know, even the play they ran against us, it was really a play actually this week, uh, Vable and those guys when they were in Tennessee ran that against Kansas City. Um, the play they ran. Um, and uh, yeah, so they ran that that play, the hitch that we ran. I mean, it's been run a lot through the years. So sometimes you come up with something that's a little bit unique or has, you know, the same type of play with a little different twist on it. Sometimes you're running the exact same play. But yeah, ultimately we'll look at it together. Coach Campbell and myself, either he comes up with something, whatever. Sometimes I come up with something. But yeah, ultimately he makes the call to when to put it on, when not to put it on, all that. >> Over the last couple weeks, Andre Cisco really carved out a role for himself on the Jets special teams. Uh Dan said that he wanted to get him involved pretty quickly out in this next game. On defense, is he someone that you feel like, you know, can impact your unit as well? >> Yeah, you know, we got a lot of moving parts uh really last week also and then this week, that adds another one. But yeah, we want to, you know, if he's going to be up and active on the game, then he's going to have to play. And if he's not starting on defense, which I'm assuming it would be harder to go out and start on defense right away or play whatever every play on defense right away, maybe you got to roll. Um, and if that's the case, then you're going to have to have a role for us to take whatever to balance out the load. Um, so yeah, he's done a great job. He's come right in. Obviously, it helps. Uh, you know, he played in Jacksonville early in his career, a lot of special teams, and year one and then year two was a little bit less of that, a little bit more defense. and uh same thing with three and four there and then he went to the Jets. Um and then he started to come back into playing teams again a little bit. Um so yeah, I think the biggest thing when you're looking at players like that is kind of what's their internal motivation, you know, like how bad do they want to play these on these units because that's a huge part of it. Um like I told our guys last week, last week we were playing against the Dolphins and I said to those guys, "Hey man, I'm just going to tell you right now, these guys play hard and they're good. every every player in this league, if you're good enough to be in this league, you're a good football player. So, most of the time it comes down to the other stuff, your effort, your execution, your footwork, your technique, um, and those things win. So, anyway, um, yeah, and he's been great in terms of that. Like, he wants to go and play and contribute and help out and so I definitely see him having a role going into this one. >> Dave, you mentioned Jack being a weapon. You've seen a lot of punters around this league. Does anyone have as good of an arm as >> I thought Johnny Hecker back when he was at the Rams they used him to throw the ball and I thought he was very very good. He was a similar thing. He was a high school quarterback. Um I think he was recruited to Oregon State to be a quarterback. Um and they end up becoming a punter for them. Um and then obviously they used that in LA. But I would say he was the one guy um that I thought was like that. I haven't seen anybody um look like Fox since then for sure. And I don't know which one's better, but they're both good. I know we played against Hecker a handful of times and uh it was an issue I mean going into the game. >> And then yesterday was Veterans Day. Just giving your personal ties to the military and the fact you were just nominated for the salute to service a year. Does yesterday provide you a chance to reflect at all or is that just a daily inspiration for you no matter what today might be? >> Yeah. Um, that's a good question. I mean, yeah, I don't I don't Yeah, the military is important to me. My dad was shaped by the military and um my dad speaks of the military in the highest regard or highest terms um or spoke of it and uh I know that it it had such a positive impact on him and changed the trajectory of his life so much and he conveyed that to us clearly through his stories. Um so I definitely have a very fond appreciation for the military and the sacrifices those people make. Um I'm embarrassed because I did not make that sacrifice. Um so it's very humbling um to be honored um through the military stuff here is is very humbling. Um and uh yeah, I just I I I think the ability to be selfless is incredible. I think uh mothers are incredibly selfless um people and I think it's just a it's a trait or equality that really we don't emphasize or put a ton of importance on um in society today and I think the military man those people are selfless and they they really give and could give the ultimate sacrifice their life for us and the fact that somebody would do that for me or for our country or for the values that this country stands by is very humbling. Um, so I often think of it, I'm reminded of it in certain times, obviously any holiday like that. Um, and uh, anytime you hear the national anthem, I can't help but think about the the young men and women, and a lot of them are young um, kids out there that are putting themselves in that situation, and they all volunteered for it. Um, and uh, so yeah, it's very humbling. Um, I'm I'm tremendously grateful for our armed services and the people who sacrificed their lives. There's a lot of other people that we don't even know what they're doing and they're doing it for our country. Um, yeah, so it's humbling. So I think about it on those holidays and uh obviously just very grateful.

title: Can Kirk Cousins Keep Up With Jordan Love?
text: Kirk Cousins is set to start for the Minnesota Vikings in Lambeau Field, but can he keep up with Jordan Love in that high-flying Packers offense? >> You are locked on NFL crossover, part of the Locked On Podcast Network. Your team every day. >> Welcome inside a crossover Thursday. Locked on Packers, locked on Vikings. I'm Peter Bukowski. I host Locked On Packers. I'm joined by Luke Braun. He hosts Locked On Vikings and we have a ton to get to. We're going to have an absolute blast on the show today. And I'm just I'm a little disappointed, Luke. Where's the Where's the chain? You don't have a chain for today? What's going on? >> I I do not own a chain and I will never own a chain. I think most of our listeners would be relieved to learn this. >> Today's episode brought to you by GameTime. Download the the GameTime app, create an account, use code locked on for $20 off your purchase. We will, of course, get into everything related to this game, the big storylines. I think we can think of at least one big one, Luke. [laughter] Uh some matchups to get into here and, of course, the keys to victory as well as I make sure my chain is outside of my sweater so everyone can see it right now.
