title: George Kittle Sounds Off on the 49ers’ Trade for Keenan Allen
text: What does Keenan Allen add to the offense? >> Um. Let see. I mean, just somebody who understands how to run routes. Um. You know, there's only so many different, you know, concepts really in the NFL. And so like, well, you might not know the verbage of our offense, like he's ran all the routes before. And so like, it's similar to Mike. Like you be like, hey, we need you to run this type of post. And he knows how to set up a corner if he's in quarters or if it's like man to cover man coverage. Like he just knows how to run the route. There's not a lot of coaching. And so he can just fill in right away. He knows how to get open. Catches everything. Like he's what you want in a vet player. And I'm just excited to play with Keenan cuz I used to draft him in fantasy football back when I played. So I'm really excited about it. And seeing the AC Jordan person was pretty cool as well. >> When you see him in your fantasy football scouting and stuff like that, do you say to yourself, oh, that's a guy who would fit in in a Kyle Shanahan >> Oh, yeah. I mean, like I said, like I've been a fan of Keenan Allen for a long time. Like he's one of the I mean, is he Yeah, I mean, he's what same age as Mike or just a year older maybe? But like he's one of the guys who's been doing it at a very high level for a long time. He's very dependable. Like I said, great hands, runs great routes, gets open when you need him to, catches the ball in tight coverage. And he knows what he's doing. So when you have a guy with confidence, no ego, he's ready to go out there and play. I'm just looking forward to us lining up next to him. >> George, statistics suggest the Cowboys are one of the worst defenses in the NFL. What do you see that when you watch them that suggest they're not as, you know, woeful as the numbers suggest? >> I think their D line is really good. Um. Uh coach Shanahan shared with us that like I think they're ranked 31st in run defense, but they've given up like five 50 plus runs. So if you just take off those explosives, they're like a top 12 defense. So he's you just got to watch film and, you know, look at it for what it is. They have spell like talented players. They have really good defensive tackles. Their edge setters are good. Um. And they play really sticky man coverage. So, you know, I think they're going to be fired up to play us. Uh you know, it's a Dallas Cowboys versus San Francisco 49ers rivalry. The fans are going to make it a rivalry. It's going to be a big game. Um it's just one of those games that's like it doesn't matter what the record is. Like it's going to be a really tough game. It's going to be a fantastic atmosphere in Dallas. And I know that uh both teams are going to give it their best. >> George, you guys have uh at least so far on historic pace in the red zone. What would you kind of attribute the success you've had there so far this season? >> Um I think that you know, our guys are getting open. Our guys making plays. Um Christian has like seven 1 yd touchdown runs. That helps. title: Raheem Morris Gives an Honest Assessment of the 49ers’ Pass Rush
text: No sacks in the last two games, but the ball's coming out quick. How would you assess the pass rush? Are you getting what you want from it? >> It's really hard when you talk about that. You know, um the ball does come out quick, but it's never excuse. Um it's really about, you know, what happens when the ball comes out quick. And last week, we sent a bunch of screens and a bunch of guys really getting to the football and knocking it down and being in the right spots. They hit some balls, they got some completions on us that you wish you had back. You know, there was a couple interceptions out there where you're forcing things early. you know, got a really critical hit by Keon White during that game on double move that they had, you know, potentially had some hay on, but you know, Keon made a great rush. So, you're really excited about where you can go. You know, obviously you want the production, particularly for the individual stats and the guys, but, you know, really happy where the defense is and when they're playing in the most critical moments. You know, they're being their best when their best is required and that's that's really all you can ask. >> You've had a lot of young guys obviously step up this year. Der example something. I'm curious, what is your philosophy on getting guys to make an early impact. Is there something that you'd like to see early in training camp or early season to gain that trust for you? >> I I think it starts in the draft process, you know, just really having a vision for the players when you pick them up or, you know, free agency or however you acquire the player, you know, having a vision for that guy. You know, every once in a while you get a guy just throughout the course of it when you get him on the grass and you see what he can do and you're able to plug and play guys. But for the most part, a lot of the young guys that we're talking about, you know, were visions from the draft process, you know, whether it was Halton unfortunately going down or whether it was Duggar, you know, being able to go out there and make plays and, you know, a bunch of our other rookies and, you know, second year players being able to come back and step up. But, um, I I really just, you know, try to hold to that vision and then let those guys go out there and play it out. And the better you do, the more you play. >> Raheem, snap count. Mel played 20 snaps. So, I'm excited about where they can go. um you never go in. Right now, we have no injury limitations with those guys. title: 49ers share GOOD NEWS on Mike Evans…
text: All right, Thursday night football in the books. And after 49ers practice, some really good news dropped because everybody has been wondering about the limbo that Mike Evans seems to be in. I've been repeating over and over again that it the the the signs make it seem clear that the 49ers are managing Mike Evans, like NBA style load management. And Kyle Shanahan essentially confirmed that and I thought gave a stronger quote to KMBBR than even I expected. He said that I think it would be hard to keep Mike Evans out if this was the last game. Meaning that if this were the playoffs or if this were a bigger game, I think that you could read in between the lines from Kyle Shanahan. Mike Evans would play. It's obviously not the playoffs and Dallas has maybe the worst defense in the entire NFL. So, Mike Evans is not going to play. And I think this is how the 49ers had it drawn up for a few weeks. We just saw Washington with a seasonsaving win against the New York Giants on Thursday Night Football. Washington was the opponent when Mike Evans was battling through the Achilles tendonitis, but could not finish the game. exited at halftime. But it seems we're dealing with a very good player, who obviously has little video, but what there is...He's accurate. He can get rid of the ball quickly.  He has a strong hand.  This will be exciting. You've had to rotate a few guys in recent weeks due to injuries. What have you seen from guys like Connor or Riley Mills getting a little more playing time? Yes, I think you're seeing the same thing, two different players.  I think Riley has much more experience playing defense than Connor.  I think Riley is constantly progressing.  I believe that some of the greatest successes are in the game against takeaways. I think Riley is a very good pass rusher.  And in the game against takeaways, he's starting to understand some of the techniques that we use, they were different from what he used in college.  And I think Connor made a huge leap.  I think Connor...he's working hard to get into the rotation.  He is eager to get playing time because when he is on the field, I felt his performance on Sunday.  I think he had about 12 plays a game, and, you know, he put pressure on the players and did a great job of it. And he did it without training, as far as I'm concerned .  For a young guy who hasn't played much, what does that demonstrate? He just…I think, Connor, that when players get to a point where they have their own process, they understand their role. They understand what they have to do.  I think they can play fast.  And Connor already has it.  He has his own process during the week.  He is getting ready.  He knows his stuff.  He doesn't need to go beyond the boundaries.  He just knows exactly what to do.  And he also has a plan for how he makes breakthroughs, he understands how he fits into the big picture, he acts—and he does his job well. How fast does Byron Murphy work out the game and how fast is he playing now? Yes, Byron does a great job.  I still think he can reach a whole other level.  I think he does an extremely high job in the game against takeaways.  I think he should keep pushing to do more effective things.  In my opinion , he is an extremely powerful player.  It's like driving a pole into the ground—it's very difficult to move that pole during removals.  I think he has potential for development. One of them will be on Sunday.  He made a catch in the end zone (TFL) when he moved more, hopefully there will be more moments like that.  I believe he can achieve more, and I think his passing game is also at a high level. Attacks during your first game scenarios.  Sometimes they are trying to achieve a specific result, and sometimes they are trying to learn something about how the defense plays. How does this work in defense?  Are you intentionally demonstrating certain patterns to prepare future draws, or are you simply reacting to what you see? Um, yes.  I think sometimes you go in with plans because I think in every draw you're trying to get information.  Um, sometimes you attack as a defense , and sometimes you defend.  And I know how it sounds, but sometimes you really defend yourself, playing according to the standard scheme, trying to understand everything and adapting as the game goes on, but I think that after each play you reassess the situation, understand what's happening, what they're giving you, and then you act from that . We talk a lot, or you talk a lot about unity when you're evaluating the possibility of bringing someone into the rotation or into the team. How do you determine that a player will be selfless and willing to adopt this approach?  I think they prove it with their play.  What do you mean when you evaluate someone from the outside? I think it's different for free agents and for those who are drafted.  With drafted players or undrafted agents, you have the ability to see them, know them and understand them, you can rely on experience.  When you work with guys who come in as free agents from other teams, you have to let the game footage speak for them. What do you like about Nick about playing against tight ends, knowing he played against McBride a lot last week? I suppose he'll see some of ours , at least.  What exactly do you like about this confrontation?  I think Nick has long limbs, long arms, he's athletic and comes out of turnovers like a smaller player. His personal guarding skills, I believe, are not limited to situations against tight ends.  I've seen him do it against big receivers too.  He has the ability to play individually, keep up with players, and his arm length helped him play through the opponent's hands and knock the ball out in the last play against Arizona.  What about Bowers?  What kind of matchup is this? The same.  I think he's a big player who can move quickly when changing direction.  So sometimes, when playing against big players, they push back, gain an advantage, understand how to operate at the top of the route.  I think Bowers does a great job of breaking away in these spaces.  He has a good ball-catching radius , so you can pass even when he is in contact with you.  And Nick , I think Julian does a good job of that too What's the next level for Byron?  You said there was still a level he could reach.  What does this mean?  Exactly what I said: work consistently on every down.  There have been games where he has taken the game over , and he just needs to continue to consistently press and develop in that situation. And I think he's only at the beginning of his journey, because there are still many moments ahead where experience will play a role—over time he will learn different patterns and situations. He'll understand what plays are going to be made because I think at this position you get these situations and these setups every day and there's only a certain amount of things that can happen based on blocking schemes, downs and spacing, and it allows you to see Leo , sometimes Leo and Jay Reed, make some great plays because they're playing the forward pass, and I think over time Byron can learn from those guys and make those plays on early downs. He told us that you gave him permission to do a two-point lunge.  How did this even come about? Um, I just think it's him because he has unique mobility skills I believe he has very unique lower body strength and moves like a He moves like a winger when he gets close to opponents and uses leverage because he's not very tall. So you can go under players, and we just thought it was a good idea and tried it probably since last year, before the Tennessee game.  I think the Tennessee game was the first one where he did it, and he made a serve during the pressure that we organized together with Spoon. And I think that was the first time we did it, and then he started practicing it in practice, and it became a reality this season. Did you have another defensive tackle that you worked with who had done this before? I did it.  Leo did it last year.  We ...but it was more like the way the wingers, when they went inside, created distance and space, and some of his movements, I think, carried over to a certain extent.  So we're just checking if we can do it. What exactly was it about Murphy that made you think a two-point stance would work?  Speed ​​or the fact that it's lower to the ground? Yes, speed, agility, low stance, lower body strength. He has, I believe, elite short-distance speed, his ability and his plasticity.  He is very coordinated. in a general sense.  What is the advantage of a two-point snatch over a three-point snatch? Um, it's different for different players.  I think space and time are changing.  They curve because the line is moving.   It matters who you take the leap with.  Um, down and distance, the situation you're in .  All of these things change to some extent .  If you have time, it makes it easier to get past the players.  It's like taking people out into the open. What guidance do you give on when to do it and when not to?  He presented it as a green light that he could do it whenever he wanted.  And he wouldn't do that on a first down, right?  So, do you have a name for this or something?   Is there a name for this or something like that?  What What do you say? Is there a name for this?  He has a name for it.  Yes. This is called ninja mode.  He got a Yes.  He and the guys have a name for it .  Yes. Anything else? Thank you.

title: Jadarian Price: "I'm Feeling Great Now" | Seattle Seahawks
text: what you were able to do in the passing game. I think you know when we probably talked to you after the draft, you didn't have a lot of receiving numbers in college, but you made the point that, you know, something you can do. Is it is it nice to be able to show more of that side of your game when when given an opportunity? >> Yeah, most definitely. just being able to show uh what I can do in this game and uh getting a lot more one-on-one opportunities this past Sunday was was pretty fun and I shown that I could do it in this past spring and training camp pretty much the whole offseason quarterbacks knew what I could do so they trusted me. >> When you're involved that much in the passing game, does it, this might be a weird question, like does it help you stay in the run game? Is it two different things that you're thinking about or is it just the feel of the game that's important? The way I look at it is you get a over- the-sh shoulder catch like that or something, it's like, okay, I just got something a hard thing out the way. Um, or like, okay, I got an explosive out the way now. I can go focus on getting this gritty four yards and then turn that into an explosive eventually. That's kind of how I look at it. I think it does help the run game overall. >> Do you feel like you guys are getting closer to springing some of those outside zone, you know, runs that, you know, obviously you did a lot of at Notre Dame? I think we are and credit to the coaches for putting so much time and effort and finding ways for us to get better and get more um space for the backs. >> Do you have a a preference in terms of inside and outside zone and the the reads that come with those? >> Um I've always said, you know, gap scheme runs, it's it's always nice to just be able to hit it vertical and especially speed, but um you know, we're a wide zone team and I like the way we do things. you know, like we the way we blocked them and just something we got to keep keep on getting better at every week. >> When you got here, obviously Zach Shony was fairly recently removed from surgery and rehabbing to see him come as far as he had and then do what he did last week. Just what's kind of his process been like to watch being close to it? Yeah, just watching him um out there on field three um every day in training camp just just busting his tail like um hitting the numbers on a GPS and and finding his way back despite all the adversity and um also like being on the sideline watching what he's doing out there on the field. You saw the four-minute drive uh last week and his physicality, his run style, like it really inspires me to go out there and do the same. >> You feel like your guys' styles like complement each other well. you kind of you can do some of the same stuff but also do things a little differently. Is that good for an offense to have two backs that can do it a little differently? >> Yeah, I think I think so for sure. >> What about you going through your injury? What what was that like? >> Um definitely something that you know I did not expect. Um my my main goal coming into the season was you know be available for every game and that didn't happen. I missed four games and you know what do you do from there? What's important now? like how do you get over that? Um and I just continued to stay focused in the meetings and um at practice and and you know in the weight room just trying to stay conditioned and by the time I got out of here two games later, you know, I'm feeling good. >> It sounds like it it happened in the first Arizona game and what was it like playing through that in the Washington game? >> Um well, you know, things happen and adrenaline and rush and you know, you get through it. Um felt it a little bit in the Washington game, but it is what it is. Like we're football players. to go through things all the time. Um um but I'm I'm feeling great now and I'm glad that you know training I can trust the training staff to get me better. >> And last one on that. Was it two separate injuries? You had the chest injury and then we seen you with a shoulder stabilizer. Was it two different injuries or are they kind of one and the same? >> One and the same. >> Okay. >> You have you wore a red no contact jersey before the Chargers game. Is that right? >> Yes. How difficult was that or different I should say was that to get ready for a game without being full go all week >> before the Chargers game? >> I think it was >> it was for the Washington game but um I was full go Chargers week. Um >> yeah, it's definitely like you want to get the physical. You know, we're getting later on in the season so our practices aren't as physical, but definitely as a running back you want to see the linemen get their reaches and and and see how they're fitting so you can run off the blocks. Um, but as long as you're getting reaching the speeds that you want to hit, I think you're prepared for Sunday. >> We've heard a lot about the importance of falling forward and getting those yards and it doesn't really matter like what it looks like. Why has that been a point of emphasis and why does that need to be a point of emphasis? >> Um, because we've challenged ourselves as an offense to be more efficient on first and second down. So, if you can turn a two- yard gain into a four- yard gain, cuz some plays might be blocked for two yards, but you continue to push through and and get uh two or three more, it it opens up the game plan for second and third down. So, that was, you know, that's been our emphasis. Um, and we want to continue to get better at that. And it's also demoralizing for the defense if you continue to move forward. Um, so yeah. >> What is it about Drew as just a a quarterback, a leader, someone commanding your huddle that that gives you confidence in him? Um, yeah, Drew was a is a loose and focused guy and and someone who's, you know, got a lot of talent and um I caught a lot of balls from him in in training camp. So, being able to catch that some some balls from him in uh in the in the game last week was was pretty cool. Um, yeah, all of our quarterbacks are awesome people and um I'm excited for this week. And Jadian, I think I asked you about it after the game, but on that first touchdown drive, you and Zach combined for every yard until you got down to the goal line there and AJ punched it in. Just to kind of have a drive like that where you guys factored so heavily, how h how big of a springboard can that be maybe for you guys room just to kind of as you guys both come back from injuries and get up to speed to kind of show what you guys can do as a as a group? >> Yeah, when you're in when you're in the flow of the game, like you don't realize that going back and forth and we're getting all the way down the field. I didn't realize that either, but um you know, just taking one play at a time and um you know, me and Zach are finally get our feet under us coming back from injury and it's only going to get you know more production from here on out. >> Obviously, like any career, you know, responding to adversity is a big part of it and you had the injury you talked about kind of responded to that. You had some of the ball security stuff earlier. How do you how do you kind of respond to that? What have you been working on in that regard? >> Yeah, it's already, you know, coming from college, it seems like it's already been a long season, even though I missed four games. um it's been everywhere. But just continue to focus on the things that I can get better at in practice every day. Um those three days of practice where we're running full speed, how can I, you know, make better cuts, be more decisive. Um and then what am I doing outside of practice, you know, in the film room, watching film by myself and things like that. Um so I've really challenged myself to get better in those areas. >> What's been maybe something you didn't expect from playing in the NFL this first season? Um, something I noticed watching, you know, when I was younger, but when you really experience it, like every game is its own game and you're not blowing teams out like you are in college. So, like you really got to stay focused the whole 60 minutes. There's no like this past game we were up 173 and we did not feel comfortable at all. We were like, oo like we got to we got to get it going. If we get a three and out here, they got a chance to come back. So, you never get satisfied or content in in the game. You just got to keep you just got to stay locked in the whole game. >> When you were sitting out for those handful of games, I'm curious if there's anything that you gained perspective on versus like sitting out versus not playing. >> Um that every every day is is different and and you know, injuries happen. Like Mo Kelly said it while the rookies got here, everyone's going to get injured at some point in their career, whether it's early on or later on. and it's how you respond to it. Um, and I've carried that with me the past, you know, 10 weeks, like how am I going to respond to things like this? And, um, like I said, just staying focused on the game plan. Um, watching how George and Emanuel Wilson worked their tails off, um, to keep our offense going. So, >> you got your first, uh, kick return this week. Uh, is that something that you went to the team and said, like a chance at, did they come to you? Um, do you prefer getting those opportunities? No, they came to me and, you know, it's whatever I can do to help this team, you know, be successful. Um, help the offense out, get to a better field position, uh, hopefully sometime in the future, score on one of those. And, you know, they came to me because I have the history and experience of of doing well on kick return. So, yeah. >> How much different does that play feel the way the NFL does it versus versus college? Um, one difference is they're not coming at you, you know, 100 miles an hour from far away. But the other difference is like the holes do close faster. You think it's there, it's going to close pretty fast. So, you still have to hit it even though they're, you know, shorter distance. >> Thank you.

title: Drew Lock On Preparing To Start Week 10 vs. Raiders | Seattle Seahawks
text: All right. >> How you feeling? >> Good. Feeling good. Um yeah, feeling good. Kind I talked about after the game. I feel like we did a great job handling the week last week and here we are. We just got a little something added to it and I think we're doing the same. We're doing a great job getting ready. Good stuff in the morning before meetings. Nice and warmed up heading into practice today and we'll go out there and roll it. >> How much are you feeling the oblique injury while you throw? >> Not too much. Um honestly talked about it being on the backside which is way better for a thrower instead of the front side, so grateful for that. >> Have you ever had an oblique injury before? >> I have um when I was in New York. >> And what what was that like as a quarterback to go through? >> That was on the front side. So yeah, that that was not fun for a couple weeks. Took a couple weeks off. It was in the preseason though, so uh missed the last two preseason games. Had the little like three or four day weekend before the first week and then I was back to being the backup for that first week, so. >> Are you in a better position for the challenge? You've got two injuries. Not mentally. I mean does it even matter or >> No. No, there's see when you get out there they've done all the prep work pregame that's necessary. When you get out there your adrenaline starts rolling you're playing for more than just yourself. It kind of just goes away. >> You with it with it being on the backside, how does that I guess when you're going through your throwing motion, how does that feel different than when you dealt with it when it was on the front side? >> Um I mean mechanic wise like yeah, you got to use a little bit of the backside, but when you're rotating and pulling through it's all this. And uh that's really when the torque happens. The speed of the arm comes through with that. Um so allowing it to be back here mechanically speaking it is a little better. >> Do you feel like when >> you know, when you have those disruptions to your routine and that kind of stuff through a week, like are you are you better prepared to be able to move through those things as a little bit more of a veteran player than when you were younger? Like just having that kind of midweek adversity, how how are you better prepared to to to shoulder that than maybe five years ago or >> Yeah. Um there's always a weird thing I feel like maybe not every player, but most players can you attest to like playing through something playing through an injury. It takes a lot of focus during the week or like extra thoughts throughout the week. They're just not there. You're thinking about getting better, thinking about getting on a practice uh doing the best you can in practice and getting ready for Sunday. It's just that extra thing to think about and it kind of takes your brain away from all the nonsense that may try to drag you in. Um but as far as like being a little older um yeah, I feel like it wouldn't have had a too big of a difference from a young me to now go out and attack every Sunday with the same, you know, ferociousness, so to say, and uh go out there and play every snap like it's my last. >> I assume that the defenses are probably trying to give you looks pre-snap to discourage you from going to JSN, given all the things he's done. Do you guys have kind of different rules for him about like if he's getting this look, we'll still potentially go there versus maybe other guys we wouldn't? >> Yeah. Um I Jacks would love that. Jacks would tell you that. If he's doubled, he's still open. Um that's kind of been [clears throat] the the funny line this year, but um no. I For me personally, and I think um for everybody, you know, involved our read is our read. If Jacks is number one and he's covered, we go to number two. If number one's covered and it's not Jacks, we go to two and Jacks is for some reason three. And Jacks is open, we'll throw him the ball. Um that's how I'll play back there. That how I'm thinking and uh just go through reads, go through progressions, knowing you're hot and play good football. >> I think you might have You might have touched on this after the game, but is it easier in a way to prepare in a week that you're not physically doing everything because you've been a backup and you know that is to prepare when you're not getting all the reps? it's definitely it's definitely a good blend of both. Um you want to be out there. You want to get every single rep. Um but at the same time if I'm not and that's that's what we're deciding today or yesterday like hey let's let's pull this back a little bit, give you another day to rest then I don't feel like I'm missing too much in prep because of the fact that for the last couple of years that's that's how I've been able to get ready for games. It's the only way I've been able to get ready for games. It allows uh us to be I feel like a little more fluid as to how I'm feeling day by day. >> Is there >> week it was th- I think 50% third down conversions. What did you like about what you guys were able to accomplish on early downs and what still needs to get better? >> Yeah. Uh critical for us being good on first and second down. Like speaking towards our our third down last last week just guys making plays with the ball in their hand mixing in whether was a a run, a quick pass, a deep drop back like having all aspects of our offense available on third down was was big for us and it keeps defenses on their toes and um but mostly let's let's keep being efficient on first and second down and giving us that you know advantageous situations on third. >> Is there uh a thing you found that forces teams out of certain coverages where they're really trying to concentrate on Jacks? Like is it amount of production by other guys? Is it a specific route that if you hit this it's going to force them to respect it? What what forces defenses to maybe change? >> No, that that's going to be a good question for a defensive coordinator whenever you get in front of them. Um they're still humans. They still feel games. They're on the sideline. They feel momentum shifting. They feel a guy getting the ball. They want to double Jacks, they'll double Jacks. They want to take him away from a game and we have we have other players that are going get the ball and and make it work. it's really on them how they want to attack us that week and it's our job to respond and you know find ways to convert thirds and and be great on first and second. >> How much do you find um the run game actually affects what kind of coverages that they can play? >> Yeah, I feel like that's that's the classic, right? Run the ball to be able to throw it. Um run the ball, run the ball, force them to get in single high coverages three or man and that opens up the pass game then you start hitting the pass game they got to play shell and then you come back to the run. The classic, you know, complementary football between run game and pass game. >> Jahan in the passing game obviously made some guys miss, made some big plays just Well I guess when we have a player who's able to do that in the open field is it is it their sense like just let's get the ball in his hands and tell him to do his thing? >> Yeah, that and to be honest with you that's how I feel about just about everybody on this team. Um you know let's get the ball in these guys' hands, keep it in our hands, see what they do with it and uh you know in in my in my opinion there's not a guy on our offensive side of the ball that I don't feel comfortable doing that too. JD was fantastic at it last week. Um moving forward he can continue to do that but we'll see who it is this week and I have full confidence that it could be any one of our our skill players. >> Zach and JD looked different last week which makes sense, right? They they had their week to kind of come back and get their feet wet. You always have faith in the guys but was there something that looked or felt different being around them, a look in their eye or you just kind of knew that it was different? I think when Sharps does his classic like you can't tackle me thing and like shoves people to the ground it's pretty it's pretty fun to watch and that's kind of like uh oh there's that's Zach. That's what we know him the Carolina clip from years ago was like kind of one of his first big ones. Um man if when we see more and more of that happening including the look in his eye when you come back to the huddle yeah it's there's definitely a feel. >> You said after the last game that the combination of maybe the coaching staff and then building all stuff allows you to feel as confident as you've ever been going into the and I'm wondering if break down more what is giving you that certainty of what is it the coaching staff or the building or the preparation what is allowing you to go in and feel as confident as as you've ever felt. >> Ironically it goes back to you know when I get traded here the first couple talks that you know I had with Pete and John about how much confidence they had in me and deal moving forward with you know being traded about how excited they were to get me here. So to get set off on that foot right as I get here. Um I know we've had different coaches in the quarterback room, offensive coaches, head coaches. It's all been the same. It's it's all felt that way. There's we want you to go be you. We believe in you. Go out and execute and and don't ever think anything. Just go be yourself. And when you keep getting that like pressed upon you whether it's me or Jerry Price or Tory Horton like that builds a confidence and this building has done a phenomenal job of of from what I've seen for myself and other players that sit in those chairs that you know they're they're going to be confident going into Sundays because they get preached that to them. >> Do you enjoy it when when defenders are talking out there when they're talking a little bit or do you just prefer just to play? >> Yeah no I do I do have fun with that. I'd say earlier in my career I had more fun with it. Told Joey Bosa he was tired once when I was playing for the Broncos then he proceeded to like swim a tight end in tackles in the backfield for a three-yard loss and like kind of get in my face. That was like the last time I've ever really talked like a defensive [clears throat] lineman during a game. But it is fun like I've seen AB get a little riled up you know like it it's cool. >> Uh sorry I got one more. Playing through the injuries is there any part of that that like makes it easier to play within yourself as a quarterback? Like there's the the saying in golf you know like >> Yeah and I get what you're saying. It does. No I guess you can mentally get into a point where like you know I'm going to I'm going to stay like you said stay within myself. You know not play hero football so to say but we're always trying to avoid playing hero football cuz that's when bad things happen but as far as like my situation this week I I'm not looking at it as staying in you know staying whatever we said beneath myself here like injury is what it is. It's going to be ready to go by Sunday I'm going to go out and play normal. >> How did once the adrenaline wore off how did everything feel Sunday night and Monday? >> Pretty good Sunday. Pretty good Monday and then by about 5:00 or 6:00 you start feeling some things. Really I thought I was like getting a sore throat or something but it was really just the neck head going back and not used to the hits so um just classic football feelings after a game nothing too crazy. >> Drew you got your family posted some really wonderful news on social media and obviously that's always going to be great but it comes with this awesome time in your career right now this week too like how special putting all that together yeah? >> Yeah it's fun. It's fun this said it before but this place is you know special to us. you know two children here married here being able to uh I've hopes in the dreams of the third you know God willing being with us here soon. Soonish it's in May but we'll see if that one's still here. just excited love this place. It's always good feelings good vibes and uh excited to play on Sunday. >> Thanks thanks Drew.

title: The Seahawks' QB Situation Is Impossible...
text: obviously Sam Darnold has battled injuries. Literally from the first drive of this season we saw uh Drew Lock step in last last game. So is there anything else more we should know about the status of of either of the two quarterbacks? >> Well it it certainly sounds like Drew Lock's going to give it a go, doesn't he? And Sam Darnold when he had his oblique injury now this is not the playoffs like like when Sam Darnold had his so it's a little bit of a different situation there but I suppose it's not because if Sam if Drew Lock does not play you you're then putting a lot of pressure on Jaylen Milroe. So uh he's going to give it a go and if he can get through this game I'm sure he will be able to. I'm sure there'll be things they can do to to put him in a place to to perform. It might not be Drew Lock at his absolute physical best and we saw a little bit of that at the weekend didn't we? The the spiral was not quite as tight as you'd expect for someone with such a fantastic arm as Drew Lock clearly has. Uh but I imagine he's going to be able to manage the game and he's going to get it done and with Jadarrian Price and Zach Charbonnet looking quite promising against the Cardinals he should be well supported. Uh you know there's always the option of throwing it to Jackson Smith and Jigba and letting him just run away from everybody. So they'll they'll probably do a bit of that as well. So I I feel pretty good about that. I think the the broader problem with the quarterback debate is I I I kind of feel as if we're in this horrible no man's land at the moment where I I'm sort of speaking to you on the 11th of November. It's the 10th where you are. And as we sit here today >> the future Rob. Tell us the future. What's going to happen? >> knows what's going on. We've been asking all these questions but Rob tell us. >> I can I can tell you that Wednesday follows Tuesday. That's as much of [laughter] clarity I can provide here. >> Honestly that's kind of where we're all at in life. >> You know that's reassuring actually. It's helpful. >> Yeah. It's definitely Wednesday here. But the the thing is is that it's that lack of clarity that bothers me a little bit. There's nothing you can do about it. There's there's no one's to blame for this uh really. But you have a situation where I don't know whether you want to have Sam Darnold on a $42 million cap hit next year. I don't know whether you want to pay Sam Darnold $55 million year. I don't know if you want to trade Sam Darnold. I don't know if you want to go with Drew Lock instead. title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler: Why the Colts Didn’t Lower the Price for Jonathan Taylor | The Rich Eisen Show
text: The Giants truly did kick a tire on trying to add a big name at running back. Walk me through what they were looking to do and could not accomplish or did not. >> Yeah, Rich, they were looking to upgrade at two positions primarily, running back, defensive tackle. They didn't have a fourth round pick coming up. They're missing a four and a five. So, that was part of the equation. So, this is a team that was going to try to upgrade, but I wasn't wholly convinced that they were going to go all the way with it because they're still a little bit in transition roster-wise. Chiefs, Bills, Jaguars, all have a solidified star quarterback and a team that can win it all this year. title: Aaron Rodgers Press Conference (November 11) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: I'm sure you guys looked at some of the struggles in the red zone and all to go over the off week. When you guys have struggled with that over the years, what's kind of been the remedy to get back on track? >> I mean, it's just execution, you know, there's fixable things. I feel like the bye week always comes a good time regardless when it is. I always look forward to it and I appreciate Mike's bye week schedules over the years. >> Say how how how how has that how have you seen it work been successful to come off the bye week over the course of your career? How have you seen how like some of the details on how that's worked over the years? >> I think that's one of those stats you can just find if you're looking for it. Obviously there's a you know, the slight advantage in in rest, but yeah, I just think that's a outlier stat probably. >> Aaron, how do you feel like you guys have managed through some of the wide receiver injuries and do you feel like some of these guys will be back soon? >> Yeah, I mean, I hope so. We've obviously raised up a couple of our P squad guys who are talented. Still would love to get some opportunities for Max at some point whenever he comes off. Were you hoping for a wide receiver addition at the deadline yesterday? Were you hoping your breath was at 4:00 that maybe a move would get made? >> I've learned to never hold my breath around the trade deadline because I don't know that I've ever been a part of a team other than when we got Devonte in Jersey where there was an addition. You know, teams get interesting around the the deadline whether or not they to move guys. I feel like in the last five years there's a lot more not going to say tanking necessarily, but teams looking to add draft capital if they don't think they're going to make the playoffs. I feel like being six and two is really good. When you win sometimes, it can gloss over some areas that need improvement if you want to get to where you want to get to. We got to go in there and do the same and come out with a win. >> Aaron, what were some of the things you liked about that first game offensively against the Bengals? I know that was kind of the day it felt like the run game kind of started to coalesce and wake up. Um why was that the case and how can you build off of that this time around against them? >> Well, if you go back and watch what 30 did in that game, that was kind of his uh stepping into the spotlight moment uh this season. title: A special tribute from Scott Van Pelt to broadcasting legend Dan Hicks | SC with SVP
text: Ours is an unusual and remarkable business in many respects. If you're lucky and you have a long run, you might find yourself traveling all over the world, covering the biggest events in sports. You get to know the people who do the same at other networks. We're all on the same journey as part of this unique traveling circus. When you do golf, you're there for the week, often far away from home, maybe in another country. You seek the company of the people you truly come to know and care about because they make home feel not so far away. It's all one big family. Doesn't matter if you're Mike Flag, says ESPN, CBS, or Fox, or NBC. We're all in this together. In that way, our entire TV family is grieving on this day along with our friends at NBC with the stunning news that we lost Dan Hicks. I woke this morning to those texts and couldn't fathom they were real. A fit 64 year old with a razor sharp wit and immense talent. Dan elevated some of the more remarkable moments we've ever seen in sports. Dan's voice an indelible part of those memories. Calls that will live forever. And we all know that we do not. But this news arriving so suddenly on this day stopped us all wherever we were. a sobering reality of just how fragile all of this is and how every moment is meant to be treasured. And as sad as we are for our colleagues at NBC, it pales to our concern for beloved members of our ESPN family. Dan lovingly called them Hicks Chicks, his wife Hannah Storm, and their three lovely daughters. Every one of us at ESPN lifts you up in prayer and holds you in our hearts in the hope that somehow you don't feel alone in enduring this the most difficult moment of your lives because you're not. And I'd hesitate to speak on behalf of our company, let alone an entire industry. But I feel certain I speak for every one of us in front of or behind a camera in any shop that covers sports when I say we love you and your family. And we stand ready to do whatever might be helpful in this moment and in the days, [music] weeks, months, and years to come.
